items.title: Rays bank on rested Drew Rasmussen to make difference in Game 2
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: MILWAUKEE -- The Tampa Bay Rays hope ace right-hander Drew Rasmussen will benefit from an extra day of rest as they look to even the World Series at one win apiece against the Milwaukee Brewers on Saturday.
items.body:
MILWAUKEE -- The Tampa Bay Rays hope ace right-hander Drew Rasmussen will benefit from an extra day of rest as they look to even the World Series at one win apiece against the Milwaukee Brewers on Saturday.
Rasmussen, who originally was expected to start the opener, will be opposed by rookie right-hander Logan Henderson in a matchup of teams that have never won a World Series title.
The Brewers, whose only other World Series appearance was a seven-game loss in 1982, held on to win the opener 3-2 on Friday night when closer Trevor Megill struck out Johnny DeLuca with runners on second and third in the ninth inning.
The Brewers used their ace, Jacob Misiorowski, in Game 1, and he got the win. The hard-throwing right-hander allowed one run on four hits in five innings.
Now the Rays will hand the ball to their top starter in Game 2.
"We want him to be at full strength and feeling really good when he gets on the mound," Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash said of Rasmussen. "Our information tells us over many, many times of doing this that that extra day plays a huge benefit."
Rasmussen, who broke into the majors with the Brewers in 2020, has dominated in his three postseason starts this month. He is 2-0 with a 1.29 ERA in the playoffs after going 9-0 with a 1.86 ERA in his final 12 regular-season starts.
Rasmussen allowed two runs on eight hits in six-plus innings in the opener of the American League Championship Series, although Cleveland rallied to win 7-3. Rasmussen came back to limit the Guardians to one run on four hits in seven innings in the Rays' 3-1 victory in Game 5.
In the AL Division Series opener against the Yankees, Rasmussen allowed just one hit over eight scoreless innings, striking out 10 in a 1-0 Rays victory.
In 2020 and part of the 2021 season with Milwaukee, Rasmussen appeared in 27 games, all in relief, going 1-1 with one save and a 5.01 ERA. He struck out 46 in 32 1/3 innings but walked 21.
"Had the Brewers been playing anyone else in the World Series, man, I'd be rooting for them," Rasmussen said. "It's a really unique, really cool matchup. I'm excited for this one. But ... we're here to do a job just as they are. I'm excited for their fan base and their organization, but at the end of the day, it is us they're competing against, and we really want to win a World Series as well."
Rasmussen, named to the AL All-Star team each of the past two seasons, finished second in the AL this year with 16 wins and fourth in ERA at 2.67.
The Rays, making their first World Series appearance since 2020, were 11-for-11 in stolen-base attempts in the first two postseason series, but Brewers catcher William Contreras threw out runners twice to end innings on Friday.
"Look, he's a very talented player on both sides of the ball," Cash said postgame. "We knew that coming in. Not surprised by anything that he did, but that's not going to change our aggressive approach, certainly on the bases."
Henderson started Game 2 in Milwaukee's first two postseason series, getting a no-decision in both although the Brewers won each game. The 24-year-old Houston native allowed a total of six runs (three earned) in nine innings while striking out six and walking five. The latter figure was surprising considering Henderson walked just 19 in 98 1/3 innings while going 11-3 with a 2.47 ERA over 18 regular-season starts.
"I think there's definitely value in having thrown it a couple games now rather than just getting activated and throwing the first time in the playoffs and the World Series, I think there's some value to it," Henderson said Friday.
Henderson missed about six weeks due to a lower back strain, but he went 9-2 with a 2.39 ERA in 13 starts after coming off the injured list on July 9. He finished 6-0 with a 1.84 ERA in eight home starts this year.
--Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

items.title: NBA roundup: Hawks crush Hornets, set franchise mark for largest win
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Jalen Johnson and reserve Aaron Wiggins each scored 19 points as visiting Atlanta blew out the Charlotte Hornets 128-81 on Friday, the biggest margin of victory in Hawks history.
items.body:
Jalen Johnson and reserve Aaron Wiggins each scored 19 points as visiting Atlanta blew out the Charlotte Hornets 128-81 on Friday, the biggest margin of victory in Hawks history.
The 47-point gap topped the old record of 46 set in a 126-80 victory over the Sacramento Kings on Nov 15, 2017. Nickeil Alexander-Walker put up 14 points, CJ McCollum posted 13 points, Dyson Daniels contributed 11 points, nine rebounds and seven steals and Corey Kispert also had 11 points for Atlanta, which won its second straight to start the season.
It was a miserable home opener for the Hornets, who won two nights earlier at Brooklyn to start their campaign. They committed 27 turnovers. Naz Reid scored 17 points for Charlotte and Grayson Allen came off the bench for 11 points. Both players were in their home debuts with the Hornets. Reserve Tidjane Salaun also scored 11 points.
The gap reached 97-62 by the end of the third quarter. The Hornets couldn't even get it cranked up when the margin was out of hand, needing about 6 1/2 minutes to reach a double-digit total in the fourth quarter.
Celtics 107, Knicks 103
Jayson Tatum scored a game-high 36 points, including nine late in the fourth quarter, as Boston withstood a late comeback bid by visiting New York to escape with a victory.
Tatum finished with nine rebounds and seven assists for the Celtics, who have split their first two games. Paul George and reserve Neemias Queta had 15 points apiece while Derrick White added 12 points.
Karl-Anthony Towns (22 points, 10 rebounds), OG Anunoby (20 points, 10 rebounds) and Josh Hart (10 points, 12 rebounds) all had double-doubles for the reigning NBA champion Knicks, who have lost their first two games.
Bulls 132, Bucks 125
Norman Powell scored 25 points and rookie Caleb Wilson added 21 to help visiting Chicago earn a victory over Milwaukee.
Leonard Miller had 19 points, while Jalen Smith chipped in 14 points and 13 rebounds for Chicago, which rebounded after suffering a 43-point loss to the Toronto Raptors on Wednesday. Buddy Hield scored 13, Isaac Okoro had 12 and Tre Jones tallied 11 points and eight assists for the Bulls, who trailed by 15 points after the first quarter.
Tyler Herro led Milwaukee with 34 points, followed by Jaime Jaquez Jr.'s 19 points and 11 boards. Kyle Kuzma scored 14 and Myles Turner had 12, while Ryan Rollins, AJ Green and Kel'el Ware scored 11 apiece for the Bucks, who lost their second straight to open the season.
Mavericks 121, Pacers 105
Kyrie Irving scored a game-high 24 points as Dallas defeated Indiana in Indianapolis, but the victory was overshadowed by a left shoulder injury to Mavericks star Cooper Flagg.
Flagg was hurt in the last minute of the first half when he was fouled from behind by Aaron Nesmith, who was assessed a flagrant-1 foul. Flagg finished with 14 points, five rebounds and six assists, while teammate P.J. Washington added 20 points and 13 rebounds.
Pascal Siakam paced Indiana with 23 points and Tyrese Haliburton contributed 18 points. Both teams ended the game with a 1-1 record.
Rockets 114, Spurs 110
Alperen Sengun pounded his way to 29 points, including 14 in the fourth quarter, as Houston ground out a win over San Antonio in Austin, Texas.
Kevin Durant and Amen Thompson added 20 points apiece for the Rockets, who improved to 2-0. Thompson also collected 10 rebounds and also blocked Victor Wembanyama's attempt at a game-tying layup in the final second.
Wembanyama registered 25 points and 13 rebounds as the Spurs fell to 0-2. Dylan Harper had 20 points, and De'Aaron Fox added 19 points and nine assists.
Lakers 125, Clippers 117
Austin Reaves scored 28 points and added nine assists while Luka Doncic recorded 23 points as the Los Angeles Lakers used a third-quarter surge to stay perfect through two games with a victory over the visiting Los Angeles Clippers.
Walker Kessler scored 22 points for the Lakers, hitting 10 of 14 shots. He is 22 of 26 over two games with his new team.
Darius Garland scored 26 points and Brook Lopez added 22 as the Clippers fell to 1-1. The Clippers committed 26 turnovers that the Lakers turned into 33 points.
Raptors 112, Wizards 102
Scottie Barnes collected 28 points and 14 rebounds and RJ Barrett added 23 and nine, respectively, lifting visiting Toronto past Washington.
Barnes made 12 of 26 shots from the floor to offset eight turnovers for the Raptors, who never trailed in the contest. Kawhi Leonard recorded 16 points and nine rebounds.
Trae Young produced 22 points and 12 assists for the Wizards. AJ Dybantsa, the top overall pick of the 2026 NBA Draft, sat out his second straight game due to a sprained left ankle.
Timberwolves 115, Magic 93
Anthony Edwards and Jaden McDaniels scored 15 points apiece, and Minnesota cruised to a win over host Orlando.
Rudy Gobert added 14 points and nine rebounds for Minnesota, which won its second straight game to start the season. Ayo Dosunmu finished with 14 points and 10 assists, and LaMelo Ball chipped in 12 points.
Wendell Carter Jr. tallied 20 points and nine rebounds to lead Orlando, which dropped its second straight game under first-year head coach Sean Sweeney. Franz Wagner recorded 18 points before fouling out, and Paolo Banchero and Jalen Suggs finished with 14 points apiece.
Pistons 128, Heat 111
John Collins scored 23 points and grabbed seven rebounds and Paul Reed finished with 19 points and 11 rebounds as Detroit prevailed at Miami.
The Pistons led wire to wire after scoring the game's first 11 points and built a 23-point advantage in the third quarter. Detroit's Jalen Duren exited in the second quarter due to a right thigh injury and did not return.
Giannis Antetokounmpo put up his first double-double for the Heat with 36 points, 12 rebounds and five assists from. Davion Mitchell totaled 18 points and five rebounds.
Jazz 120, Pelicans 119
Jaren Jackson Jr. logged 24 points and 10 rebounds and Keyonte George added 19 points and 10 assists to rally Utah to a victory over New Orleans in Salt Lake City.
Utah rookie Darryn Peterson scored 15 points, including two go-ahead free throws with 50.5 seconds left. Jaxson Hayes chipped in 17 points off the bench and Lauri Markkanen added 16 to help the Jazz beat the Pelicans for the first time since November 2023.
Zion Williamson led the Pelicans with 23 points and reserve Saddiq Bey added 20. Dejounte Murray chipped in 16, but missed a potential game-winning jumper with a second left as the Pelicans fell to 0-2.
Grizzlies 111, Warriors 108
Ty Jerome scored a game-high 28 points and Memphis used a 17-0 fourth-quarter spurt to rally for a victory over Golden State in San Francisco.
Rookie Cameron Boozer added 25 points, 13 rebounds and six assists for Memphis, which won its second straight game to begin the season. Jaylen Wells scored 17 and Cam Spencer chipped in 11 for the Grizzlies, who outscored Golden State 27-18 in the fourth quarter.
Stephen Curry's 24 points led the Warriors, while Brandin Podziemski and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg contributed 18 points apiece. In his second game, Lendeborg also tallied 13 rebounds and six assists. Golden State has dropped its first two games of the year for the first time since 2020-21.
Trail Blazers 128, Kings 120
Deni Avdija scored 26 points and Portland overcame a 12-point first-quarter deficit en route to a victory over host Sacramento.
Damian Lillard and Toumani Camara scored 19 points apiece and Sidy Cissoko scored 15 points, all in the first half, as Portland improved to 2-0. Robert Williams III scored 13 points while Ja Morant and Jrue Holiday each had 12 points.
Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. scored 33 points in his second career game and Domantas Sabonis had 27 points, 19 rebounds and 10 assists for his 69th career triple-double. Zach LaVine scored 22 points as Sacramento, in its home opener, lost its second straight game to open the season.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Rugby Fiji avenge Pacific Nations loss in thrilling 34-28 win over Japan
items.author: Anton Bridge
items.creator: Anton Bridge
items.summary: Fiji prevailed over Japan 34-28 in a nail-biter in Tokyo on Saturday, avenging a loss five weeks ago when the sides met in the final of the Pacific Nations Cup.
items.body:
Fiji prevailed over Japan 34-28 in a nail-biter in Tokyo on Saturday, avenging a loss five weeks ago when the sides met in the final of the Pacific Nations Cup.
The sides battled end to end, sticking to quick hands and making expansive runs despite wet conditions in a game at Chichibunomiya Stadium in central Tokyo to mark the 100th anniversary of the Japan Rugby Football Union.
Fiji battered Japan with powerful tackles and outran the hosts in open play but Japan took their chances while in the Fijian 22 to stay in the game.
Tied at three converted tries apiece at the end of the first half, Fiji kept up their momentum to finish ahead by two penalty conversions, even though a dangerous tackle by number 8 Motikiai Murray on counterpart Faulua Makisi in the 34th minute took them down to 14 men for 20 minutes.
Japan found success at the maul, scoring two tries off lineout mauls in the first half, but were undone by handling errors and beaten in the air, with Fiji trusting to their power, pace and footwork to edge the hosts.
A thundering tackle on Japanese inside centre Charlie Lawrence forced a turnover on the Fijian 5-metre line and winger Nacani Boginisoko ran the length of the pitch before offloading to scrum half Terio Tamani for Fiji’s fourth try.
Fiji had earlier displayed their flair in an attack starting on the halfway line, with an angled run by outside centre Tuidraki Samusamuvodre that dissected the Japanese defence to bring about Fiji's second try in the 14th minute.
Japanese skipper Warner Dearns led the resistance, putting in some thumping tackles of his own and muscling over two tries. Japan, nicknamed the Brave Blossoms, fought to the final whistle but couldn’t string together enough phases in attack to overturn the deficit.
Both sides are now looking to the northern series of the Nations Championship that begins next month, with Fiji facing France, Ireland and Italy, while Japan will play Wales, England and Scotland.

items.title: South Africa paceman Nortje ruled out of third test
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: South African quick bowler Anrich Nortje is out of the last test against Australia after a groin injury suffered early in the comprehensive second test victory in Gqeberha this week, Cricket South Africa said on Saturday.
items.body:
South African quick bowler Anrich Nortje is out of the last test against Australia after a groin injury suffered early in the comprehensive second test victory in Gqeberha this week, Cricket South Africa said on Saturday.
The 32-year-old Nortje pulled up in his fourth over and played no further part in the test, which South Africa won by an innings and 31 runs on Thursday
He is the only change to the squad for the third test, which starts at Newlands on Tuesday
Nortje had only returned after a lengthy spell out of first-class cricket after a litany of injuries stalled his career
South Africa and Australia are level at 1-1 in the three-match series

items.title: Johnson & Johnson's prostate cancer drug shrinks tumors in early-stage trial
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Johnson & Johnson on Saturday said its experimental once-daily oral prostate cancer drug caused tumors to disappear or shrink in an early-stage trial.
items.body:
Johnson & Johnson (JNJ.N) on Saturday said its experimental once-daily oral prostate cancer drug caused tumors to disappear or shrink in an early-stage trial.
J&J had gained access to the drug through its $3.05 billion [USN:L4N3WT0VR TEXT:"deal"] to buy Halda Therapeutics last year.
Here are more details:
The company was testing JNJ-6143 in patients with advanced prostate cancer who had received multiple treatments
Its novel approach selectively kills cancer cells by interfering with a protein they need to survive
In the trial, 77% of 31 evaluable patients receiving the 50-milligram dose saw their PSA levels, a blood marker used to monitor prostate cancer, fall by at least 50%; in 48% of patients, PSA levels fell by at least 90%
Among patients whose tumors could be measured using imaging, 69% had a confirmed complete or partial response
"It adds a new mechanism of action to J&J's prostate cancer portfolio," a Johnson & Johnson spokesperson said
Common side effects were nausea and elevated cholesterol and triglyceride levels. One patient discontinued treatment due to adverse effects
The data were presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress

items.title: Czech coalition advances media overhaul in rushed overnight vote
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: In a rare overnight vote, the Czech ruling coalition pushed public media funding changes through a first parliamentary hurdle despite criticism that they could weaken broadcaster independence.
items.body:
In a rare overnight vote, the Czech ruling coalition pushed public media funding changes through a first parliamentary hurdle despite criticism that they could weaken broadcaster independence.
The populist government of billionaire Prime Minister Andrej Babis, backed by the far-right SPD party, has frequently criticised public and private media coverage of its policies and accused some outlets of bias.
Opposition parties have compared the proposed changes with reforms in Hungary under former Prime Minister Viktor Orban, who oversaw a [USN:L8N41K0KR TEXT:"major expansion"] of pro-government media.
The government says it is scrapping the 205 crown ($9.45) monthly household broadcasting fee to ease costs for consumers. Funding would instead come from the state budget.
The proposal was brought to the floor outside the planned order of proceedings on Friday. Speaker Tomio Okamura of the SPD limited debate and scheduled the vote for 4:36 a.m. (0336 GMT) on Saturday.
The coalition's majority then voted to send the bill to committees for further discussion.
SUNDAY PROTEST PLANNED Hundreds of protesters gathered outside parliament, with some remaining overnight. Local media reported that several people unsuccessfully tried to enter the building.
Critics say the changes would weaken the broadcasters and make them more vulnerable to political pressure. Czech Television is the country's most-watched broadcaster across major age groups, while public media are among the most trusted news sources in the country, according to a 2025 Reuters Institute survey.
The proposal would cut funding for Czech Television and Czech Radio by about 15%, possibly as early as next year, and keep nominal funding unchanged for several years.
"There is no war for independent media," Babis said on Facebook late on Friday. "There is no fight for democracy and no nationalisation of media is being prepared."
The proposal and its fast-track treatment drew criticism from the broadcasters, international journalism groups and institutions including universities and the Catholic Church.
"The bill goes against the European Media Freedom Act (EMFA), which requires adequate, stable and predictable funding for public service media," the European Federation of Journalists said in a statement.
Journalists and other employees at the broadcasters announced a strike for November 3, while a civic group called a public protest for Sunday.
($1 = 21.6880 Czech crowns)

FAST

MANILA: Two Philippine Air Force trainer aircraft crashed during a training flight at an air base south of the capital Manila, killing four pilots, the military said on Saturday (Oct 24).
The aviation accident on Friday involved two SF-260 aircraft during a training flight at the Fernando Air Base in Batangas province, the Philippine Air Force said in a statement.
Local media has reported the two planes collided in midair.
The aircraft crashed within the grounds of the air base but there were no other casualties.
The Air Force has temporarily grounded its fleet of SF-260 trainer planes pending an investigation into the cause of the accident.
In May, two pilots were killed when an SF-260 trainer aircraft crashed in a mountainous area in northern Philippines, while another SF-260 TP Marchetti crashed during a 2023 training flight, also killing two pilots.
The military used SF-260 aircraft during months of air strikes on southern Marawi City after militants loyal to Islamic State seized the area in 2017.

items.title: Le dirigeant nord-coréen Kim Jong Un en visite en Chine
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le dirigeant de la Corée du Nord Kim Jong Un s'est rendu samedi en Chine en empruntant un pont tout juste ouvert entre les deux pays, a-t-on appris d'un responsable gouvernemental sud-coréen.
items.body:
Le dirigeant de la Corée du Nord Kim Jong Un s'est rendu samedi en Chine en empruntant un pont tout juste ouvert entre les deux pays, a-t-on appris d'un responsable gouvernemental sud-coréen.
Kim est arrivé dans la ville chinoise de Dandong en empruntant un pont au-dessus du fleuve Yalu, a ajouté ce responsable s'exprimant sous le sceau de l'anonymat.
Il a été accueilli dans cette ville frontalière par le Premier ministre chinois, Li Qiang, a rapporté l'agence sud-coréenne Yonhap.
On ignore s'il rencontrera le président chinois Xi Jinping.
Le ministère chinois des Affaires étrangères n'a pas répondu dans l'immédiat à une demande de commentaire.
Long de trois kilomètres, le Nouveau Pont du fleuve Yalu été inauguré ce mois-ci avec un long retard sur le calendrier initial. Il constitue désormais la plus importante liaison terrestre entre la Corée du Nord et la Chine.
Son ouverture doit permettre de relancer les relations commerciales entre les deux pays après des années de perturbations dues à des tensions diplomatiques et aux effets de la pandémie de COVID-19. Elle illustre aussi le réchauffement en cours entre la Chine et la Corée du Nord, dont les dirigeants ont participé à deux sommets lors des 13 derniers mois.

items.title: France deploys 70,000 security personnel as new protests raise riot fears
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: Paris has boarded up shops and shut 3 major museums ahead of Saturday's protests, while a football match has been postponed; President Macron acknowledged planning failures after last weekend's unrest ...
items.body: By Samy Adghirni A new round of protests is set to hit France Saturday, raising fears of a repeat of last weekend’s riots. The French government has vowed to subdue any violence, deploying 70.000 security officials, including elite anti-terror forces, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez told reporters Friday. He blamed social media calls for violence on the far left.  Shops in Paris including luxury boutiques boarded up windows and hired more security personnel, and some will remain shut. Three popular museums, the Louvre, Musee d’Orsay and the Picasso Museum will close Saturday. The scheduled football match between Paris Saint-Germain and Olympique Lyonnais in Paris was postponed.  “We will be uncompromising with hooligans, looters, and anyone who commits acts of violence — including far-left political groups,” Nunez said, while stressing that the police is “ready” to face rioters. Soldiers will help guard sensitive buildings. Helicopters, water canons and armored vehicles known as Centaurs will also be available. Some cities, including Lyon, banned protests on Saturday and extended curfews.  President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday acknowledged “planning failings and elements of surprise” last weekend, when protests drew more than half a million people and degenerated into vandalism. Rioters attacked public buildings and looted stores across the country. The French leader, who postponed a planned tour across West Africa, blamed ultra-left groups for what he called seditious acts.  Supported by a disparate movement of social media figures, students, unions and left-wing parties, Saturday’s protests are framed as an “Acte II,” or second round, of a movement calling for better public services and government help with the cost of living. Much of the anger is targeted at Macron, who six months before the end of his second term, has never been so unpopular. Polls show the violence has benefited far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, the frontrunner for next year’s election. Adding to tensions, Le Pen is due to convene thousands of supporters in the central city of Orleans on Saturday for her National Rally party congress. Anti-Le Pen opponents are heading there to protest. The unrest has also increased fears about public finances. While France dodged a downgrade at Moody’s Ratings late Friday, it’s struggling to reduce the budget deficit ahead of the 2027 election. A closely watched gauge of bond risk rose to levels last seen during the euro-area debt crisis: The spread between 10-year yields in France and Germany, the region’s safe asset, reached 178 basis points on Thursday, compared with just 85 basis points at the start of September. Private-sector economic activity also shrank this month, with the Composite Purchasing Managers’ Index compiled by S&P Global dropping to 48.4 in October from 51.1 last month. That’s below the 50 threshold separating expansion from contraction. France isn’t the only European country dealing with a popular anger. In Italy, demonstrations by students and other youth are expected in Milan and Rome over the weekend. The government has said will deploy military forces in Milan after protests led to looting and rioting there last weekend.  Protests are also expected in Belgium while Albania is grappling with a second week of violent student-led demonstrations fueled by discontent with Prime Minister Edi Rama’s rule.

SEOUL: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for the country's army companies to be turned into elite, self-sufficient combat units during a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang, state media KCNA said on Saturday (Oct 24).
The event underscored Kim's consistent policy priority of strengthening the military.
In a speech at a conference of company commanders for North Korea's Army on October 22-23, which KCNA said was the first military-wide gathering since the Ninth Congress of North Korea's ruling party in February, Kim called for every company to fully prepare so that "the goal of the new-era military build-up" can be achieved.
"Let us build the strongest army and speed up a military revolution in our style", Kim said.

During the Ninth Congress of North Korea's ruling party in February, which sets the country's direction for the next five years, Kim called for stronger conventional armed forces as well as reaffirming efforts to develop nuclear weapons and missiles.
CHINA VISIT Kim arrived in Dandong, China, on Saturday on a visit to the neighbouring country via a newly opened bridge, South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported, citing a South Korea government source.
A spokesperson for South Korea's Unification Ministry did not have an immediate comment. China's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Chinese President Xi Jinping shakes hands with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during a welcome ceremony in Pyongyang, Jun 8, 2026. (Photo: AP/Korean Central News Agency)

China and North Korea officially opened their most significant land border crossing in Dandong this month, aiming to rejuvenate trade and commerce after years of strained ties and pandemic-related disruptions.
Kim's last known visit to China was in September 2025, to attend the 80th Victory Day celebrations in Beijing, when he held a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Xi made a state visit to North Korea in June, in a sign of improving ties.
US President Donald Trump has been eager to jump-start talks with North Korea, but United States and South Korean officials see fading chances of him meeting Kim this year, Reuters reported on Friday.
China hosts a summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum next month in Shenzhen, which Trump is expected to attend.

items.title: Allemagne-Le "nid d'aigle" des nazis en Bavière incendié
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Le "nid d'aigle", ancienne résidence des dignitaires du régime nazi dans les montagnes bavaroises du sud de l'Allemagne, a pris feu vendredi soir et un suspect a été arrêté, a annoncé la police allemande.
items.body:
Le "nid d'aigle", ancienne résidence des dignitaires du régime nazi dans les montagnes bavaroises du sud de l'Allemagne, a pris feu vendredi soir et un suspect a été arrêté, a annoncé la police allemande.
Environ 200 pompiers ont été déployés pour lutter contre l'incendie ravageant le bâtiment, le Kehlsteinhaus, près de Berchtesgaden.
La police a dit avoir arrêté un suspect près des lieux du sinistre.
Aucune piste n'a été évoquée concernant un éventuel mobile.
Construite en 1938 en tant que lieu de retraite pour les dignitaires nazis et leurs invités, cette bâtisse érigée au milieu des reliefs des Alpes est distincte de la résidence d'été d'Adolf Hitler, située à proximité et baptisée le Berghof.
Désormais propriété du Land de Bavière, le Kehlsteinhaus a été classé monument historique après la Seconde Guerre mondiale.

items.title: 30 años de Tamagotchi: la estrategia de Bandai Namco para convertirlo en la marca kawaii de Latinoamérica
items.author: Isaac Garrido
items.summary: La compañía japonesa aprovecha el auge de la nostalgia y los kidults para convertir el juguete en una marca de estilo de vida.
items.body: Cuando Mark Zuckerberg presentó en septiembre el Muse Charm, un dispositivo de bolsillo impulsado por el agente de inteligencia artificial de Meta, una generación entera lo comparó con un Tamagotchi. Su diminuto formato evocó a la mascota virtual con la que Bandai Namco conquistó el mercado a mediados de los noventa. En plena celebración de su 30 aniversario, con 100 millones de unidades distribuidas en todo el mundo hasta julio de 2025, la compañía japonesa busca consolidar al Tamagotchi en Latinoamérica como una marca referente del estilo de vida kawaii. Esta tendencia nipona se caracteriza por diseños tiernos y personajes adorables que generan vínculos emocionales con los consumidores. “Queremos ser la marca kawaii y electrónica juvenil número uno de toda la región”, dijo a Bloomberg Línea César Muratalla, director de marketing, ventas y licencias de Bandai Namco México y Latinoamérica. La meta, dijo el ejecutivo, es alcanzar esa posición para 2030 apoyados en acuerdos de licencia para categorías como ropa, papelería y productos de consumo. “No solo nos enfocamos en crecer el dispositivo, estamos produciendo muchos otros productos que no tienen que ver con el universo digital del Tamagotchi”, refirió sobre postres inspirados en el Tamagotchi que han lanzado con Dairy Queen o una línea de fundas para celulares lanzada por Casetify. Además explorarán nuevos canales de venta como la próxima llegada de Tamagotchi a la cadena Miniso. Lanzado a fines de 1996, el Tamagotchi definió una era al convertirse en la primera mascota virtual. Con forma de huevo y solo tres botones, el juguete permitía cuidar de una criatura, dándole cuidados como alimento y bañarlo. La fiebre occidental por aquella mascota de unos cuantos píxeles se apagó hacia finales de los noventa. Sin embargo, en Japón, Tamagotchi siguió evolucionando con versiones a color, modelos con Wi-Fi y colaboraciones con franquicias como Evangelion y Pokémon. El regreso a América se dio en 2017, cuando se relanzó el modelo original y encontró una oportunidad entre los millennials que crecieron con ella. Muratalla recuerda que lo incorporaron “de forma tímida”, pero “siempre se vendía todo”. En 2026, Tamagotchi vive una nueva efervescencia impulsada por la nostalgia y el auge de los kidults , adultos que compran juguetes por colección o nostalgia. Bandai Namco ha aprovechado este fenómeno para ampliar la presencia de su mascota electrónica en eventos como la San Diego Comic-Con y ha comenzado a abrir espacios especiales en tiendas departamentales como Liverpool, en México. “Estamos creciendo a triple dígito año con año”, apuntó Muratalla, quien precisó que el diminuto dispositivo ya comienza a conquistar a consumidores más jóvenes. De ahí que parte de la estrategia de crecimiento, se enfoque en el community marketing, una manera de Bandai Namco para mantener el vínculo con ellos a medida que crecen. “Si alguien compró un producto nuestro a los 10 años, lo va a querer seguir comprando cuando tenga 30 o 60 años”. Mientras se alista para el lanzamiento de Tamagotchi Ring, una nueva versión en anillo, la empresa japonesa también aprovechará la popularidad de cadenas asiáticas que han crecido en la región como Miniso y la recién llegada Daiso. “Eso nos dice que el mercado cada vez más quiere cosas kawaii, japonesas, cosas de las que Tamagotchi es su ADN”, dijo. “Recibimos muy bien la cultura japonesa, lo kawaii, eso nos gusta muchísimo como latinos”. De forma paralela, Bandai Namco desdoblará una ambiciosa estrategia para posicionar la marca Tamagotchi en toda Latinoamérica. Los esfuerzos comenzaron en Brasil, donde la compañía abrió cuentas oficiales. “Ha sido un fenómeno”, expresó Muratalla. La empresa apunta a Chile, Argentina, Colombia y Ecuador. “La intención es que vayamos coordinados a ser una mancha grande de una marca kawaii: Quiero que si piensas en alimento se vea Tamagotchi, si piensas en bebidas, también”. Para lograrlo, la compañía también contempla el retailtainment, una estrategia que combina la compra con actividades y espacios diseñados para generar una conexión más profunda entre consumidores y marcas. Muratalla comentó que un minorista está interesado en llevar a México el concepto de Tamagotchi Factory, una tienda experiencial de Tamagotchi ubicada en Tokio que se ha vuelto viral. La apuesta por llevar a Tamagotchi a otros niveles es tal que ya tienen en el radar llevar el huevecillo electrónico a la joyería de autor. Aunque por ahora es solo un plan, Muratalla advierte que en la era de la IA resguardarán la simpleza que coronó al dispositivo. “Por mas que evoluciones, cuidamos mucho la esencia. Eso lo valora la gente”.

items.title: Four Philippine Air Force pilots killed in training accident
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Two Philippine Air Force trainer aircraft crashed during a training flight at an air base south of the capital Manila, killing four pilots, the military said on Saturday.
items.body:
Two Philippine Air Force trainer aircraft crashed during a training flight at an air base south of the capital Manila, killing four pilots, the military said on Saturday.
The aviation accident on Friday involved two SF-260 aircraft during a training flight at the Fernando Air Base in Batangas province, the Philippine Air Force said in a statement
Local media has reported the two planes collided in midair
The aircraft crashed within the grounds of the air base but there were no other casualties
The Air Force has temporarily grounded its fleet of SF-260 trainer planes pending an investigation into the cause of the accident
In May, two pilots were killed when an SF-260 trainer aircraft crashed in a mountainous area in northern Philippines, while another SF-260 TP Marchetti [USN:L4N34A68W TEXT:"crashed"] during a 2023 training flight, also killing two pilots
The military used SF-260 aircraft during months of air strikes on southern [USN:KBN1CS0DM TEXT:"Marawi City"] after militants loyal to Islamic State seized the area in 2017

items.title: France's luxury stores board up windows ahead of fresh protests
items.author: Alessandro Parodi
items.creator: Alessandro Parodi
items.summary: Staff at LVMH brands Louis Vuitton, Dior and Bulgari said they weren't taking any chances and security at their stores had been increased for the day.
items.body:
Luxury boutiques in France boarded up their normally glitzy windows and added guards ahead of [USN:L1N4690GR TEXT:"fresh protests"] on Saturday, with some planning to stay closed after rioters looted shops across the country last weekend.
France, the most visited country in the world, draws large numbers of overseas shoppers seeking Chanel handbags and Hermes scarves, an important source of revenue for brands facing slowing demand.
But some decided staying open was too risky after [USN:L1N46608H TEXT:"last week's events"], when rioters smashed and looted hundreds of shops in Paris, Marseille and Bordeaux.
A Rolex retailer and a De Beers store near the capital's famous Place Vendome will remain closed on Saturday, staff said, while managers at stores including Richemont-owned (CFR.S) IWC said they would decide whether to close early depending on the intensity of the protests.
Groups including France's main student union UNEF and the Yellow Vest group, which emerged as a potent anti-establishment movement in 2018, plan to march through central Paris later on Saturday to protest against high living costs and cuts to public services.
NOT IN THE MOOD Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said on Friday that his ministry would deploy 70,000 police officers, backed by specialist units, to prevent the violence that occurred last week.
But staff at LVMH brands Louis Vuitton, Dior and Bulgari said they weren't taking any chances and security at their stores near Place Vendome had been increased for the day. Additional private security to supplement the police presence in the neighbourhood is also planned.
Nearby department store Printemps also increased its security staff, carried out safety repairs and added security measures to reinforce shop windows and entrances, a spokesperson for the store said.
Hermes finance chief Eric du Halgouet said this week the company had increased security measures at its French stores, adding it was too early to say how much impact recent events would have on business.
The image-conscious industry can ill afford further negative publicity. Consumer sentiment is gloomy worldwide and tourism is slowing as a result of the Iran war — contributing to disappointing quarterly reports at [USN:L6N45Y0VL TEXT:"LVMH"] (LVMH.PA) , [USN:L6N46816C TEXT:"Hermes"] (HRMS.PA) and [USN:L6N4680E3 TEXT:"Kering"] (PRTP.PA) this month.
Lidiya Shevchenko, a sales assistant at a Graziella Braccialini store, said she doubted many people would be looking to visit stores anyway during the protests.
"I suppose the mood is just as important when it comes to shopping," Shevchenko said.
One tourist who has already been put off is Cambodian Jerry Lay, who purchased several items from Louis Vuitton on the Champs-Élysées earlier this week.
"We do enjoy shopping in France, but after experiencing the protest (last Saturday), I'd say it's 50/50 whether I would consider coming back next time," Lay said.

items.title: 金総書記が訪中、昨年9月以来　丹東で李強首相と会談と報道
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ソウル　２４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ソウル　２４日　ロイター］ - 北朝鮮の金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記が２４日、中国を訪問した。韓国政府当局者が明らかにした。金氏の訪中は２０２５年９月以来で、１９５０─５３年の朝鮮戦争に中国人民義勇軍が参戦した日の前日というタイミングとなった。

韓国政府当局者によると、金氏は、開通したばかりの、中朝を結ぶ新鴨緑江大橋を渡り、中国遼寧省丹東に到着した。韓国聯合ニュースは、中国の李強首相が丹東で金氏と会談したと伝えた。

２５年９月の訪中時は、北京で開かれた戦勝８０周年の記念行事に出席し、習近平国家主席と会談した。習氏は今年６月に北朝鮮を公式訪問した。

トランプ米大統領は北朝鮮との対話再開に意欲を示している。１１月には中国・深センでアジア太平洋経済協力会議（ＡＰＥＣ）首脳会議が開催され、トランプ氏も出席する予定だ。 

金氏が今回利用した新鴨緑江大橋は今月開通した。橋自体は１４年に完成したが、北朝鮮側の準備が整わず、開通が遅れた。

items.title: Jordan tightens security after deadly church attack kills eight
items.author: Abdelhadi Ramahi
items.creator: Abdelhadi Ramahi
items.summary: Security was stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across Jordan, the US embassy in Amman said on Saturday, as authorities searched for gunmen who killed eight people and wounded 40 in a church attack.
items.body:
Security was stepped up at malls, foreign embassies and other locations across Jordan, the US embassy in Amman said on Saturday, as authorities searched for gunmen who killed eight people and wounded 40 in a church attack.
The assailants fired for several minutes in broad daylight during a funeral at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak governorate on Friday, in what Jordanian authorities described as an act of extremist terrorism. There was no immediate claim of responsibility.
Such attacks are rare in Jordan, although authorities in the US-allied kingdom say they have repeatedly foiled plots by Islamist militants in recent years.
Authorities said they were still searching for the attackers, adding it was too early to determine whether they had links to known groups inside or outside Jordan.
"A massacre, a massacre in every sense of the word," said Tarek Ammarin at a hospital where the wounded were being treated. A relative of Ammarin's was injured in the attack.
Reuters video footage showed police patrolling on Saturday outside the Hamoud church, about 120 km (75 miles) southwest of the capital Amman.
"This is a result of a terrorist ideology and blind extremism and we will not allow society to go down this path," Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said in a post on X.
Jordan's King Abdullah, a US partner in the fight against militant Islamist groups, visited Karak hours after the attack and said the perpetrators would be punished "with an iron fist".
Christians make up a minority of Jordan's population. The country is home to several biblical sites that attract Christian pilgrims from around the world.
Jordan has been among the US allies in the Middle East to be hit by Iranian attacks this year after the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February.

items.title: North Korea's Kim Jong Un visits China via Dandong bridge, South Korean official says
items.author: Joyce Lee
items.creator: Joyce Lee
items.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un arrived in China on Saturday, visiting the neighbouring country via a newly opened bridge, a South Korean government official said.
items.body:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un arrived in China on Saturday, visiting the neighbouring country via a newly opened bridge, a South Korean government official said.
Kim arrived in Dandong through the New Yalu River Bridge connecting North Korea and China, the official said on condition of anonymity as they are not authorised to speak publicly about the matter.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang met Kim in the border city, another South Korean official familiar with the matter said on condition of anonymity as they are not authorised to speak to media. Kim's visit comes a day before the anniversary of China joining the 1950-1953 Korean War.
Kim was expected to return to North Korea after Saturday's visit, South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported. A South Korean official familiar with the matter told Reuters it was unlikely Kim would visit Beijing ahead of high-level meetings of China's Communist Party from Monday.
China's foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
China and North Korea opened the 3-km (2-mile) New Yalu River Bridge, their most significant [USN:L1N46103M TEXT:"land border crossing,"] this month after a long delay, aiming to rejuvenate trade and commerce after years of strained ties and pandemic-related disruptions.
A visit by Kim now is consistent with the current phase of closer economic ties and more frequent high-level exchanges between China and North Korea, said Lu Chao, an expert in China-North Korea relations at the Liaoning Academy of Social Sciences, a Chinese government think-tank in Shenyang.
"The opening of the bridge has resolved a major bottleneck in China-North Korea trade logistics," Lu said. "With the logistics constraint eased, bilateral trade is likely to increase further."
The bridge is expected to help move heavy equipment, raw materials and energy products that North Korea needs for development. The opening is the latest sign of warming ties between Beijing and Pyongyang, after two summits between their leaders in the past 13 months.
Kim's last known visit to China was in September 2025, to attend the 80th Victory Day celebrations in Beijing, when he held a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping. Xi made a [USN:L1N42G106 TEXT:"state visit"] to North Korea in June.
"Kim has given his imprimatur to bilateral trade by crossing the New Yalu River Bridge to enter China," said Christopher Green, a Korea specialist at Leiden University in the Netherlands. "That bridge was for more than a decade a symbol of how dysfunctional bilateral relations could become."
China, which fought alongside North Korea in the Korean War, is Pyongyang's main economic and diplomatic backer and accounts for most of its official trade. However, North Korea has drawn closer to Russia since Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, which analysts say has reduced Pyongyang's reliance on Beijing.
US President Donald Trump has been eager to jump-start talks with North Korea, but US and South Korean officials see [USN:L1N4690EW TEXT:"fading chances"] of him meeting Kim this year, Reuters reported on Friday.
China hosts a summit of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum next month in Shenzhen, which Trump is expected to attend.

items.title: 米英首脳が電話会談、北海油田やウクライナ・フォークランド巡り協議
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ワシントン　２３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ワシントン　２３日　ロイター］ - トランプ米大統領は２３日、バーナム英首相と電話会談し、北海油田の開発について協議したと明らかにした。イランやウクライナの紛争についても「ごく軽く」触れたとしている。

トランプ氏は、中間選挙に向けフロリダ州での遊説に出発する前、ホワイトハウスで記者団に対し「彼らは北海油田を開放しようとしている」と述べた。「私は２年間それを求めてきた。アンディ（・バーナム氏）がそれを実現しつつある」と語った。

トランプ氏は２１日、英国が北海のジャックドー・ガス田の開発を承認したことを称賛した。

英首相府の声明によると、バーナム氏はまた、フォークランド諸島沖の石油探査問題も取り上げた。同諸島は英国の海外領土で広範な自治権を持つが、アルゼンチンが長年にわたり領有権を主張している。

バーナム氏はウクライナを巡り、ロシアに対して自衛するためにウクライナがスターリンクへの全面的なアクセスを確保することの重要性を強調した。また、ロシアのプーチン大統領を交渉の席に着かせようとするトランプ氏の努力を歓迎した。

両首脳は中東についても協議し、バーナム氏はフーシ派の攻撃に直面するサウジアラビアへの英国の支持を改めて表明したという。

items.title: How Trump's energy dominance turned into hubris
items.author: Ron Bousso
items.creator: Ron Bousso
items.summary: When Donald Trump returned to the White House in 2025, “energy dominance” was the bedrock of his economic and foreign policy plans. But an unpopular war with Iran and soaring household fuel costs have now made energy policy a major liability for the US president heading into next month’s midterm elections.
items.body:
When Donald Trump returned to the White House in 2025, [USN:L1N3Q1127 TEXT:"“energy dominance”"] was the bedrock of his economic and foreign policy plans. But an unpopular war with Iran and soaring household fuel costs have now made energy policy a major liability for the US president heading into next month’s midterm elections .
Ironically, it was the US position as the world's top oil and gas producer, perhaps more than anything else, that enabled Trump to pursue foreign policy goals that may turn out to be the costliest of his political career.
In the first two years of Trump’s second term, vast US oil and gas resources emboldened Washington abroad, strengthened its hand in trade disputes and underpinned a broader effort to restore US geopolitical dominance.
Yet the Iran war exposed the central weakness in that vision: dominating energy production does not mean controlling energy prices.
What began as a pursuit of US energy independence evolved into a doctrine of energy dominance. That is now looking like energy hubris.
UNLEASHING AMERICAN ENERGY The foundations of Trump’s strategy were laid long before his return to office last year. The development of cost-effective techniques to tap the country's onshore shale basins transformed the US into the world’s largest producer of natural gas in 2009 and petroleum in 2018. By 2022, it was the leading exporter of liquefied natural gas, giving Washington unprecedented influence over global energy markets.
US crude production rose from around 5.5 million barrels per day in 2010 to nearly 14 million bpd today, around a fifth of global supplies, while the country also accounts for more than a quarter of global LNG exports. No single nation has ever occupied such a commanding position in the global energy system.
Trump sought to turn that advantage into a governing doctrine.
On his first day back in office, he declared a national energy emergency and ordered the government to [USN:S0N3NI004 TEXT:"“unleash American energy”"], prioritising oil, gas, coal and nuclear power while sidelining renewables.
Within weeks, he made “energy dominance” official US policy, establishing the National Energy Dominance Council and reviving his familiar “drill, baby, drill” slogan as the purported cure for elevated inflation and economic anxiety. In an October 2025 proclamation, Trump summed up the philosophy as “maximum production, maximum prosperity, and maximum power”.
ENERGY POLICY IS FOREIGN POLICY This doctrine extended far beyond domestic energy policy.
The administration’s national security strategy, published last December, explicitly linked US influence in the Western Hemisphere to energy dominance, drawing on the 19th-century Monroe Doctrine that sought to oppose European political intervention in the region.
In a little over a year, the administration wielded US oil and LNG exports in trade negotiations, promoted energy deals as part of efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war , and highlighted Greenland’s resource wealth in a push for greater influence over the [USN:L6N45E05Y TEXT:"Arctic territory"].
The high-water mark for Trump’s energy doctrine arguably came early this year after [USN:L6N3Y407K TEXT:"Washington removed Venezuelan President"] Nicolas Maduro in a swift military operation.
The US subsequently [USN:L1N3ZM1KL TEXT:"took control"] of Venezuelan oil exports and revenues, forced through changes to the country’s hydrocarbons legislation that displaced Chinese companies, and secured an unprecedented agreement granting it access to a fifth of Venezuela’s oil reserves.
By February, Trump’s vision of building an economy and foreign policy around abundant fossil fuel resources appeared to be taking root. The US possessed not only more energy than any rival, but also the ability to use that abundance to shape trade, diplomacy and security.
Trump’s decision to go to war with Iran in late February put that doctrine to the test.
THE IRAN QUAGMIRE The president initially claimed that the joint campaign with Israel against Iran would last only a few weeks. He also repeatedly indicated that vast US oil and gas resources, together with newfound access to Venezuela’s oil wealth, would shield the economy from any resulting spike in energy costs, which he also suggested would be brief.
Those assumptions have not aged well.
The war launched on February 28 led to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly one-fifth of global energy supplies used to flow, triggering one of the largest energy disruptions in modern history. Middle Eastern producers cut output and rerouted exports where possible, while major importers across Asia reduced consumption.
This caused oil prices to nearly double in the first two months of the conflict, with global benchmark Brent crude peaking at $118 a barrel in March.
That was well below the record [USN:L03220220 TEXT:"$145 reached in 2008"], when Iran-related geopolitical tensions, surging Chinese demand and a weakening US dollar drove prices higher. It was also far less than many had feared, largely thanks to reduced Chinese oil imports, ample crude stocks and the surprising adaptability of global markets. But it still represented a severe shock.
Moreover, the risk premium from the Iran war is becoming entrenched. Even though crude flows from the Middle East have mostly recovered, Brent is trading around $110.
The conflict has also spread across the Middle East, pulling in most of Washington's Gulf allies, most notably the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia, which have suffered multiple deadly attacks by Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis. This has upended the market’s confidence in the security of Middle Eastern crude, unravelled longstanding supply routes and sent [USN:L6N45R160 TEXT:"shipping prices"] skyrocketing.
Trump wanted to put his stamp on global energy markets, but this was clearly not what he had in mind.
PAIN AT THE PUMP In one respect, the 2026 energy shock has vindicated Trump’s strategy. The war cemented the US position as the world’s top supplier of crude, refined fuels and LNG, delivering enormous profits to domestic producers and exporters and allowing the US to expand its position in the global market.
Energy independence certainly offered US consumers some protection against the energy shock, particularly compared with Asian economies, where prices and demand destruction were much more extreme this year.
But that protection has been far from ironclad.
US gasoline prices at the pump climbed above $4.60 a gallon in May, the highest level since 2022, while [USN:L1N45211Q TEXT:"diesel"] surged to a record $6.50 a gallon in September as global refining capacity was squeezed.
Those increases rapidly became a political problem for the White House as cost-of-living concerns moved to the forefront of the campaign ahead of the midterms on November 3.
The administration sought to contain the fuel-price spike by pulling almost every available lever, including [USN:L6N44M0V8 TEXT:"easing biofuel blending mandates"] and, most controversially, reaching a [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"diesel supply agreement"] with Russian President Vladimir Putin.
This dynamic underscores the difference between commanding supply and controlling prices.
Oil, LNG and refined fuels are internationally traded commodities. US producers sell them at prices shaped by global supply and demand. They don’t typically reserve cheap energy for American households.
While Trump briefly floated the idea of a [USN:L6N45E0T3 TEXT:"diesel export ban"], officials ultimately rejected it. Even though a ban might have brought down domestic prices initially, it would likely have resulted in higher fuel prices over the medium term due to global market dynamics.
‘ENERGY SECURITY IS NATIONAL SECURITY’ The administration’s assertion last October that “energy security is national security” appears more relevant than ever. The Iran war has shown that cheap and reliable energy is essential for economic growth, whether it powers heavy industry or the data centres underpinning the artificial intelligence race.
But the conflict has also changed the meaning of energy security.
For countries dependent on imports, particularly [USN:L6N3ZY18D TEXT:"many in Asia"], the shock has revealed the risks of relying heavily on distant suppliers, vulnerable shipping routes and a concentrated global refining system. Their response is likely to be broader diversification: securing more suppliers, expanding domestic fossil fuel production where possible, accelerating renewable power and shifting more transport towards electricity.
That will not kick the US off its lofty energy perch, but it will likely weaken the allure of oil and gas for many countries over the coming years.
Trump likely felt emboldened to embark on the Iran war — something his predecessors had baulked at — precisely because US energy independence made a Middle East adventure seem less risky than it had when the US was heavily reliant on Gulf oil and gas.
But the conflict has, perhaps permanently, undermined Trump’s promise that energy dominance would guarantee low prices and economic security at home.
Hubris can be a dangerous thing.
(The opinions expressed here are those of Ron Bousso , a columnist for Reuters.)

items.title: Mumbai Indians promote Pollard to head coach, replacing Jayawardene
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Mumbai Indians have appointed Kieron Pollard as head coach for the 2027 season in place of Mahela Jayawardene, the Indian Premier League team said on Saturday.
items.body:
Mumbai Indians have appointed Kieron Pollard as head coach for the 2027 season in place of Mahela Jayawardene, the Indian Premier League team said on Saturday.
Pollard, who helped the West Indies win the Twenty20 World Cup in 2012 and won five IPL titles with the Mumbai Indians between 2013 and 2020, served as the team's batting coach under Jayawardene before the [USN:L4N46300R TEXT:"Sri Lankan's departure"] last week.
Mumbai Indians are the joint most-successful side in IPL history, with five titles, but have struggled since their last victory, finishing outside the playoffs in four of the past six seasons.
"Having experienced this journey as a player and then as a coach, I understand what Mumbai Indians stands for and the responsibility that comes with representing the Blue and Gold," the 39-year-old said in a statement.
"I look forward to working closely with the players and support staff, building on the team's legacy, helping our talent grow and giving the (fans) many more reasons to celebrate."

items.title: ＧＭＯ、政府に能動的サイバー防御要請　金銭の要求には応じず
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２４日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Kentaro Okasaka

[東京 ２４日 ロイター] - ＧＭＯインターネットは２４日、自社のＦＸ（外国為替証拠金取引）の自動売買サービスが受けたサイバー攻撃について、「能動的サイバー防御」の適用を政府に緊急要請したと発表した。攻撃者とみられる相手から同社に対し金銭の要求があり、応じなければ自社や顧客の情報を公開するとの連絡を受けたという。

要求には応じない方針。警察などと連携して対応するとしている。また、サービスの全利用者に一律５０００円の見舞金を支払うことを決めた。

能動的サイバー防御は、被害が深刻化する前に国や関係機関が主導して攻撃者のインフラや侵入経路を特定し、無力化して被害の未然防止を図る仕組み。同社は今回の事案について、一般国民の取引口座（金融資産）を標的とした不正操作・資産毀損という「極めて悪質かつ前例のない手口」だと判断。政府に先制的な対応を求めることを決めた。

同社によると、今月１９日に顧客からの問い合わせを受け調査を開始。２０日にサービスの一部顧客のサーバー環境への不正なプログラムの設置を確認し、２１日には被害拡大防止のため全プランのサーバーを順次停止した。顧客から取引口座での身に覚えのない操作などの報告があり、２２日に警察へ相談したという。

[東京 ２４日 ロイター] - ＧＭＯインターネットは２４日、自社のＦＸ（外国為替証拠金取引）の自動売買サービスが受けたサイバー攻撃について、「能動的サイバー防御」の適用を政府に緊急要請したと発表した。攻撃者とみられる相手から同社に対し金銭の要求があり、応じなければ自社や顧客の情報を公開するとの連絡を受けたという。

要求には応じない方針。警察などと連携して対応するとしている。また、サービスの全利用者に一律５０００円の見舞金を支払うことを決めた。

能動的サイバー防御は、被害が深刻化する前に国や関係機関が主導して攻撃者のインフラや侵入経路を特定し、無力化して被害の未然防止を図る仕組み。同社は今回の事案について、一般国民の取引口座（金融資産）を標的とした不正操作・資産毀損という「極めて悪質かつ前例のない手口」だと判断。政府に先制的な対応を求めることを決めた。

同社によると、今月１９日に顧客からの問い合わせを受け調査を開始。２０日にサービスの一部顧客のサーバー環境への不正なプログラムの設置を確認し、２１日には被害拡大防止のため全プランのサーバーを順次停止した。顧客から取引口座での身に覚えのない操作などの報告があり、２２日に警察へ相談したという。

items.title: Último debate entre Flávio e Lula reedita troca de acusações e avança pouco em propostas
items.author: Maria Marcello
items.creator: Maria Marcello
items.summary: A dois dias do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, o debate entre os dois candidatos -- o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) -- na TV Globo foi palco de mais um round de trocas de acusações e avançou um pouco em relação à exposição de planos de governo.
items.body:
A dois dias do segundo turno da eleição presidencial, o debate entre os dois candidatos -- o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e o senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) -- na TV Globo foi palco de mais um round de trocas de acusações e avançou um pouco em relação à exposição de planos de governo.
Os candidatos foram para o debate com estratégias específicas de olho no eleitor indeciso. Flávio decidiu focar no custo de vida e prometeu manter programas sociais. Lula chamou a atenção para a defesa da democracia e lembrou que foram os governos petistas que criaram e reforçaram os programas sociais em vigor.
"Em quatro anos de governo, você consegue comprar mais ou menos com o seu salário?", questionou Flávio.
"Está difícil comprar. Quando você consegue comprar, você está levando menos para a sua casa, esse é o legado do atual governo", disse Flávio.
Já Lula, não só defendeu a democracia como acusou o adversário de "miliciano".
"Eu sou um homem que tenho biografia, tenho história", disse o presidente. "Eu queria, primeiro agradecer... e pedir o voto de vocês no domingo porque ou a gente mantém a democracia funcionando ou a gente vai ter um miliciano governando esse país dentro do Palácio do Planalto", disse Lula, em menção a Flávio que rendeu um direito de resposta ao senador.
Flávio negou envolvimento com milícia na sequência -- "isso é coisa da sua cabeça" -- e prometeu classificar as milícias como narcoterroristas.
A organização do debate chegou a impor regras sobre a circulação dos candidatos, de forma a evitar desgastes ocorridos no debate de domingo na TV Band. Veículos e entidades paralelamente fizeram o acompanhamento do debate para checagem de fatos. Mas ainda assim, houve uma reedição de trocas de acusações e era perceptível o clima de Fla-Flu na plateia, que em alguns momentos chegou a se manifestar.
Lula questionou Flávio sobre posicionamentos públicos do senador contrários a programas sociais e chegou a perguntar ao senador por que se referiu ao Bolsa-Família como "Bolsa-Farelo".
Flávio, por sua vez, apontou a gestão petista dos gastos públicos como responsável pelos juros altos, que resvalam no poder de compra da população. No quesito juros, aliás, Lula lembrou que foi no governo de Jair Bolsonaro, pai de Flávio, que foi aprovada a autonomia do Banco Central, entidade responsável pela definição da taxa básica de juros do país.
Os candidatos também conseguiram emplacar argumentos e frases com forte apelo, principalmente para os cortes e edições de trechos a serem usados nas redes sociais nessas últimas horas antes da abertura das urnas eleitorais.
Em resposta a Flávio, que referiu-se ao presidente como "nove dedos", Lula lembrou que perdeu o dedo em um acidente de trabalho.
"Se tem alguém aqui nesse púlpito que sabe o que é o mundo do trabalho sou eu. Se tem alguém que perdeu o dedo com 17 anos fui eu", disse Lula, provocando reações da plateia. "Milhões de trabalhadores se acidentam por irresponsabilidade patronal, que obriga a gente a trabalhar em jornada que a gente tem que trabalhar. Eu era menor e trabalhava à noite, porque ou trabalhava ou não comia e não vou aceitar que um granfino, com uma prática política muito duvidosa, venha me chamar de nove dedos."
Após a dura declaração do presidente, Flávio se desculpou, dizendo que não tinha intenção de ser ofensivo.
O senador, por outro lado, buscou se apresentar como o candidato da mudança, da novidade.
"Nem parece que ele é o atual presidente da República... Ele parece que parou no tempo. Infelizmente o atual presidente da República, as ideias que ele tinha -- que eram boas lá atrás --... hoje não funcionam mais", afirmou.
Os dois também cometeram deslizes no decorrer do debate. Lula volta e meia se perdia nas regras e precisava ser lembrado pelo moderador que ainda tinha tempo para desenvolver sua fala.
Já Flávio -- questionado por Lula sobre sua escolha em atuar na defesa de um policial acusado de matar uma criança de 5 anos em Niterói, no Rio de Janeiro -- cometeu um equívoco. Na intenção de prestar solidariedade à mãe da menina, que estava na plateia, se confundiu ao chamá-la pelo nome da criança morta.
Em outro momento, o ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro voltou a ser citado. Lula cobrou Flávio sobre o dinheiro que pediu ao banqueiro -- o senador reafirmou que era para o financiamento de um filme sobre seu pai, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro. O senador, por sua vez, acusou Lula de receber um uísque do banqueiro de presente.
Houve até mesmo uma renovação do desafio de Lula para que os dois abram suas contas bancárias e provem que não são corruptos.
Flávio Bolsonaro é alvo de dois inquéritos no STF: um que apura suspeitas relacionadas exatamente ao financiamento do filme "Dark Horse" e outro sobre suspeita de lavagem de dinheiro envolvendo o advogado Willer Tomaz.
Mas se Lula não é alvo de investigação criminal conhecida atualmente, Flávio voltou a se concentrar em seu filho, conhecido como Lulinha, que é investigado pela Polícia Federal sobre suposto tráfico de influência.
Na segunda metade do debate, quando os ataques e acusações de ambos os candidatos se intensificaram, a plateia começou a se manifestar e a reagir a respostas dos presidenciáveis. O clima, no entanto, foi mais ameno que no debate do último domingo.

items.title: 米司法省、アラスカ上院選の結果認定阻止へ訴訟　「候補者名酷似」理由に
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［２３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［２３日　ロイター］ - 米司法省は２２日、１１月中間選挙のアラスカ州連邦上院選で共和党の現職候補が僅差で敗北した場合に、州による選挙結果の認定を差し止めるよう求める訴訟を起こした。投票用紙にほぼ同姓同名の共和党候補が２人記載されており、有権者の混乱を招く恐れがあると主張している。

アラスカは共和党が上院多数派を維持できるかを左右する可能性のある州の一つで、共和党の現職ダン・Ｓ・サリバン氏が、民主党のメアリー・ペルトラ氏と接戦を繰り広げている。

司法省は、選挙にダン・Ｊ・サリバン・ジュニアという名の共和党候補が出馬していることを問題視。訴状は、同氏が「サリバン上院議員の支持者を誤って自身に投票させる意図を持って」立候補していると主張している。

司法省は訴状で、「有権者の混乱の影響を受けた可能性がある」結果の認定を差し止めるよう要請。これにより「ダニエル・Ｊ・サリバン氏に投じられた票が本来はサリバン上院議員に投じられるはずだったものかどうかを調べる調査」が可能になるとしている。

トランプ大統領は２３日、記者団に対して、訴訟を支持すると述べ「やれと言ったのは私だ」と語った。

items.title: ＭＬＢ＝ＷＳ開幕、ブルワーズが先勝　ミジオロウスキーが最速記録
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［２３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［２３日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は２３日、ワールドシリーズ（ＷＳ、７回戦制）の第１戦を行い、ブルワーズがレイズを３─２で下し、先勝した。

１９８２年以来４４年ぶりのＷＳ出場となったブルワーズは一回、指名打者クリスチャン・イエリチの適時三塁打で先制し、ウィリアム・コントレラス捕手の適時打で２点目を挙げた。

四回に１点を返されたが、七回にはジャクソン・チョウリオ外野手の適時打で１点を追加。九回には１点差に迫られ、２死二、三塁のピンチを迎えたものの、４番手トレバー・メギル投手が最後の打者を三振に仕留めた。

先発ジェーコブ・ミジオロウスキー投手は５回を投げ、４安打１失点、１四球、３三振で勝利投手となった。試合の初球に時速１０３．５マイル（約１６６．６キロ）を計測し、球速の計測が始まった２００８年以降のＷＳ最速記録を樹立した。

items.title: 北朝鮮の金総書記、「軍事革命」加速を要求　精鋭部隊育成へ
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［ソウル　２４日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［ソウル　２４日　ロイター］ - 北朝鮮の金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記は、平壌で２日間にわたり開かれた朝鮮人民軍の中隊長会議で、各中隊を自立して戦闘を遂行できる精鋭部隊にするよう求めた。朝鮮中央通信（ＫＣＮＡ）が２４日に伝えた。

今回の会議は、軍事力強化を一貫して政策の優先課題とする金氏の姿勢を鮮明にした。

金氏は１０月２２─２３日に開かれた会議で演説し、「新時代の軍備増強の目標」の達成に向け、全ての中隊が万全の準備を整えるよう求めた。ＫＣＮＡによると、２月の第９回朝鮮労働党大会以降、全軍規模の会議が開かれたのは初めて。

金氏は「最強の軍隊を建設し、われわれの方式による軍事革命を加速させよう」と述べた。

今後５年間の国家の方向性を定める２月の第９回党大会で、金氏は通常戦力の強化を求めるとともに、核兵器とミサイルの開発を進める方針を改めて示していた。

items.title: ＮＢＡ＝八村、古巣レーカーズ戦で16得点　クリッパーズは初黒星
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［２３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
［２３日　ロイター］ - 米プロバスケットボール協会（ＮＢＡ）は２３日、各地で試合を行い、八村塁が先発したクリッパーズはレーカーズに１１７─１２５で敗れ、今季初黒星を喫した。

古巣対戦となった八村は計３３分１６秒の出場で、３本の３点シュートを沈めるなど１６得点、６リバウンド、１アシスト、２スチールだった。ダリアス・ガーランドがチーム最多の２６得点を記録した。レーカーズはオースティン・リーブスが２８得点、９アシストで牽引。ルカ・ドンチッチは２３得点、６リバウンド、７アシストも、１１回のターンオーバーを喫した。

セルティックスは昨季王者のニックスに１０７─１０３で競り勝ち、今季初勝利を挙げた。ジェイソン・テイタムが両チーム最多の３６得点に、９リバウンド、７アシストと活躍。ニックスはカールアンソニー・タウンズ、ＯＧ・アヌノビー、マイルズ・マクブライドの３選手が２０得点以上を記録したが及ばなかった。

ロケッツは昨季西地区覇者のスパーズを１１４─１１０で下した。アルペレン・シェングンが両チーム最多の２９得点に、ケビン・デュラントとアメン・トンプソンも２０得点を記録した。スパーズはビクター・ウェンバンヤマが２５得点、１３リバウンドと奮闘した。

ピストンズはヒートに１２８─１１１で勝利し、２連勝とした。ポール・リードが１９得点、１１リバウンド、３アシストのダブルダブルで貢献。ヒートはヤニス・アデトクンボが３６得点、１２リバウンド、５アシストと躍動したが、チーム全体の３点シュート成功率が２９．４％にとどまり、２連敗となった。

ティンバーウルブズはマジックを１１５─９３で下し、２連勝。そのほか、ホークス、ラプターズ、グリズリーズ、トレイルブレイザーズも２連勝とした。

items.title: Atlético de San Luis gana de visita al Atlante en el torneo mexicano de fútbol
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Atlético de San Luis sacó el viernes un triunfo de su visita al Atlante por 1-0 en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
items.body:
Atlético de San Luis sacó el viernes un triunfo de su visita al Atlante por 1-0 en la decimocuarta jornada del torneo Apertura del fútbol mexicano.
Con su quinto triunfo, Atlético de San Luis llegó a 19 puntos para ubicarse en el décimo lugar general, cerca de la zona que da acceso a la postemporada. Los clubes que ocupan los primeros ocho lugares de la tabla general al final de las 17 jornadas de la temporada regular clasifican a dicha instancia.
En el partido disputado en el estadio Azteca de la Ciudad de México, Atlético de San Luis se puso en ventaja a los 59 minutos por conducto de Benjamín Galdames, quien metió el balón por el ángulo izquierdo con un disparo desde el vértice del área.
En el transcurso del encuentro, ambos clubes tuvieron opciones de anotar, pero las atinadas intervenciones de los porteros evitaron que se concretaran.
Atlante tuvo la oportunidad más clara de empatar en tiempo de reposición con un tiro penal, pero el portero Gibran Lajud tapó el disparo del paraguayo Walter Clar, quien en el contraremate estrelló el balón en el travesaño a los 94 minutos.
En el otro partido que se jugó el viernes, Necaxa y Bravos de Ciudad Juárez empataron 1-1. Para Necaxa anotó Owen González y para Bravos de Ciudad Juárez lo hizo Luca Martínez.
El sábado, León jugará ante Toluca, Guadalajara visitará a Monterrey y Pumas UNAM enfrentará a Tigres UANL.
El domingo, Atlas será local ante Puebla, el actual campeón Cruz Azul visitará a Querétaro, el líder América jugará ante Pachuca y Tijuana será rival de Santos Laguna.

items.title: Late 17-0 surge carries Grizzlies to comeback win over Warriors
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Ty Jerome scored a game-high 28 points and the Memphis Grizzlies used a 17-0 fourth-quarter spurt to rally for a 111-108 victory over the Golden State Warriors in San Francisco on Friday.
items.body:
Ty Jerome scored a game-high 28 points and the Memphis Grizzlies used a 17-0 fourth-quarter spurt to rally for a 111-108 victory over the Golden State Warriors in San Francisco on Friday.
Rookie Cameron Boozer added 25 points, 13 rebounds and six assists for Memphis, which won its second straight game to begin the season. Jaylen Wells scored 17 and Cam Spencer chipped in 11 for the Grizzlies, who outscored Golden State 27-18 in the fourth quarter.
Stephen Curry's 24 points led the Warriors, while Brandin Podziemski and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg contributed 18 points apiece. In his second career game, Lendeborg also tallied 13 rebounds and six assists.
Graham Ike and De'Anthony Melton both scored 10 points for Golden State, which has dropped its first two games of the year for the first time since 2020-21.
After trailing by four at halftime, Golden State took its first lead of the third quarter on Podziemski's 3-pointer with 2:09 left to put the Warriors ahead 86-84.
Golden State finished the third on an 11-0 run and held a 90-84 advantage entering the final quarter.
Spencer hit a triple to cut Memphis' deficit to three with 6:54 left before Melton and Lendeborg made back-to-back treys and Podziemski sank a driving layup to extend Golden State's lead to 103-92.
Melton drilled another triple to make it a 12-point game with 3:47 to go, but the Grizzlies answered with 17 straight points, including Boozer's turnaround jumper to give the visitors a 108-106 lead with 20.1 seconds left.
Draymond Green was then whistled for an offensive foul, leading to a technical foul on Warriors coach Steve Kerr with 12.8 seconds remaining. Jerome made the technical foul shot and hit a layup to give Memphis a 111-106 lead.
Lendeborg rebounded a Melton miss and was fouled with a half-second remaining. He made both foul shots to cut the deficit to three.
The Grizzlies then ran out the clock on the ensuing possession to ice the comeback win.
Podziemski sank each of his four first-quarter field-goal attempts, including a buzzer-beating runner, to help the Warriors take a 34-33 lead into the second quarter.
Trailing by a point, Memphis rattled off a 16-2 run and grabbed a 54-41 lead on Spencer's 3-pointer with 4:42 remaining in the first half.
A 10-0 Golden State run, stamped with Gui Santos' free throws, pulled the Warriors within a point. Jerami Grant finished the opening half with a three-point play to give the Grizzlies a 60-56 advantage at the break.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Trump foreign policy hits voters in the pocketbook, imperiling Republicans in midterms
items.author: Matt Spetalnick
items.creator: Matt Spetalnick
items.summary: Foreign policy is rarely the deciding factor in US midterm elections. But this time, Trump’s approach to world affairs has itself become a pocketbook issue.
items.body:
Foreign policy is rarely the deciding factor in US midterm elections, when economic considerations usually drive voters’ choices.
But this time, with Donald Trump’s war against Iran and his sweeping tariff campaign pushing up costs for Americans, a president’s approach to world affairs has itself become a pocketbook issue.
As the November 3 elections approach, there are growing signs that voters are drawing that connection directly, creating a major liability for Trump and his fellow Republicans and imperiling their control of Congress.
Those include a Reuters/Ipsos poll earlier this month showing some 78% of Americans [USN:L6N45T0W3 TEXT:"blame Trump's policies"] for rising prices that are outpacing their earnings.
Not since 2006, when President George W. Bush’s Republicans lost both legislative chambers while he was mired in the unpopular Iraq war, has a US leader’s handling of international events appeared so central to shaping the midterms outcome.
The political backlash for Trump could be even bigger, with opinion polls showing that voters feel the economic pain from high gas prices and rising grocery bills in a way that they didn’t two decades ago.
“The bottom line is people are experiencing the impact of Trump’s war and other policies,” said Christopher Preble, a senior fellow at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington. “Now voters have a chance to register their discontent with how he’s dealing with all this.”
POLITICS DRIVING FOREIGN POLICY With Trump’s [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"approval ratings"] touching historic lows, he has left little doubt, despite his public claims to the contrary, that he sees the straight line voters are drawing between his foreign policy and their cost of living.
That has prompted some controversial policy moves in the run-up to the elections.
Chief among them was Trump’s lifting of sanctions on [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"Russian diesel"] exports aimed at bringing down fuel prices, a step his critics, including some fellow Republicans, say reinforces the impression that he is increasingly siding with Moscow in its war in Ukraine.
He has also pressed Kyiv to halt strikes on [USN:L1N46203J TEXT:"Russian refineries"] as he tries to shift the blame for high US gasoline prices despite experts saying the surge in energy costs is mainly the result of the war he launched alongside Israel against Iran nearly eight months ago.
At the same time, he has promised not to order any [USN:FWN45U1SW TEXT:"new attack"] on Iran before the midterms, though the US and Israel are widely reported to be preparing for a possible major escalation after the elections.
Polls have shown that most voters oppose the war initiated by Trump, who had campaigned on avoiding new foreign interventions. He has insisted Americans should accept temporarily higher gas prices so that he can block Iran from developing a nuclear weapon.
Iran says its nuclear program is for civilian purposes. The UN nuclear watchdog and US intelligence community have assessed that Tehran shuttered a nuclear weapons development program in 2003.
Some Republican candidates have [USN:L4N45N1R0 TEXT:"distanced themselves"] from Trump on matters ranging from the conflict in the Middle East to the trade war with Canada and his pressure campaign against Ukraine.
For its part, Iran has sought to keep oil prices high and hurt Trump in the midterms by deploying new tactics to target ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and deliberately prolonging the [USN:L8N46515R TEXT:"diplomatic stalemate"], senior Iranian officials have told Reuters.
Defending the administration's approach, White House spokesman Matt Middleton said: "President Trump has always been clear about temporary market disruptions as a result of the conflict in Iran, but the contrast between President Trump’s economic record and Democrats’ ruinous alternative is clear."
‘IT’S THE ECONOMY, STUPID’ Midterm elections historically have been seen as a referendum on the performance of the incumbent in the White House.
And in one election after another in recent decades, the conventional wisdom has been that economic concerns - “it’s the economy, stupid,” as the Clinton-era adage goes - dominate voters’ choices.
Opinion polls for this year’s midterms, including the Reuters/Ipsos survey, show that while voters rank foreign policy low on their list of priorities, it is clear that most Americans see some of Trump’s signature moves on the world stage, such as the Iran war and tariffs, feeding into their higher costs.
Other polls have shown that a majority of Americans have also soured more broadly on Trump’s international approach.
The Chicago Council on Global Affairs said its latest nationwide survey “finds that most Americans believe the Trump administration’s foreign policy actions have negatively impacted America’s global standing and hurt national and household economic conditions.”
Since returning to the White House last year, Trump has shaken up the rules-based global order that Washington helped create from the ashes of World War Two while his relations with allies have steadily worsened and the [USN:L1N45G0ZJ TEXT:"limits of US power"] have been increasingly exposed, analysts say.
LEGISLATIVE BALANCE OF POWER IN PLAY Against this backdrop, Democrats are widely projected to [USN:L6N465159 TEXT:"gain control"] of the House of Representatives in the midterms, with the Senate also seen as increasingly in play.
For Republicans, losing either chamber could complicate Trump's agenda in the last two years of his second term.
But even with a shift in the balance of power on Capitol Hill on November 3, lawmakers will have a hard time reining in Trump’s capacity to pursue foreign policy as he sees fit.
Once the ballots are counted, a big question will be whether Trump will feel either restricted or emboldened on the world stage as he enters what is traditionally considered a lame-duck phase - when a president is barred from running again and no longer faces electoral consequences for decisions made.
“For many presidents who feel politically constrained (at home), foreign policy is the area where they are able to act with relative freedom,” said Jon Alterman of the Center for Strategic and International Studies think tank in Washington.
Analysts say Trump's handling of adversaries such as Iran, Russia, China and even Cuba or his approach to allies across the globe could go either way -- or he could simply lose interest and double down on his string of construction projects, such as the White House ballroom.
