items.title: Deni Avdija propels Blazers to comeback victory over Kings
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Deni Avdija scored 26 points and the Portland Trail Blazers overcame a 12-point first-quarter deficit en route to a 128-120 victory over the host Sacramento Kings on Friday night.
items.body:
Deni Avdija scored 26 points and the Portland Trail Blazers overcame a 12-point first-quarter deficit en route to a 128-120 victory over the host Sacramento Kings on Friday night.
Damian Lillard and Toumani Camara scored 19 points apiece and Sidy Cissoko scored 15 points, all in the first half, as Portland improved to 2-0. Robert Williams III scored 13 points while Ja Morant and Jrue Holiday each had 12 points for the Trail Blazers.
Kings rookie Darius Acuff Jr. scored 33 points in his second career game and Domantas Sabonis had 27 points, 19 rebounds and 10 assists for his 69th career triple-double.
Zach LaVine scored 22 points, Precious Achiuwa added 14 and Keegan Murray had 12 as Sacramento lost its second straight game to open the season. The contest was the Kings' home opener.
Portland shot 47.9% from the field, including 14 of 48 (29.2%) from 3-point range. Camara made five 3-pointers and Donovan Clingan grabbed 10 rebounds for the Trail Blazers.
The Kings made 46.2% of their attempts and were 8 of 31 (25.8%) from behind the arc.
Portland scored the first 15 points of the third quarter to turn a five-point deficit into a 74-64 advantage. Camara scored the final seven points of the burst.
Morant drained a 3-pointer to make it 84-73 just prior to the midway point of the quarter. Sacramento trailed 88-83 after Achiuwa's layup with 3:39 remaining in the period before Portland pushed the lead back to 103-90 on Avdija's floater with 1.3 seconds left.
The Trail Blazers had an 8-1 edge in 3-pointers during a 44-point third quarter while committing just one turnover.
Lillard's short jumper gave Portland a 113-102 edge with 7:09 remaining. Acuff scored the next six points for Sacramento, and he later connected on a 3-pointer to bring the Kings within 118-113 with 4:51 to play.
Sacramento got within three, but Camara responded with a trey to give Portland a 121-115 lead with 3:47 left.
Four straight points by Clingan gave the Trail Blazers a seven-point lead with 1:50 to play.
Avdija sank two free throws to make it an eight-point margin with 28.3 seconds left as Portland sealed its fifth straight victory over the Kings.
Sabonis had 17 points, 12 rebounds and seven assists in the first half, when the Kings never trailed. Sacramento led 64-59 at the break.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Uncovering 'heat storms'
items.summary: Why we needed new language to describe modern heat waves
items.body:
Follow on Apple or Spotify . Listen on the Reuters app.

Reuters reporters set out to define a heat wave and uncovered something far bigger: "heat storms" that now blanket vast stretches of the planet. On this episode of On Assignment, the journalists behind the investigation, Maurice Tamman and Ben Welsh, explain how extreme heat became a constant feature of modern life, and why they needed a new language to describe it.

items.title: Lakers ride 39-point 3rd quarter to surge past Clippers
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Austin Reaves scored 28 points and added nine assists while Luka Doncic recorded 23 points as the Los Angeles Lakers used a third-quarter surge to stay perfect through two games with a 125-117 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Clippers on Friday.
items.body:
Austin Reaves scored 28 points and added nine assists while Luka Doncic recorded 23 points as the Los Angeles Lakers used a third-quarter surge to stay perfect through two games with a 125-117 victory over the visiting Los Angeles Clippers on Friday.
Walker Kessler scored 22 points, Ziaire Williams contributed 14, while Matisse Thybulle and Quentin Grimes each had 13 as the Lakers won for the ninth time in their past 13 games against the cross-town Clippers.
Kessler hit 10 of 14 shots from the floor and is now 22 of 26 over two games with his new team after a trade from the Utah Jazz in July. The Lakers had 13 steals and forced the Clippers into 26 turnovers that they turned into 33 points.
Doncic committed 11 turnovers, while Kessler and Grimes led all rebounders with eight apiece.
Darius Garland scored 26 points and Brook Lopez added 22 as the Clippers dropped their first road game of the season. Derrick Jones Jr. and Rui Hachimura each scored 16 points.
The Clippers shot 49.4% from the floor and 43.2% from 3-point range but lost as the Lakers shot 58.2% from the floor and 43.8% from distance.
The Lakers led 77-76 with 7:18 remaining in the third quarter when a 3-pointer from Thybulle kicked off a 14-1 run that gave them a 91-77 lead with 3:43 remaining in the period.
The Lakers took a 103-90 lead into the fourth quarter after scoring 39 points in the third while shooting 72.7% from the floor.
The Clippers used an 8-0 run to pull within 119-113 on a 3-pointer from Garland with 3:21 to play before Grimes sealed the victory on two free throws with 40.9 seconds remaining for a 125-117 lead.
The Clippers led 31-27 after one quarter and went up by as many as 11 points less than three minutes into the second before the Lakers closed the gap. A three-point play by Doncic with 5.6 seconds remaining tied the game 64-64 at the half.
Doncic led all scorers with 16 points before the break.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Alperen Sengun, Rockets win physical battle against rival Spurs
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Alperen Sengun pounded his way to 29 points, including 14 in the fourth quarter, as the Houston Rockets ground out a 114-110 win over the San Antonio Spurs on Friday in Austin, Texas.
items.body:
Alperen Sengun pounded his way to 29 points, including 14 in the fourth quarter, as the Houston Rockets ground out a 114-110 win over the San Antonio Spurs on Friday in Austin, Texas.
The Rockets led by two at halftime and by four after three quarters. San Antonio rallied to take a 104-103 lead on Dylan Harper's 3-pointer with 4:19 remaining. Houston kept feeding Sengun, who battled inside for a layups, two free throws and a three-point play on three consecutive possessions to put the Rockets ahead 109-104.
Harper's emphatic dunk with 46.1 seconds left brought the Spurs within 112-110, and two defensive stops gave San Antonio one final chance with five seconds remaining. The Spurs went to Victor Wembanyama deep in the lane for the tying basket, but Amen Thompson blocked his layup above the rim.
Fred VanVleet grabbed the rebound for Houston with 0.6 seconds remaining and sank two free throws to seal the win, the Rockets' second straight to open the season.
Kevin Durant and Thompson added 20 points apiece for Houston, with Thompson also collecting 10 rebounds. VanVleet finished with 14 points, and Tari Eason scored 12.
Wembanyama paced the Spurs with 25 points and 13 rebounds. Harper had 20 points, De'Aaron Fox added 19 points and nine assists, Stephon Castle tallied 15 points, and Devin Vassell scored 10 for San Antonio, which has opened the season with consecutive losses.
Thompson's dunk capped a late Rockets run that gave Houston a 32-27 lead after the first quarter. Houston extended its advantage to 11 points, but the Spurs rallied to tie the game at 56 on Julian Champagnie's 3-pointer with 54.2 seconds left before halftime.
The teams then traded baskets before VanVleet sank a 3-pointer at the buzzer to give the Rockets a 61-59 lead at the break.
Wembanyama led all scorers and rebounders in the first half with 17 points and seven rebounds. Fox added 10 points. Sengun and Thompson paced Houston with 11 points apiece, while Durant scored 10.
The Rockets led by as many as 10 in the third quarter. San Antonio responded with a Champagnie 3-pointer and a pair of free throws from Vassell to pull within four heading into the fourth.
--Field Level Media

items.title: ATP roundup: Alexander Bublik survives thriller to reach Almaty semis
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Third-seeded Alexander Bublik of Kazakhstan rallied past fifth-seeded Russian Karen Khachanov 4-6, 7-6 (5), 7-6 (5) in Friday's Almaty Open quarterfinals in Kazakhstan.
items.body:
Third-seeded Alexander Bublik of Kazakhstan rallied past fifth-seeded Russian Karen Khachanov 4-6, 7-6 (5), 7-6 (5) in Friday's Almaty Open quarterfinals in Kazakhstan.
Bublik hammered 21 aces and finished with 49 winners in his first match of the tournament after advancing via a second-round walkover. Khachanov secured the only service break of the match in the opening set, but Bublik responded by winning both ensuing tiebreakers. He will face top-seeded Daniil Medvedev, who reached the semifinals with a 6-4, 6-4 victory over France's Terence Atmane. Medvedev did not face a break point and won 91% of his first-serve points.
Seventh-seeded Stefanos Tsitsipas of Greece also advanced in straight sets, defeating Australia's James Duckworth 6-3, 6-4. Tsitsipas fired 15 aces, did not face a break point and won 34 of 37 first-serve points. He will meet qualifier Nikoloz Basilashvili after the Georgian rolled past France's Adrian Mannarino 6-3, 6-1.
BNP Paribas Fortis European Open
Top-seeded Arthur Fils of France fought off fifth-seeded American Alex Michelsen 6-4, 7-6 (12) to advance to the semifinals in Brussels.
Fils needed six match points to finally close out the 14-12 second-set tiebreaker. He won 79% of his first-serve points, recorded six aces and converted three of four break chances in the one-hour, 50-minute match. He will face Germany's Jan-Lennard Struff, who ended Belgium's hopes of a home semifinalist by defeating No. 6 seed Zizou Bergs 6-3, 7-6 (6).
The Netherlands' Tallon Griekspoor rallied to eliminate No. 2 Jiri Lehecka of the Czech Republic 4-6, 6-4, 6-3. Griekspoor converted three of four break points and overcame Lehecka's 11 aces to reach his second semifinal of the season. He will play third-seeded Francisco Cerundolo after the Argentine dispatched French qualifier Clement Chidekh 6-2, 6-4.
Grand Prix Auvergne-Rhone-Alpes
Second-seeded Taylor Fritz topped Germany's Daniel Altmaier 7-6 (5), 6-2 to set up an all-American semifinal at the ATP 250 event in Lyon, France.
Fritz beat Altmaier for the first time in three career meetings. He will next face No. 4 seed Tommy Paul, who needed two hours, 45 minutes to subdue France's Corentin Moutet 6-4, 3-6, 6-3. Paul converted five of 10 break point chances and saved 10 of 14 opportunities.
Top-seeded Flavio Cobolli of Italy recovered from a set down to defeat fifth-seeded Brandon Nakashima 4-6, 6-4, 6-4. Cobolli will meet countryman Lorenzo Musetti after the No. 6 seed survived another lengthy quarterfinal, edging France's Luca Van Assche 7-6 (5), 6-7 (7), 6-4 in three hours, 33 minutes.
--Field Level Media

items.title: ソフトバンクＧ出資のオーペイ、米ＩＰＯで最大44億ドルの評価額目指す
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: ［２３日　ロイター］　 -
items.body:
［２３日　ロイター］　 - ソフトバンクグループが出資するデジタル決済企業オーペイは２３日、米国での新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）で最大４４億２０００万ドルの評価額を目指すと発表した。新興国で拡大するデジタル金融サービスの需要を取り込む狙い。

ナイジェリアを主力市場とするオーペイは、米国預託株式（ＡＤＳ）約１６００万株を１株当たり１９─２１ドルで売り出し、最大３億６６００万ドルの調達を目指す。

米ＩＰＯ市場は、インフレ率の上昇と人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株の急落で圧力にさらされている。新規上場に対する投資家の意欲が後退し、複数の企業が上場計画の延期を余儀なくされる中でのＩＰＯとなる。

オーペイは２０１８年設立。決済、送金、貯蓄、融資などのデジタル金融サービスを提供し、インドネシア、エジプト、パキスタンでも事業を展開している。

世界で６番目に人口が多いナイジェリアは、アフリカ有数のフィンテック市場に成長。調査会社トラクションによると、モニーポイント、フラッターウェーブ、インタースイッチなどのフィンテック企業を輩出している。

提出書類によると、ソフトバンク系企業は今回の売り出し前の時点でオーペイ株の６．６％を保有している。

items.title: Bolsonaro and Lula clash on living costs, corruption in final Brazil election debate
items.author: Andre Romani
items.creator: Andre Romani
items.summary: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva sparred over the cost of living and traded personal attacks on Friday in the last presidential debate before Sunday's runoff, as both candidates sought to win over undecided voters amid a tight race.
items.body:
Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro and President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva sparred over the cost of living and traded personal attacks on Friday in the last presidential debate before Sunday's runoff, as both candidates sought to win over undecided voters amid a tight race.
Bolsonaro, son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, led Lula in the first round of the election earlier this month, but opinion polls have shown the two candidates [USN:L1N4681FZ TEXT:"about even"] this week after the gap between them narrowed.
Bolsonaro and Lula repeated their campaign proposals during the over two-hour debate hosted by Globo, Brazil's most-watched TV channel, focusing on themes such as the cost of living, welfare and security, while exchanging allegations of corruption.
Lula, who is seeking his fourth term after winning back the presidency in 2022, has defended his government's above-inflation minimum wage increases and stressed that his administration helped millions of Brazilians to escape hunger.
The president said the younger Bolsonaro "is like students studying for college entrance exams. They can memorize things, but they can't learn." He also said that "in the gated community where Bolsonaro lives, people don't go hungry."
Bolsonaro responded by saying food prices for Brazilians rose during Lula's administration, and he criticized a tax reform approved by the current government, projecting the new rules would raise the tax burden on consumers.
"Lula doesn't even remember the last time he went grocery shopping because he lives in a luxury palace now."
The two candidates mostly limited the discussion to pre-established themes in the first few segments of the debate, toning down the [USN:L6N46406G TEXT:"personal attacks"] that marked the only previous debate in the campaign between the two.
At one point, Bolsonaro apologized to Lula after saying the president gives to Brazilians with one hand but "takes away with nine fingers." Lula lost his left little finger in an accident while working as a lathe operator in a factory.
"I will not accept some rich guy, with a highly questionable political practice, calling me 'nine fingers,'" the incumbent said, demanding a retraction.
"Lula, if I offended you by calling you 'nine fingers,' then I sincerely apologize, I sincerely apologize," Bolsonaro said. But he added: "Will you apologize to Brazilians suffering from insecurity ... in debt?"
The discussion heated up in the last minutes of the debate, when both candidates were allowed to interact without moderation, as Lula and Bolsonaro sought to link each other to the fraud involving lender Banco Master.
Lula pressed Bolsonaro on [USN:L1N4530F5 TEXT:"alleged links"] to the bank's jailed banker Daniel Vorcaro, and Bolsonaro questioned Lula [USN:L1N43X02G TEXT:"about accusations"] involving his son and a pension fraud.
The debate was one of the campaign's final events, as Brazilian electoral law bars the candidates from broadcasting radio and TV campaign advertising starting on Saturday. They can still hold rallies until the final hours of the day.

items.title: Saudi Arabia Expands Missile Factory Using Suspected Chinese Technology
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two U.S. researchers who analyzed more than a year of commercial satellite images. More capable missiles could help Saudi Arabia …
items.summary_source: The China-Global South Project source metadata
items.body:
Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two U.S. researchers who analyzed more than a year of commercial satellite images.

More capable missiles could help Saudi Arabia to deter attacks by Iran and make its military more self-reliant, while possibly strengthening its position in a deadly conflict with Yemen’s Tehran-backed Houthi fighters.

But they risk fueling a regional missile race and could deepen opposition in the U.S. Congress to a U.S.-Saudi civilian nuclear agreement that has already raised concerns about proliferation.

Satellite company Planet Labs, based in the U.S., took images of the al-Duwadimi complex about 125 miles (200 km) west of Riyadh between April 2025 and September 2026.

The two researchers, Sam Lair and Michael Duitsman of the Foreign Policy Research Institute, assessed that those images show a new building that houses casting pits — wells in which a mixture of fuel ingredients is poured into missile motor casings and allowed to harden.

The Saudi embassy and Information Ministry did not respond to requests for comment.

The building, flanked by what appear to be walls to protect nearby structures from accidental explosions, is at least twice as large as the one believed to house the plant’s existing casting pits, Lair and Duitsman said in their assessment. The Foreign Policy Research Institute (FPRI) is a non-partisan research organization in Philadelphia.

They said a second new building could store fuel ingredients or finished missile components.

The imagery “suggests that Saudi Arabia is expanding the infrastructure at the missile production complex, likely to produce larger missiles which could deliver larger payloads or reach longer ranges,” they wrote.

Militaries favor solid-fuel missiles because they can be stored for long periods and launched more quickly than liquid-fuel systems.

Lair and Duitsman and experts from the London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) and the CNA research and analysis organization told Reuters that the makeup of Saudi Arabia’s missile force suggests that the al-Duwadimi complex relies on Chinese technology. Lair and Duitsman said that its characteristics also are similar to Chinese missile plants.

Saudi Arabia secretly acquired about 40 liquid-fuel DF-3 ballistic missiles from China in 1987, according to a 1991 declassified CIA estimate. It displayed two of them for the first time in an April 2014 military parade, according to a YouTube video and photographs of the event.

The FPRI team also recently identified from social media videos and photos what they assessed was the wreckage in Yemen of a Saudi-fired Chinese-designed DF-15 missile.

Lair said the kingdom may now be producing the solid-fuel DF-15, and that the expansion of a1-Dumadimi is likely for the production of the longer-range DF-21 or a similar missile.

Riyadh is believed to have turned to Beijing because Washington has long restricted exports of longer-range missile systems.

The Chinese embassy and defense ministry did not respond to requests for comment. The CIA declined to comment. The White House did not respond to a request for comment.

Missiles Would Alter the Balance of Power

Sascha Bruchmann, a research fellow at IISS, said longer-range missiles would allow Saudi Arabia to strike Iran without risking its U.S.-supplied F-15 jet fighters against Iranian air defenses.

“You’d want a system to threaten whatever is holy to Tehran … if you don’t have the political will to send an F-15 with JDAMs over Tehran,” said Bruchmann, referring to U.S.-made satellite-guided bombs. “Iran has a lead because its missiles and drones can strike Saudi wherever it wants. The Saudis could close that capability gap a bit.”

Bruchmann, who reviewed the FPRI analysis at Reuters request, concurred that the expansion of al-Duwadimi could be for producing more powerful solid-fuel missiles.

Janes, the defense intelligence company, also reviewed it and said the buildings “may suggest an effort to expand production capability or support the development of longer-range missiles.”

Saudi Arabia’s apparent pursuit of more powerful missiles comes as other Gulf powers are also seeking to expand their offensive and defensive arsenals, said Decker Eveleth, a CNA analyst who has been tracking the al-Duwadimi construction with commercial satellite imagery and concurred with the FPRI assessment.

“This is being replicated across the Middle East,” he said. “You see exactly the same thing happening in the UAE. You see the exact same thing happening in Turkey. Everybody is doing this now.”

The expansion of al-Duwadimi could have political consequences in the U.S. by stiffening bipartisan congressional opposition to a U.S.-Saudi agreement under which the U.S. would help Riyadh establish uranium enrichment for power generation.

Opponents say that the deal lacks sufficient safeguards to prevent Riyadh from secretly building a nuclear weapon. The kingdom has denied any such plan.

Work Began Last Year

The FPRI assessment said the Planet Labs imagery showed that the expansion at al-Duwadimi began in April 2025 with ground-clearing and digging for the suspected storage building. Work on the suspected casting-pit building began later that month or in early May, it said.

A December 12, 2025, photo showed what researchers assessed were two deep pits inside the building that had no roof yet.

A September 18, 2026, photo shows the roof still partly missing and “heavy-duty blast-diverting walls” on either side to prevent accidental explosions from damaging adjacent structures.

The walls, the researchers said, are somewhat similar to those depicted in imagery of U.S. and Iranian missile plants and “further evidence the building is for casting solid propellant motors.”

Finishing the roofs would not take long, the FPRI said, but installing casting equipment may take several months. The facility could be ready to start producing missiles as early as the end of the year.

items.title: Jaren Jackson Jr., Jazz eke out home-opening win over Pelicans
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Jaren Jackson Jr. logged 24 points and 10 rebounds and Keyonte George added 19 points and 10 assists to rally the Utah Jazz to a 120-119 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday in Salt Lake City.
items.body:
Jaren Jackson Jr. logged 24 points and 10 rebounds and Keyonte George added 19 points and 10 assists to rally the Utah Jazz to a 120-119 victory over the New Orleans Pelicans on Friday in Salt Lake City.
Utah rookie Darryn Peterson scored 15 points, including two go-ahead free throws with 50.5 seconds left.
Jaxson Hayes chipped in 17 points off the bench and Lauri Markkanen added 16 to help the Jazz beat the Pelicans for the first time since November 2023. New Orleans went 3-0 against Utah each of the previous two seasons and had won eight straight in the series.
The Jazz earned the home-opening victory after dropping their overall opener on Wednesday at Memphis.
Zion Williamson led the Pelicans with 23 points and reserve Saddiq Bey added 20. Dejounte Murray chipped in 16.
Murray missed a potential game-winning jumper with a second left as the Pelicans fell to 0-2.
New Orleans center Yves Missi went to the locker room with 6:24 left in the second quarter after sustaining a left knee injury. Missi could not put any weight on his left leg as he was helped off the court. He tallied six points on 3-of-3 shooting in nine minutes.
Even without Missi, New Orleans erased a 15-point deficit in the third quarter and took its first lead at 75-74 midway through the quarter on a reverse layup from Murray. The Pelicans scored on 10 consecutive possessions during the rally. Murray accounted for five baskets in that stretch.
The Pelicans scored 38 points in the third quarter and carried that momentum into the fourth. Back-to-back baskets from Bennedict Mathurin and Bey helped New Orleans build its largest lead at 99-94.
George drained a 3-pointer and fed Hayes for a floater, capping a 15-3 run that put the Jazz back in front 109-102 with 5:35 left.
Utah dominated in the paint early to assert control. The Jazz scored 22 of their 31 first-quarter points in the paint.
The Jazz never trailed before halftime and claimed a 40-30 lead early in the second quarter behind a 9-0 run. Markkanen and Brice Sensabaugh bookended the surge with 3-pointers.
Utah eventually expanded its lead to 67-52 early in the third on another trey from Markkanen.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Marquez wins thrilling Australian MotoGP sprint to retake championship lead
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Ducati's Marc Marquez emerged victorious in an electrifying battle with championship rival Jorge Martin before going on to win the Australian Grand Prix sprint from pole position on Saturday and reclaim the MotoGP championship lead.
items.body:
Ducati's Marc Marquez emerged victorious in an electrifying battle with championship rival Jorge Martin before going on to win the Australian Grand Prix sprint from pole position on Saturday and reclaim the MotoGP championship lead.
Victory moved seven-times MotoGP champion Marquez up to 365 points in the championship standings, 10 points ahead of Martin, who did not finish the sprint after suffering a gruesome crash in the eighth lap.
The reigning champion can further extend that lead in Sunday's race, with Martin declared unfit after breaking his wrist in the crash.
After a couple of [USN:L4N4691TI TEXT:"wet qualifying sessions"] earlier in the day, the sprint began on a dry track at the Phillip Island Grand Prix Circuit, with dark clouds looming overhead.
Pole-sitter Marquez shot off the line and held on to his lead, though his start was matched by title rival Martin, who barrelled past Alex Marquez and Johann Zarco into second place from fourth.
Without the rain to hinder him, Martin squeezed every ounce of pace he could out of his Aprilia on the circuit's swooping corners and stole the lead from Marquez three times, only to overplay his hand and quickly give it away on every occasion.
The 2024 champion continued to push, and his overzealousness proved to be his undoing in the eighth lap, as his bike slid out from under him and he went hurtling into the gravel at high speed.
"It was a title battle. Of course I gave everything. I was aggressive and he was faster than me, but I tried to defend in the best way possible," Marquez said after his win.
"There were nice overtakes, limit overtakes. And in the end, both of us were riding on the limit. Both of us deserved the victory because we are pushing a lot. But, you know, racing is like it is.
"Today, it was on my side, but, this (season) is super long, so, keep calm, keep going, and yeah, happy for today."
MARTIN TO MISS RACE Martin was carried away from the site of the crash on a stretcher as Aprilia confirmed that he had been taken to the medical centre for evaluation.
The Spaniard was later pictured walking out of the medical centre with his arm in a sling and his wrist wrapped up tightly.
"Jorge Martin has been declared unfit to race after suffering a fracture to his right wrist! Wishing Jorge a speedy recovery," MotoGP said in a statement on social media.
Martin will also be a doubt for next week's Malaysian Grand Prix.
Trackhouse Aprilia rider Raul Fernandez, who won the Australian Grand Prix in 2025, was also ruled out of Sunday's race due to inflammation of tissue around a finger fracture that he sustained at the [USN:L1N45X01G TEXT:"Indonesian Grand Prix"] this month.
"It’s not how I wanted to say goodbye to Phillip Island, but my finger has said it’s enough. I need to take a break and recover so I can come back at 100%," Fernandez said on social media.
Marquez's brother Alex of Gresini Racing finished second, with Fabio Di Giannantonio (VR46 Racing) completing the podium.
"It was quite dramatic. For me, I had the best seat, sitting in the third place (behind Marc Marquez and Martin)," Alex said.
Martin's teammate Marco Bezzecchi finished in fourth place, keeping his outside shot at winning the title alive.
Home hero Jack Miller of Pramac Racing was eighth in the final sprint [USN:L6N46607H TEXT:"at Phillip Island,"] with the Australian Grand Prix moving to the streets of Adelaide next year.

items.title: Moonshot curbs hacking ability in new Kimi model as fears grow over AI-powered cyberattacks
items.author: Eduardo Baptista
items.creator: Eduardo Baptista
items.summary: Moonshot AI has reduced the cyber-offensive capabilities of its newest model, the Chinese startup said on Saturday, as fears grow that increasingly autonomous AI could turbocharge hacking.
items.body:
Moonshot AI has reduced the cyber-offensive capabilities of its newest model, the Chinese startup said on Saturday, as fears grow that increasingly autonomous AI could turbocharge hacking.
Beijing-based Moonshot announced the curbs while introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro, which it describes as its most capable 3-trillion-parameter-class open-weight model. The company plans to publish the model's weights — files allowing outside developers to run and modify it on their own systems — by November 4.
Moonshot said it removed cyber-related data from the training corpus and reinforcement-learning environments used to develop the model, while retaining general coding skills.
"We aim not to release open weights that would extend the absolute frontier of cyber capability," the company said.
Governments, technology companies and security researchers are growing increasingly concerned that AI could make sophisticated hacking easier and cheaper. Models that can write code, operate software tools and complete long, multi-step tasks may help users identify weaknesses in programs and automate parts of cyberattacks.
China [USN:L1N46209C TEXT:"proposed export controls"] last week that would ban exports of AI-driven malware-generation and mutation technology and restrict AI-assisted vulnerability-discovery tools. The draft measures, which remain open for public comment, cite the risk that such capabilities could be used against critical infrastructure, defence-industrial and core government systems, or to bypass security protections.
Moonshot said open-weight models can improve security by helping more organisations inspect and secure their own software, including older systems that receive little attention.
Unlike proprietary, closed-weight AI systems, however, open-weight releases make central oversight more difficult. Once the files are widely distributed, the original developer has less ability to restrict access, monitor use or update safeguards than with a hosted service.
K3.1 Pro scored 81.0% on its internal cyber benchmark, compared with 90.5% for a similar version without the risk-reduction measures, the company said. The test involved finding and exploiting software vulnerabilities in a controlled environment. Moonshot said the comparison showed that filtering cyber-related data reduced the model's offensive cyber performance, although it still outperformed its predecessor. The results have not been independently verified.
K3.1 Pro has a 1-million-token context window, allowing it to process very large amounts of text at once. Moonshot also released a faster version, K3.1 Pro Highspeed, which it said runs at two to three times the speed of the standard model.

items.title: Nathan MacKinnon's 4-point night powers Avs past Lightning
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists, Mackenzie Blackwood turned away 31 shots, and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-3 in Denver on Friday night.
items.body:
Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and three assists, Mackenzie Blackwood turned away 31 shots, and the Colorado Avalanche beat the Tampa Bay Lightning 6-3 in Denver on Friday night.
Martin Necas had a goal and two assists, Artturi Lehkonen and Devon Toews each collected a goal and an assist, and Nazem Kadri and Fedor Svechkov also scored for Colorado, which snapped a two-game skid.
Jake Guentzel scored twice, Charle-Edouard D'Astous added a goal and an assist, Brayden Point had two assists, and Andrei Vasilevskiy made 18 saves for Tampa Bay, which had its three-game winning streak snapped.
Toews gave Colorado the early lead when Necas fed him with a cross-ice pass, and he beat Vasilevskiy with a wrist shot 1:08 after the opening faceoff. Kadri made it 2-0 on the power play at 5:52 of the first period, taking a pass from T.J. Hughes in the slot and scoring with a snap shot.
The Avalanche extended their lead to 3-0 just 24 seconds into the second period when Svechkov's pass attempt in front of the net deflected off a sprawling Erik Cernak. Svechkov then tapped the puck out of the air and into the net.
The Lightning got on the board during one of their five power-play opportunities in the second period when Guentzel scored on a rebound at 8:13. Lehkonen made it 4-1 at 13:57, converting a centering pass from MacKinnon.
Tampa Bay answered at the end of another power play when Guentzel stuffed home a pass from Point at 19:17 of the second period. Colorado unsuccessfully challenged the play for a missed stoppage, giving the Lightning another power play.
MacKinnon restored Colorado's three-goal lead at 4:18 of the third period. He took a pass from Lehkonen in the neutral zone, skated in on Vasilevskiy and buried a shot inside the near post.
D'Astous cut the deficit to 5-3 at 15:13. Vasilevskiy came off for an extra attacker with less than three minutes remaining, and Necas scored into the empty net seconds later.
Avalanche forward Logan O'Connor made his season debut, recording three shots in nearly 15 minutes of ice time.
--Field Level Media

items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: MILWAUKEE -- Brewers closer Trevor Megill wasn't perfect, but he was good enough to give Milwaukee a one-game advantage in the World Series.
items.body:
MILWAUKEE -- Brewers closer Trevor Megill wasn't perfect, but he was good enough to give Milwaukee a one-game advantage in the World Series.
Hard-throwing ace Jacob Misiorowski allowed one run over five gritty innings and Megill stranded the tying run at third base to preserve the Brewers' 3-2 victory over the Tampa Bay Rays on Friday night in the opening game of the World Series.
Milwaukee, whose only other World Series appearance was a seven-game loss in 1982, scored two runs in the first inning off Nick Martinez and added a run in the seventh on Jackson Chourio's RBI single to go up 3-1.
The Rays scored one run in the ninth off Megill, who entered to start the inning and conceded consecutive one-out singles to Jonathan Aranda and Chandler Simpson. Pinch runner Jorge Mateo and Simpson executed a double steal, and Junior Caminero walked to load the bases.
Liam Hicks appeared to bounce into a game-ending double play, but a video review showed that shortstop Cooper Pratt was pulled off the bag at second on the throw by second baseman Brice Turang.
Hicks was out on the fielder's choice as Mateo scored to make it 3-2, leaving runners on second and third. Megill then struck out Jonny DeLuca for his fifth postseason save in five opportunities.
"A lot of times those plays stand during the year, but I'm sure now they have every angle, and they took their time and got it right." Brewers manager Pat Murphy said of the review. "Megill kept his composure. We talk about it all the time. When there's a challenge, do not walk off the mound. Kept his composure, and that was the biggest at-bat of the game."
Misiorowski (1-0), whose 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts each led the majors during the regular season, allowed one run on four hits in five innings. He fanned three and walked one in a 78-pitch outing.
Misiorowski set the tone by throwing a 103.5 mph fastball to open the game, the fastest pitch in World Series history.
"I thought Miz was great tonight," Murphy said. "What we're used to seeing in the regular season was Miz just mow through people and have two strikeouts an inning. That's unrealistic. This is the best team in the American League. They proved that during the regular season and proved that in the postseason so far. One of the ways they do that is to make contact better than anybody in baseball."
Afterward, the 24-year-old Milwaukee ace was trying to process his first World Series appearance.
"I still don't know how I felt. I feel like I'm still trying to take everything in and understand what happened," Misiorowski said. "Obviously went out and did my best and did enough for the team to get a win. That's all I can ask for."
After Misiorowski's exit, Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby combined for three scoreless innings, striking out five.
"We came up a little bit short, but there's some benefit maybe from a loss," Rays manager Kevin Cash said. "We saw Ashby. We saw Uribe. We saw Megill. I'd like to think that's going to help us moving forward a little bit."
The Brewers posted two quick runs against Martinez (1-1), who got the start when ace Drew Rasmussen was pushed back to Game 2 for an extra day's rest.
Chourio singled on the first pitch and scored on Christian Yelich's one-out triple off DeLuca's glove on a diving catch attempt in right-center. William Contreras followed with an RBI single to left.
The Rays got a run back in the fourth. Aranda drew a leadoff walk and advanced to third when center fielder Garrett Mitchell misplayed Caminero's 112.7 mph drive into a double. He scored on Hicks' groundout.
The Brewers made it 3-1 in the seventh. Steven Matz walked Pratt, who advanced on a groundout and scored on Chourio's two-out single down the right field line against Kevin Kelly.
Martinez allowed two runs on five hits in five innings, striking out five and walking none.
--Jim Hoehn, Field Level Media

Taiwan counts 1 dead and 527 injured after Typhoon Champi sweeps past

Once a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi has weakened but continues to pack wind gusts of around 126 kilometres per hour near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration.

YILAN: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday (Oct 24), killing 1 person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continued to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast though it was not expected to make landfall there.
At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi is weakening though still packing gusts of around 126 kilometres per hour (kmh) near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA).

Typhoon Champi swirls over the Philippine Sea, as seen from space on Oct 23, 2026 in this screengrab taken from a handout GIF image. (Photo: Reuters/CSU/CIRA)

The storm was about 150km east of Taiwan, having glanced off the island's northeastern coast in Yilan County early on Saturday, the CWA said.
The centre of the storm turned south around midnight, hugging the Yilan coastline before making a rare loop offshore and moving northward away, triggering gusts of about 227kmh in some coastal areas, knocking down power lines and sending roof tiles flying.

"It was most terrifying around midnight," said a retired teacher surnamed Lin as he inspected downed banana trees in his garden in Yilan. "It was a sleepless night. I haven't seen anything like this in many years."

The storm's forecast track shows it turning north, tracking up the Chinese coast and eventually moving into southern Japan.
Taiwan's fire department said the death toll remained at one, a man swept away by waves from the island of Liuqiu, with 527 injuries during the heavy wind and torrential rain.
Taipower said at one point more than 288,000 homes had lost electricity, though most had been reconnected.
The transport ministry said 242 flights were cancelled, an improvement from Friday, when the number was almost 1,000.
In the capital Taipei, there were downed trees and on-off squally rain showers.

An uprooted tree after strong winds brought by Typhoon Champi, in Taipei, Taiwan Oct 24, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Ann Wang)

A swathe of northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, declared a second day of office and school closures on Saturday.
Taiwan is generally well prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn too.
China's emergency management ministry sent a team to the eastern province of Zhejiang as Champi approached, warning of strong winds and heavy rain through Sunday. It said 400 rescue workers and 600 pieces of equipment had been readied, while more than 41,000 firefighters were on emergency duty.
In Taizhou, a city on Zhejiang's coast, more than 3,800 fishing boats returned to harbour, offshore fish-farm workers were brought ashore and 2,084 island visitors were evacuated, state media reported.
Authorities halted 25 offshore construction projects and suspended 18 passenger ferry routes.

items.title: Mavericks awaiting update on star Cooper Flagg (shoulder)
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The prognosis for Dallas forward Cooper Flagg, who exited the Mavericks' Friday game against the Indiana Pacers in Indianapolis due to left shoulder soreness, was unclear following the contest.
items.body:
The prognosis for Dallas forward Cooper Flagg, who exited the Mavericks' Friday game against the Indiana Pacers in Indianapolis due to left shoulder soreness, was unclear following the contest.
"He'll be evaluated in the next couple of days," Mavericks coach Dusty May said.
As for whether Flagg would require an MRI, May added, "I really don't know. I saw him in the locker room, he's in good spirits. We'll know in the next couple days what's next."
Flagg, the reigning NBA Rookie of the Year, took a hard foul late in the second quarter and did not return to action.
With 59.7 seconds left in the first half, Indiana's Aaron Nesmith challenged Flagg's dunk attempt from behind, sending Flagg sprawling to the floor. After a review, Nesmith was assessed a flagrant-1 foul.
Naji Marshall rushed in and shoved Nesmith, resulting in technical fouls for both players. Dallas carried a 77-43 lead into the locker room.
"Nesmith's a great guy," May said following the Mavericks' 121-105 win. "Heck of a player. I've known him since he was in high school. An unfortunate play. Hopefully Coop's fine, but obviously it's something we wish wouldn't have happened."
Flagg notched 14 points, six assists and five rebounds in 17 minutes of first-half play before being ruled out.
The 19-year-old registered 32 points and five rebounds in the Mavericks' season-opening loss to the Houston Rockets. He averaged 21.0 points, 6.7 rebounds and 4.5 assists in 70 games last season.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Suspect arrested as fire engulfs Nazi guest house 'Eagle's Nest', German police say
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: German police said they had detained a suspect after fire broke out at a historic mountain guest house known as the "Eagle's Nest", used as a retreat by Nazi officials, including the dictator Adolf Hitler.
items.body:
German police said they had detained a suspect after fire broke out at a historic mountain guest house known as the "Eagle's Nest", used as a retreat by Nazi officials, including the dictator Adolf Hitler.
Around 200 firefighters and emergency personnel in the area around Berchtesgaden in the southern region of Bavaria were battling the flames after the building, known as the Kehlsteinhaus, caught fire on Friday, police said.
Police are investigating whether the suspect, who was detained close to the scene, was connected to the fire, they said in a statement.
There was no immediate word about a possible motive.
Built in 1938 as a guest house for Nazi officials and their guests, the building, in a spectacular Alpine setting, is separate from Hitler's nearby summer residence, known as the Berghof.
Now owned by the state of Bavaria, the Kehlsteinhaus was classified after the war as a historical monument recalling the Nazi period.

items.title: OpenAI resumes training AI, blocks internet access over security risks
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: The company said it would keep its most advanced models offline during training until safeguards are adequate, following incidents in which AI systems accessed the web and breached external systems ...
items.body: By Rachel Metz OpenAI has begun cutting off internet access for its most capable artificial intelligence models during the training process in response to prior incidents in which its systems breached other companies. The company said in a blog post Friday that, after a pause last month, it had resumed training its most advanced models but intends to block internet access until it feels it has adequate safeguards in place to mitigate the risk of unreleased models being able to take unapproved actions online during training.  “Based on the current state of alignment research, monitoring systems, and the security of internet infrastructure, we believe the responsible approach is to conduct frontier model training with no internet access,” the company wrote. In late September, the company said it would pause training its most advanced AI models after it discovered that one of its AI agent systems that was being trained in what was supposed to be a secured, internet-free environment was able to gain access to the web to reach an external, third-party chatbot. At the time, OpenAI described the breakout as the first security incident of its kind since a combination of models gained internet access during internal testing and inadvertently breached the system of the AI platform Hugging Face in July.  The models involved in the inadvertent Hugging Face breach were operating without the usual safety guardrails, the company has said, because OpenAI had intended them to remain in a testing area known as a “sandbox” — essentially, an isolated virtual software environment that’s meant to run security tests or analyse unsafe code in a controlled way. The models were able to break out of that sandbox, however, by leveraging a software vulnerability to access the open internet. OpenAI said that after the Hugging Face incident, it reduced the connections through which its models might be able to reach the internet during training and testing but kept some for the purpose of metrics, logging and authentication. It also spent a vast amount of computing power on tasking agentic AI systems with identifying vulnerabilities in its training environments as part of a red-teaming effort, a phrase typically used to describe deliberate attempts to break into systems to uncover vulnerabilities before real attackers can. “Our red-teaming agents found vulnerabilities in almost every one of these services that gave them limited forms of internet access,” the firm said in its post. The company said it has since deployed software patches, imposed tighter network restrictions and disclosed the findings to vendors. There have been a series of disclosures in recent months from OpenAI and rivals including Anthropic PBC about incidents in which their models carried out self-directed attacks or unsanctioned actions on third-party websites and systems.  These cases, and a series of stark warnings from within the industry, have vaulted the safety debate into the mainstream. AI developers have warned that their systems could soon become too sophisticated for people to control, adding to concerns the technology could be used by malicious human actors to create bioweapons or carry out devastating cyberattacks.

items.title: Jake Evans tallies twice, adds assist as Canadiens topple Blackhawks
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Jake Evans produced two goals and an assist and Jacob Fowler stopped 20 shots, lifting the visiting Montreal Canadiens to a 4-1 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Friday.
items.body:
Jake Evans produced two goals and an assist and Jacob Fowler stopped 20 shots, lifting the visiting Montreal Canadiens to a 4-1 victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Friday.
Kaiden Guhle added a goal and assist to help Montreal earn its first road victory since opening night. Mike Matheson also scored as the Canadiens improved to 4-1-1 in their past six games.
Connor Bedard scored and Spencer Knight made 24 saves as the Blackhawks fell to 2-3-0 on a seven-game homestand.
Chicago started strong, as Bedard opened the scoring at 4:23 of the first period on a snap shot from just outside the left circle. After a Montreal dump-in glanced off a linesman, Patrick Kane collected the puck and slid it to a streaking Bedard in the neutral zone for his second goal this season.
Montreal, playing without captain and top center Nick Suzuki (upper body), struggled to find offensive footing in the early going. The Canadiens needed 3:31 to record their first shot on goal and didn't register another for another 2 1/2 minutes.
Evans tallied the equalizer at 17:29 of the first period with his first goal of the season, beating Knight with a wrist shot from in front of the net off a feed from Kirby Dach.
Montreal took the lead on Evans' short-handed goal at 7:45 of the second period. With the Canadiens pressuring the Blackhawks' five-forward power play, a Kane shot attempt redirected off Tyler Bertuzzi's skate and created an odd-man rush for Montreal.
Evans carried the puck down the left side and scored from the circle.
Fowler turned aside Roman Kantserov and Kane on a Chicago rush moments later to preserve a one-goal advantage.
The Canadiens made it 3-1 at 18:26 of the second. Guhle netted his first goal of the season on a wrist shot from the point.
Chicago finished 0-for-5 on the power play compared to 0-for-3 for Montreal. The Blackhawks' final man advantage of the game lasted just 22 seconds in the third period, as Teuvo Teravainen was whistled for interference moments after Montreal's Juraj Slafkovsky was penalized for hooking.
Matheson's empty-net goal, his first tally of the season, at 17:22 accounted for the final margin.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Kraken aim to stay hot against road-weary Wild
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Seattle Kraken will try to extend their winning streak to three games Saturday when they host the Minnesota Wild, who have lost the first two games of a five-game road trip.
items.body:
The Seattle Kraken will try to extend their winning streak to three games Saturday when they host the Minnesota Wild, who have lost the first two games of a five-game road trip.
Minnesota fell 4-3 in a shootout Tuesday at Edmonton and 2-1 Thursday at Calgary, dropping to 0-1-1 on its road trip. The Wild visit Vancouver on Sunday and Utah on Tuesday to complete the trip.
"That's two games in a row we lost the special teams battle and it cost us," said Wild forward Blake Coleman, who was in the penalty box for Calgary's first goal. "You've got guys sitting on the bench that need to be on the ice. Three penalties in a row in the first period is not the recipe and I'm certainly part of that. I'll clean it up. I know we all will and we'll go from there."
Michael McCarron scored the lone goal for Minnesota in the third period and goalie Jesper Wallstedt made 20 saves.
"We battled back and gave ourselves a chance, but ultimately, it wasn't good enough," Minnesota coach John Hynes said.
Kirill Kaprizov, the Wild's leading scorer with 17 points in 11 games (11 goals, six assists), saw his seven-game point streak (eight goals, six assists) and four-game goal streak snapped.
Minnesota defensemen Jared Spurgeon and Olli Maatta returned Thursday after missing four and three games, respectively, with upper-body injuries. Forward Maxim Shabanov (upper body) was a late scratch and Hynes said he's day-to-day.
"If you give up two goals and you're trying to chase the whole game, it's tough playing that way," Maatta said. "Kudos to them for defending hard, but also I think we got our chances and that just showed the way we've got to play the full 60."
The Wild will face a surging Seattle squad that's 5-1-1 over its past seven games, including a 5-3 win over Utah on Thursday, with Mackie Samoskevich scoring the tiebreaking goal at 14:35 of the third period and goaltender Philipp Grubauer making 33 saves.
Jordan Eberle and Brandon Montour had a goal and an assist apiece and Matty Beniers and Frederick Gaudreau also tallied for the Kraken, who are 2-0-0 on their four-game homestand that wraps up next Wednesday against Toronto.
It was the second straight game Seattle overcame a blown multi-goal third-period lead. The Kraken surrendered a 3-1 advantage against Utah after allowing Detroit to erase a 3-0 deficit Tuesday before winning 4-3 in a shootout.
"If you want to look at it from a positive standpoint, we're getting into a position where we're able to give up a multi-goal lead and still win," Kraken coach Lane Lambert said. "We've got to continue to play the game the same way that got us the lead, and that comes with a little bit of experience, a little bit of time. What it says about our team's resilience in these situations, it says a lot."
Beniers wasn't as sympathetic.
"We got to learn from it," the forward said. "We have to get better playing with leads and shutting teams down and not letting them push back."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Pistons jump out to big lead, hand Heat second straight loss
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: John Collins scored 23 points and grabbed seven rebounds, and Paul Reed finished with 19 points and 11 rebounds to lead the Detroit Pistons to a 128-111 victory over the host Miami Heat on Friday night.
items.body:
John Collins scored 23 points and grabbed seven rebounds, and Paul Reed finished with 19 points and 11 rebounds to lead the Detroit Pistons to a 128-111 victory over the host Miami Heat on Friday night.
The Pistons (2-0) led wire to wire after scoring the game's first 11 points and built a lead of as many as 23 in the third quarter.
The Heat (0-2) never got closer than eight points after Detroit's early surge despite another strong outing from Giannis Antetokounmpo. Antetokounmpo scored a game-high 36 points, grabbed 12 rebounds and dished out five assists for his first double-double in a Miami uniform.
Collins, who shot 5-of-6 from 3-point range, helped Detroit build a 22-5 lead and spearheaded a 47.4% effort from beyond the arc (18-of-38). The Pistons shot 52.8% from the field (47-of-89), with former Heat guard Duncan Robinson making five of 10 3-point attempts and finishing with 17 points.
It was another subpar defensive effort for Miami, which allowed 21 3-pointers and 131 points in its season-opening loss to Minnesota on Wednesday.
The Heat were hampered in the first half when Bam Adebayo picked up three fouls in the first quarter and sat with 1:13 remaining. Adebayo did not return until the start of the second half. He finished with just four points, six rebounds, three assists and two steals before fouling out.
Detroit's Cade Cunningham committed seven turnovers but finished with 16 points and eight assists. Daniss Jenkins scored 15 points, while Isaiah Joe chipped in 12.
Miami made 15 3-pointers but shot just 29.4% from long range on 51 attempts. Davion Mitchell totaled 18 points and five rebounds, while Bobby Portis Jr. had 11 points and eight rebounds. The Heat shot just 38.2% from the field.
Pistons center Jalen Duren left with 6:45 remaining in the second quarter due to a right thigh injury and did not return. He finished with four points and six rebounds in 10 minutes.
--Field Level Media

items.title: US accuses government contractor of leaking classified info to girlfriend's Substack
items.author: Daniel Trotta
items.creator: Daniel Trotta
items.summary: The US Justice Department accused a government contractor on Friday of leaking national defense information to his girlfriend, the publisher of a Substack newsletter.
items.body:
The US Justice Department accused a government contractor on Friday of leaking national defense information to his girlfriend, the publisher of a Substack newsletter.
The FBI arrested Ian Brinksman, 42, on Friday following a search of his Washington home, a Justice Department statement said. Prosecutors charged him with unlawfully transmitting national defense information.
A federal public defender representing Brinksman declined to comment.
“As alleged, Brinksman reached far outside his own duties to obtain some of our Nation’s most closely held secrets and handed them to a romantic partner he knew intended to publish them,” John Eisenberg, assistant attorney general for national security, said in the statement.
“That is not carelessness. It is a betrayal of his oath and the American people who entrusted him to fulfill his duties honorably,” Eisenberg said.
Brinksman held a top secret security clearance while working as an employee of a US government agency and later as a developer for systems integration for a private contractor working for the same agency, prosecutors said.
According to the sworn affidavit of an FBI agent investigating the case, Brinksman repeatedly accessed classified intelligence reports and then communicated with the journalist. The affidavit also cites phone records, database access logs, badge-swipe records, emails and other evidence.
The affidavit only identifies the journalist as "Individual 1," but it cites excerpts from articles she published.
"A fundraising article reportedly published by Individual 1 in September 2026 stated 'over the past year [Individual 1 has] published reporting based on classified [relevant U.S. government agency] assessments that I believe the public deserves to know about,'" the affidavit reads.
That quote appears in a September 28 piece published on the Capital & Empire online newsletter authored by Aída Chávez.
"Over the past year, I’ve published reporting based on classified CIA assessments that I believe the public deserves to know about," wrote Chávez, whose profile on the site notes that she worked for The Nation and other outlets before she launched the newsletter.
Chávez did not immediately respond to an email message seeking comment.
Investigators allege that on at least five occasions in 2026, Individual 1 published Substack articles containing information that mirrored the classified reports, some at the top secret level. On some of those dates, Chávez published articles that cite classified reports, some of them attributed to the CIA.
According to a LinkedIn profile bearing Brinksman's name, he worked for Deloitte as a manager and as a senior strategy security consultant after having worked as a US State Department foreign service officer at dates corresponding to those outlined in the Justice Department statement.
Deloitte did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The State Department said it needed more time to respond before commenting.

items.title: Red Wings look to extend dominance over Flames
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Two teams battling to stay in the win column square off in Calgary as the Flames host the Detroit Red Wings on Saturday.
items.body:
Two teams battling to stay in the win column square off in Calgary as the Flames host the Detroit Red Wings on Saturday.
This is the first of two meetings between these teams this season. Detroit has won eight straight in the overall series dating back to the 2022-23 season.
The Red Wings appear to have righted the ship after a lackluster start, winning three of their last four games. They played a consistent game to win 2-1 against the lowly Philadelphia Flyers, rallied late for a 4-3 shootout victory against the San Jose Sharks, and most recently secured an early lead in a 5-2 win against the Vancouver Canucks.
On Thursday in Vancouver, Lucas Raymond scored twice in the first period to give Detroit a 3-1 lead.
"He put himself in good spots tonight to score," Red Wings head coach Todd McLellan said. "I thought he did that last game. Even when he mishandled the puck a couple times three or four games ago, he was in the right spot. So now he's feeling good, the confidence is back where it should be, and hopefully he takes off."
William Wallinder and Michael Rasmussen also scored. John Gibson stopped four of five shots over two periods but did not return for the third due to an apparent eye issue, according to McLellan. Michal Postava, recalled from the AHL earlier that day, made seven saves in his NHL debut.
"It's crazy," Postava said. "I think it's for me the best option. I don't have time to think about anything, so yeah, I just warm up and be ready."
The Flames have also won three of their last four, after starting their 2026-27 campaign with five straight losses. They rallied in the third period to secure a 4-2 win over the Anaheim Ducks, scored a third-period goal to top the defending champion Carolina Hurricanes 3-2, and leaned on Devin Cooley to lock down a 2-1 win over the Minnesota Wild.
Cooley made 34 saves against the Hurricanes and 36 against the Wild.
"The last five or 10 minutes, I was like, 'Okay, now it's my turn. Like to return the favor a little bit,'" Cooley said following the win against Minnesota. "The guys battled so hard for me. I wanted to battle for them."
Aydar Suniev and Joel Farabee scored first-period power-play goals, giving the Flames an early 2-0 lead. Minnesota outshot Calgary 17-3 in the third period in an effort to rally and tie the game late, which is where Flames head coach Ryan Huska said Cooley really stood tall.
"For two periods, I thought we were really good," Huska recalled. "I thought we did a lot of good things against a good team. In the third period, our goaltender was our best player. When you find yourself in situations when you're really pushing for a win, sometimes you take on a little water, and when we did, he was unreal."
--Field Level Media

items.title: SpaceX afronta dificultades en las negociaciones por su deuda de US$40.000 millones para IA
items.author: Carmen Arroyo, Laura Benitez
items.summary: La volatilidad en los mercados de crédito ha complicado las negociaciones sobre el precio de la operación, diseñada para financiar la compra de chips de Nvidia sin registrar la deuda en los libros con ...
items.body: Bloomberg — Los esfuerzos de SpaceX ( SPCX ) por ultimar una estructura de deuda fuera de balance por valor de US$40.000 millones destinada a la expansión de su división de inteligencia artificial se han visto afectados por las recientes turbulencias del mercado, que han elevado los costes de financiación en todo el sector y han complicado las negociaciones sobre los precios. La operación que se está debatiendo está diseñada para financiar la compra de chips de Nvidia Corp. ( NVDA ) a través de una entidad con fines específicos, lo que mantendrá los pasivos fuera de los libros contables de SpaceX y salvaguardará sus calificaciones de grado de inversión, según fuentes familiarizadas con el asunto. Los banqueros, liderados por Goldman Sachs Group Inc. ( GS ), están debatiendo la estructura con inversores encabezados por Apollo Global Management Inc. ( APO ), y está previsto que Atlas SP —respaldada por Apollo— se encargue de gestionar la entidad, según indicaron dichas fuentes, que solicitaron mantener el anonimato al tratar información privada. Pacific Investment Management Co. también está valorando la posibilidad de invertir, según las mismas fuentes. Ver más: SpaceX negocia acceso a 80.000 estaciones base en EE.UU. para su nueva red móvil Aunque las negociaciones sobre el precio siguen en curso, encontrar niveles en los que ambas partes puedan ponerse de acuerdo se ha complicado debido a la inquietud que se ha extendido por los mercados de crédito en los últimos días, según indicaron las fuentes. Los inversores en deuda están cada vez más preocupados por la enorme carga de deuda que se está acumulando para financiar inversiones en IA, lo que está provocando una ola de ventas de acciones del sector de la IA, ampliando los diferenciales de los bonos corporativos y haciendo que los indicadores de riesgo crediticio se disparen. Las negociaciones de las últimas semanas habían situado una parte subordinada de la deuda en un rango de rendimiento en torno al 8%, aunque la reciente volatilidad ha obligado a los inversores a volver a empezar desde cero, según indicaron dichas fuentes. Los representantes de SpaceX y Atlas no respondieron a las solicitudes de comentarios, mientras que los de Goldman, Apollo y Pimco se negaron a hacer declaraciones. Ver más: Fusión de Tesla y SpaceX podría aumentar la fortuna de Elon Musk en US$110.000 millones Con la estructura más reciente, SpaceX podría evitar que se repita el intento de financiación del año pasado por parte de xAI, la startup de IA de Elon Musk. En esa operación, una entidad buscó obtener hasta US$20.000 millones en deuda fuera de balance mediante un acuerdo de venta con arrendamiento posterior (sale-leaseback) con Valor Equity Partners, un aliado de larga data de Musk. Sin embargo, SpaceX tuvo que contabilizar finalmente unos US$13.000 millones de esa deuda como propia después de que los auditores la declararan un “acuerdo de venta con arrendamiento posterior fallido”, según el informe de resultados de SpaceX publicado esta semana. En el marco de la operación propuesta, los banqueros que asesoran a SpaceX están buscando la estructura de una entidad con fines específicos (SPV), dado que la deuda de la empresa se encuentra a solo unos pocos niveles de calificación por debajo de la categoría de “basura” y sus bonos actuales cotizan a niveles de grado especulativo. Goldman también podría asumir parte de la deuda, según estas fuentes. Se espera que el paquete de deuda se emita en tres tramos de los denominados bonos 144a, una estructura de colocación privada que se ha vuelto habitual en la captación de fondos para unidades de procesamiento general, o chips. Ver más: Acción de SpaceX se dispara en bolsa: la IA supera a Starlink y Wall Street cree que puede subir 50% Un tramo subordinado oscilará entre US$25.000 y US$30.000 millones, y los otros dos tramos serán de US$10.000 millones y hasta US$5.000 millones, según indicaron las fuentes. Las conversaciones iniciales habían situado la deuda en diferenciales que oscilaban entre 230 puntos básicos por encima de los índices de referencia para algunos de los préstamos y más de 300 puntos básicos, según indicaron. Esta última operación se produce tras unos sólidos resultados del tercer trimestre, en el que la unidad de IA de SpaceX obtuvo ganancias por primera vez. La empresa está impulsando cada vez más sus ingresos mediante la venta de potencia de cálculo de sus centros de datos de Memphis a laboratorios de IA externos y a hiperescaladores. El aumento de la elevada carga de deuda de SpaceX podría ejercer presión sobre sus calificaciones crediticias, justo cuando se intensifican las necesidades de capital para centros de datos y chips. Durante la conferencia sobre resultados de SpaceX celebrada el martes, el director financiero, Bret Johnsen, indicó que la captación de deuda continuará, citando conversaciones con varias fuentes de capital de deuda disponibles. Ver más: Fusión de Tesla y SpaceX: 5 preguntas para entender el gigante de US$3,6 billones que estudia Elon Musk “Estamos plenamente convencidos de que podremos llevar esto a cabo de forma muy mesurada y seguir manteniendo nuestra calificación de grado de inversión (IG) a lo largo del proceso”, afirmó. Para Apollo, esta operación se suma a una serie de importantes financiaciones en el ámbito de la inteligencia artificial. Se espera que la estructura adopte un enfoque similar al de una operación de gran envergadura que Apollo lideró a principios de este año y que permitió a Anthropic PBC adquirir chips de Broadcom Inc. ( AVGO ). En aquella operación, la gestora de activos utilizó su unidad Atlas para recaudar capital y mantener la deuda fuera del balance de Broadcom, sin dejar de contar con una garantía de esta empresa de primer orden. Apollo afirmó que se trataba de su operación más compleja hasta la fecha. Lea más en Bloomberg.com

items.title: Golden Knights, Blue Jackets bothered after blowout losses
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: The Vegas Golden Knights bring a streak of four straight 6-2 games into their Saturday road contest against the Columbus Blue Jackets.
items.body:
The Vegas Golden Knights bring a streak of four straight 6-2 games into their Saturday road contest against the Columbus Blue Jackets.
The good news for the Golden Knights? They won the first two games in that span, defeating the Calgary Flames and the Pittsburgh Penguins. The bad news? They carry a two-game losing streak into Ohio, which includes a setback against the St. Louis Blues on Thursday in the opener of their two-game road trip.
The Golden Knights, who advanced to the Stanley Cup Final last season behind strong defense and solid goaltending, allowed only 24 goals over their first 10 games of the season, so allowing 12 goals in their back-to-back losses to the Tampa Bay Lightning and St. Louis could be considered concerning.
"A little bit," said Vegas center Jack Eichel, who leads the team with 19 points and 13 assists. "I feel like it's just sloppy play on our own part. The last two hasn't been like us. I think it's a good opportunity for us all to look in the mirror and know we have to be better as a group, all five guys on the ice at a time, working with our goaltender.
"I don't want to say concerning because obviously we know we have it in this room, but you don't want to give up that many goals in back-to-back games. ... We as a team have to be better."
Before the recent slump, Vegas had allowed a total of six goals in its three previous games, and just four goals in a contest twice.
"You don't want to give up six in back-to-back games," said veteran Golden Knights defenseman Brayden McNabb. "We'll look at it and get better. A humbling last couple of games, so we'll get better."
Next up is a Columbus team coming off a 6-2 loss of its own on Tuesday against the visiting Toronto Maple Leafs. The Blue Jackets, who have garnered just six points over their first eight games, trailed 5-1 after two periods and lost despite finishing with a 38-22 edge in shots on goal.
Columbus brings a two-game losing streak into the Saturday contest and has gone 1-4-0 over its past five games, including a 1-0 overtime win over the New York Rangers on Oct. 17. Only Vancouver (five) has fewer points in the league.
Blue Jackets coach Rick Bowness blames needless penalties combined with turnovers for his team's recent struggles. Columbus also brings in a streak of going 0-for-20 on the power play. The Blue Jackets have not scored with the man advantage since their opener against Buffalo on Oct. 1.
Bowness called out his team for its sloppy play after the Tuesday defeat to the Maple Leafs.
"You go back to the Rangers game, we didn't turn the puck over," Bowness said. "Then the first (period), look at all the turnovers. If it continues, people are going to start losing ice time. I'm going to have to bench some guys. If they keep taking penalties, I'm going to have to bench them. That's bringing that on themselves.
"I'm out of patience with it. You want to keep saying 'I can make that play' and then not make it, and we end up playing a three-quarters ice game, then expect to lose some ice time."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Typhoon Champi sweeps past Taiwan, leaving 1 dead, 500 injured
items.author: Yimou Lee, Angie Teo, Ann Wang
items.creator: Yimou Lee, Angie Teo, Ann Wang
items.summary: Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing 1 person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continued to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast though it was not expected to make landfall there.
items.body:
Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing 1 person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continued to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast though it was not expected to make landfall there.
At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi is weakening though still packing gusts of around 126 kph (78 mph) near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration.
The storm was about 170 km (106 miles) northeast of Taiwan, having glanced off the island's northeastern coast in Yilan County early on Saturday, the CWA said.
The centre of the storm turned south around midnight, hugging the Yilan coastline before making a rare loop offshore and moving away northward. Wind gusts touched 227 kph (141 mph) in some coastal areas, knocking down power lines and sending roof tiles flying.
'MOST TERRIFYING AROUND MIDNIGHT' "It was most terrifying around midnight," said a retired teacher surnamed Lin as he inspected downed banana trees in his garden in Yilan. "It was a sleepless night. I haven't seen anything like this in many years."
The storm's forecast track shows it turning north, tracking up the Chinese coast and eventually moving into southern Japan.
Taiwan's fire department said the death toll remained at 1, a man swept away by waves from the island of Liuqiu, with 527 injuries during the heavy wind and torrential rain.
Taipower said more than 288,000 homes had lost electricity, though most had been reconnected.
The transport ministry said 259 flights were cancelled, an improvement from Friday, when the number was almost 1,000.
In the capital Taipei, there were downed trees and on-off squally rain showers.
Taipei resident Thomas Wang, 70, said the storm felt like something out of the horror film "Poltergeist".
"It was quite scary," he said, out running morning errands.
Governments in a swathe of northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, declared a second day of office and school closures on Saturday.
Although more common in summer, typhoons can strike in autumn too.
China's emergency management ministry sent a team to the eastern province of Zhejiang as Champi approached, warning of strong winds and heavy rain through Sunday. It said it had readied 400 rescue workers and 600 pieces of equipment, while more than 41,000 firefighters were on emergency duty.
In Taizhou, a city on Zhejiang's coast, more than 3,800 fishing boats returned to harbour, offshore fish-farm workers were brought ashore and 2,084 island visitors were evacuated, state media reported.
Authorities halted 25 offshore construction projects and suspended 18 passenger ferry routes.

items.title: Jayson Tatum puts up 36 as Celtics send Knicks to second straight loss
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Jayson Tatum scored a game-high 36 points, including nine late in the fourth quarter, as the Boston Celtics withstood a late comeback bid by the visiting New York Knicks to escape with a 107-103 victory on Friday.
items.body:
Jayson Tatum scored a game-high 36 points, including nine late in the fourth quarter, as the Boston Celtics withstood a late comeback bid by the visiting New York Knicks to escape with a 107-103 victory on Friday.
Tatum finished with nine rebounds and seven assists for the Celtics, who have split their first two games. Paul George and reserve Neemias Queta had 15 points apiece while Derrick White added 12 points.
Celtics center Mitchell Robinson, the lone member of the Knicks' rotation who didn't return to the defending NBA champions, had four points and four rebounds in 22-plus minutes.
Karl-Anthony Towns (22 points, 10 rebounds), OG Anunoby (20 points, 10 rebounds) and Josh Hart (10 points, 12 rebounds) all had double-doubles for the Knicks, who have lost their first two games.
New York has taken consecutive losses for the first time since dropping Games 2 and 3 of an Eastern Conference first-round playoff series against the Atlanta Hawks in April, after which the Knicks won 15 of the next 16 games to clinch their first title since 1973.
Miles McBride scored 20 points off the New York bench, while Jalen Brunson had 19 points.
The Celtics led by as many as 12 points three times in the fourth quarter, the last at 94-82 on a three-point play by Queta, before the Knicks mounted a 9-0 run. Boston missed seven consecutive shots as New York rallied.
Towns dunked to pull the Knicks within 94-91 with 4:09 left, but he missed a long 3-point attempt 28 seconds later and Tatum responded with a layup to end the Celtics' drought.
The Knicks got within 99-98 on Brunson's fallaway jumper with 1:41 remaining, but Tatum sank a turnaround over Hart following a timeout and Towns was whistled for an illegal screen on the next possession. Tatum then hit a long corner fallaway, again over Hart, to extend the lead to 103-98.
Anunoby answered with two free throws, but Tatum hit a 3-pointer on the next possession. McBride sank a 3-pointer before Payton Pritchard iced the win by splitting a pair of free throws with 11 seconds left.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Mavericks beat Pacers as Cooper Flagg leaves with shoulder soreness
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Kyrie Irving scored a game-high 24 points as the Mavericks defeated the Indiana Pacers 121-105 on Friday in Indianapolis, but the victory was overshadowed by a left shoulder injury to Dallas' Cooper Flagg.
items.body:
Kyrie Irving scored a game-high 24 points as the Mavericks defeated the Indiana Pacers 121-105 on Friday in Indianapolis, but the victory was overshadowed by a left shoulder injury to Dallas' Cooper Flagg.
With 59.7 seconds left in the second quarter, Aaron Nesmith challenged Flagg's dunk attempt from behind, sending Flagg sprawling. After a review, Nesmith was assessed a flagrant-1 foul.
Naji Marshall rushed in and shoved Nesmith, and both players were assessed technical fouls. Dallas carried a 77-43 lead into the locker room, but Flagg, who had 14 points, five rebounds and six assists, did not return for the second half due to left shoulder soreness.
P.J. Washington added 20 points and 13 rebounds for the Mavericks, while Max Christie scored 16, Marshall had 15 and Zaccharie Risacher contributed 11 points.
Pascal Siakam paced Indiana with 23 points and Tyrese Haliburton, who missed all of last season after tearing his right Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals, added 18 points in his first home game in 491 days.
Andrew Nembhard scored 16 points for the Pacers. Obi Toppin contributed 13 points, and Ivica Zubac grabbed 11 rebounds.
Each team ended the game with a 1-1 record.
Dallas built a 30-17 lead on a 14-2 run, capped by Irving's layup with 3:27 left in the first quarter. Irving and Flagg hit back-to-back threes, giving Dallas a 43-25 lead as the first quarter wound down.
Dallas extended its lead to 50-31 when Marshall stole the ball from Siakam and fed Risacher for a one-handed dunk with 7:55 left in the second quarter. The Mavericks eventually stretched the margin to 30 points during a 15-0 run.
Toppin's three-point play capped an 8-0 Pacers run that cut their deficit to 85-62 with 4:22 left in the third quarter.
Toppin's dunk cut the deficit to 106-90 with 7:38 remaining, and Haliburton's jumper trimmed it to 118-105 with 1:56 left.
Dallas finished without Irving, who fouled out with 4:23 to go.
--Field Level Media
