Anger over living costs and strained public services has drawn students, workers and unions onto the streets in recent weeks, but authorities say radical militants and bands of young looters have taken advantage of the dispute to sow chaos.
Some far-right politicians have blamed migrants and radical Islam for the turmoil. President Emmanuel Macron has dismissed such accusations.
Ratcheting up the tensions, a man opened fire from a car west of Paris on Friday, killing one person and wounding four others, including a 12-year-old girl.
"(It was) objectively a racist attack," said local mayor Ali Rabeh, blaming far-right rhetoric for inflaming tensions.
Police have authorised only one union demonstration in Paris on Saturday, rejecting requests for rallies lodged by France's main student union, UNEF, and the Yellow Vest movement, an anti-establishment force that first emerged in 2018.

Demonstrators sit on the roadway in front of officers of the French CRS riot police during a protest organised by student collectives and trade unions in Paris, France, Oct 22, 2026. (Photo: REUTERS/Abdul Saboor)

Many French cities beyond Paris have also banned protests, but the second-largest city, Marseille, rescinded an earlier restriction order and said it would allow a union demonstration.
UNEF said its rallies, which grew from high school protests last month against teacher shortages and shabby facilities, would go ahead regardless.
Marylise Leon, the general secretary of the CFDT, one of the nation's largest trade unions, criticised Macron for not sanctioning more demonstrations.
"It's counterproductive because there is a lot of anger, a lot of anger and a demand to be considered and to be listened to," she told French broadcaster TF1. 
"It's not for the president to decide who can legitimately request to protest."

Related:

'We don't really want to cancel': Singaporeans weigh France travel plans amid violent protests

Commentary: French students are showing us what protest looks like in the age of viral spectacle

FAR-RIGHT CONGRESS A POSSIBLE FLASHPOINT Nunez said 10,000 more police would be on the streets than a week ago, while mounted police, helicopters, drones and anti-drone systems would be deployed across the country.
Armoured vehicles and water cannon vehicles would also be available, while curfews imposed in some sensitive areas this past week would remain in force.
Authorities are also concerned that the annual congress of Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally in Orleans this weekend could become a flashpoint, with left-wing and anti-racist groups announcing counter-demonstrations.
The upsurge of violence has boosted poll ratings for Le Pen, who is the frontrunner for next year's presidential election. She has portrayed the unrest as evidence of a collapse in state authority.
Fears of renewed turmoil prompted several of Paris' best-known cultural institutions, including the Louvre, the Musée d'Orsay and the Opera House, to close all day on Saturday.
Paris St Germain's home Ligue 1 football match with Olympique Lyonnais was shifted from Sunday to Monday over security concerns. However, an NFL regular-season game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints is still scheduled to be played in Paris on Sunday, although US President Donald Trump suggested it should be cancelled.
Business groups also urged shops to stay shut after some 3,000 stores and businesses were ransacked last weekend.
Alain Di Crescenzo, the president of France's chamber of commerce, said some shopkeepers were arming themselves with baseball bats, crowbars and shotguns to protect their properties. But he urged them not to turn to violence.
"It’s extremely worrying," he told Europe 1 radio. "It's not their job to do that. It would add suffering onto suffering."
The social turbulence has intensified scrutiny of France's economic outlook and ratings agency Moody's is widely expected to cut the French credit rating on Friday, underscoring concern that the government had not reined in public spending.

Source: Reuters/gs

items.title: Moderna y Merck enfrentan dudas de inversionistas pese a los avances de su vacuna contra el melanoma
items.author: Michelle Fay Cortez, Robert Langreth
items.summary: La vacuna personalizada redujo un 42% el riesgo de recurrencia del melanoma y un 38% el de diseminación a distancia. Sin embargo, los datos filtrados generaron dudas entre los inversionistas sobre su ...
items.body: Bloomberg — Los datos filtrados del tan esperado ensayo clínico de la vacuna contra el melanoma de Moderna Inc. ( MRNA ) y Merck & Co. ( MRK ) han generado una inusual discrepancia entre los médicos, que celebraron sus resultados, y Wall Street, donde se produjo una venta masiva de acciones. Normalmente, los resultados de este tipo de ensayos clínicos decisivos son binarios: médicos, pacientes e inversores descubren si un nuevo medicamento marcará una diferencia significativa en la vida de las personas y llegan a la misma conclusión. En cambio, a medida que se filtraban en las redes sociales informes sobre los resultados de la vacuna contra el melanoma, días antes de la presentación cuidadosamente preparada que tenía previsto ofrecer ante miles de oncólogos reunidos en Madrid con motivo del congreso de la Sociedad Europea de Oncología Médica, esas realidades divergieron. Ver más: Moderna cae un récord de 26% tras filtrarse datos de su vacuna contra el melanoma con Merck La vacuna personalizada contra el cáncer desarrollada por Moderna y Merck ayudó claramente a los pacientes, reduciendo en un 42% la probabilidad de que sus tumores reaparecieran tras su extirpación quirúrgica y previniendo su diseminación a distancia en un 38%. Sin embargo, las acciones de ambas farmacéuticas cayeron, y la caída de Moderna alcanzó niveles récord durante la sesión bursátil de este jueves. Los resultados suponen un gran avance para el melanoma, uno de los tipos de cáncer más comunes, y podrían constituir una nueva y potente herramienta para tratar numerosas formas operables de la enfermedad. La vacuna podría ayudar a muchos miles de personas con melanoma que presentan un alto riesgo de recidiva. Este tipo de resultados suelen sentar las bases para la aprobación de nuevos medicamentos, y los médicos acogieron con satisfacción los hallazgos. “Estoy bastante impresionado”, aseguró Michael Postow, especialista en melanoma del Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center y uno de los investigadores. Los beneficios podrían incrementar con el tiempo, señaló. “Es probable que, hasta ahora, no hayamos visto el efecto terapéutico completo de todo esto”. Incluso tras la caída de este jueves, las acciones de Moderna siguen estando muy por encima del nivel en el que se encontraban antes de que la compañías anunciara en agosto que la vacuna era eficaz, sin presentar el conjunto completo de datos. Wall Street, no obstante, ha revisado a la baja algunas de sus expectativas más optimistas respecto a la empresa biotecnológica tras la publicación de esta semana. Había descontado la idea de que la vacuna fuera el punto de partida de una línea oncológica más amplia que Moderna ha estado tratando de desarrollar, y que algún día podría incluir tratamientos similares para el cáncer de pulmón, de vejiga y otros tipos de cáncer. Los datos limitados han suscitado ciertas dudas sobre lo difícil que resultaría ello, al mostrar que la capacidad para prevenir la diseminación a distancia podría no ser tan sólida como se esperaba. La información disponible no ha infundido confianza en algunos inversionistas de Moderna, que apostaban por el giro de la empresa tras la Covid-19 para convertirse en una importante empresa dedicada al cáncer. “Aunque la aprobación parece probable, el éxito comercial es mucho menos seguro”, escribió Trung Huynh, analista de RBC Capital Markets, en una nota dirigida a los inversionistas. Los datos plantean “cuestiones fundamentales” sobre la propuesta de valor de la vacuna en comparación con el tratamiento de referencia actual, que ofrece beneficios similares a un coste potencialmente mucho menor, señaló. Ver más: Moderna se dispara 160% y deja millonarias pérdidas a quienes apostaban por su caída El éxito de la vacuna contra el melanoma también someterá a Moderna y Merck a la presión de completar los ensayos en otros tipos de cáncer, incluso cuando surgen dudas sobre las ventas a corto plazo y el mercado potencialmente más amplio para dicha tecnología. “Se trata de una forma extraordinariamente compleja y potencialmente costosa de fabricar fármacos”, afirmó Lennard Lee, profesor asociado de la Universidad de Oxford. “La logística podría hacer que Amazon pareciera sencilla”. Todos los pacientes del estudio recibieron además Keytruda, el fármaco oncológico más vendido de Merck, lo que convierte a las vacunas personalizadas diseñadas para cada paciente en una terapia complementaria. Los beneficios adicionales, junto con la ausencia de efectos secundarios graves, podrían convencer a más pacientes de optar por este tratamiento, señaló Sekwon Jang, director de investigación y terapias contra el melanoma e investigador clínico del Inova Schar Cancer Institute, en el norte de Virginia. Ver más: FDA aprueba medicamento contra cáncer de piel avanzado para pacientes sin respuesta a inmunoterapia “Con esta combinación, creo que la relación riesgo-beneficio es, de hecho, mucho más favorable”, explicó Jang. “Espero que más pacientes míos opten por recibir este tratamiento combinado”, agregó, si finalmente se aprueba. No obstante, los inversionistas ya esperaban resultados sólidos después de que las empresas emitieran un comunicado de prensa en agosto en el que se indicaba que el estudio había tenido éxito, y algo más. Esa noticia avivó las expectativas respecto al uso de la tecnología de ARNm de Moderna, diseñada para permitir a los médicos preparar el sistema inmunitario para detectar y destruir invasores extraños y otras amenazas, incluidas las células tumorales. Luego de décadas con resultados decepcionantes, estos hallazgos podrían suponer un real avance en el desarrollo de una vacuna contra el cáncer dirigida a los tumores sólidos. Aun así, los detalles de los resultados del estudio todavía no se han presentado en su totalidad a los médicos ni a los inversionistas, y se necesitan para evaluar su potencial y validar sus expectativas. Los resultados serán presentados este sábado en Madrid, donde un grupo más amplio de oncólogos evaluará los hallazgos. -Con la colaboración de Madison Muller. Lea más en Bloomberg

items.title: Amazon cloud capacity sold out through 2027, CEO Jassy says
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on Friday that Amazon Web Services' cloud computing capacity is largely sold out through 2027, with significant commitments extending into 2028, on growing demand for AI infrastructure.
items.body:
Amazon (AMZN.O) CEO Andy Jassy said on Friday that Amazon Web Services' cloud computing capacity is largely sold out through 2027, with significant commitments extending into 2028, on growing demand for AI infrastructure.
In a video podcast with Andreessen Horowitz co-founder Ben Horowitz and general partner Erik Torenberg, Jassy said Amazon is struggling to keep pace with the insatiable demand from AI labs and enterprises.
Earlier this year, Amazon had said it would spend [USN:L4N43X10O TEXT:"about $220 billion"] in capital expenditure for 2026
Jassy said the company "could invest a lot more and it wouldn't be a bad use of capital," considering cloud-computing capacity for 2026 is already sold out
"2027 is largely sold out. We always leave a certain amount for on demand and our inference service bedrock, or EC2, but largely sold out all the big chunks. A good chunk of 2028 is sold out," he said
EC2 is an AWS service that provides cloud servers for running applications, while Bedrock gives customers access to AI models to build generative AI applications
Amazon is scheduled to report third quarter results on October 29

items.title: Bulls storm back from early deficit to beat Bucks
items.author: Field Level Media
items.creator: Field Level Media
items.summary: Norman Powell scored 25 points and rookie Caleb Wilson added 21 on Friday to help the visiting Chicago Bulls earn a 132-125 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks.
items.body:
Norman Powell scored 25 points and rookie Caleb Wilson added 21 on Friday to help the visiting Chicago Bulls earn a 132-125 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks.
Leonard Miller had 19 points, while Jalen Smith chipped in 14 points and 13 rebounds for Chicago, which rebounded after suffering a 43-point loss to the Toronto Raptors on Wednesday. Buddy Hield scored 13, Isaac Okoro had 12 and Tre Jones tallied 11 points and eight assists for the Bulls, who trailed by 15 points after the first quarter.
Tyler Herro led Milwaukee with 34 points, followed by Jaime Jaquez Jr.'s 19 points and 11 boards. Kyle Kuzma scored 14 and Myles Turner had 12, while Ryan Rollins, AJ Green and Kel'el Ware scored 11 apiece for the Bucks, who lost their second straight to open the season.
Rookie Brayden Burries made a 3-pointer and Ware scored around the rim to give the Bucks a five-point lead with 2:55 left in the third quarter. Smith beat the third-quarter buzzer with a dunk that cut the Bulls' deficit to 104-102 entering the fourth.
Chicago scored the first six points of the final quarter and grabbed a 108-104 lead on Wilson's slam. The Bulls pushed the lead to eight on Hield's trey with 7:19 remaining.
With Milwaukee trailing by five, Herro connected on back-to-back 3-pointers, returning the lead to the Bucks.
Wilson made two free throws to put the Bulls ahead 124-123 with 1:16 left.
After Jones picked off Rollins' pass, Wilson made another pair from the foul line to push the lead to three. A missed 3-pointer by Herro and two more free throws from Powell gave the Bulls a five-point cushion with 20 seconds left.
Wilson's steal and Jones' subsequent two foul shots sealed Chicago's victory.
Milwaukee jumped out to a 19-6 lead on Herro's first triple less than five minutes in. Green sank a 3-pointer in the closing seconds of the first quarter to give the Bucks a 32-17 advantage.
Matas Buzelis' slam pulled the Bulls within seven, but Kasparas Jakucionis and Rollins hit consecutive treys to build the margin to 44-31 with 8:35 left in the first half.
Chicago answered again and took a 55-51 lead on Hield's 3-pointer, which stamped a 16-0 run.
Kuzma made a layup with three seconds left in the first half to give the Bucks a 62-61 halftime edge.
--Field Level Media

items.title: UK government sets out $800 million of AI security funding
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Britain's government set out around £600 million ($800 million)of funding on Saturday largely geared towards defending against health and security threats from artificial intelligence.
items.body:
Britain's government set out around £600 million ($800 million)of funding on Saturday largely geared towards defending against health and security threats from artificial intelligence.
The biggest chunk of funding will go to a new biosecurity initiative, including £100 million for a laboratory using AI to detect biological threats and £65 million to develop countermeasures against pathogens.
AI minister Kanishka Narayan said the aim was for the AI Biosecurity Lab to become a major global institution "bringing together world-leading scientific expertise to protect people from emerging biological threats".
Tech companies OpenAI and Anthropic will offer up to £200 million of model credits to the biosecurity initiative
Google Deepmind (GOOGL.O) and London-based AI life sciences startup Basecamp Research will offer other assistance
Britain's government will give its existing [USN:L8N45E18S TEXT:"AI Security Institute"] an extra £120 million
£130 million will go towards new projects to improve cyber defences for critical infrastructure and the wider economy, known as the National Cyber Shield and the National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability Centre
£60 million will go towards a fund that will invest in British companies using AI to advance robotics, autonomous systems and manufacturing
£60 million will be used for AI research and procurement contracts
An extra £23 million will go to research on the economic impact of AI
£18 million will go to a new chip design academy
£15 million will fund a prize for AI solutions to public policy problems, initially focused on healthcare
£30 million will go to regional mayors to support local AI work
Britain's [USN:L8N42P1O5 TEXT:"National Cyber Security Centre"] will receive an unspecified sum to expand in Manchester
Anthropic alone racked up [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"more than $12 billion in operating expenses"] last year
($1 = 0.7472 pounds)

items.title: Thailand welcomes US-Myanmar engagement, expects ASEAN talks on country's future
items.author: Sergio Goncalves, Miguel Pereira
items.creator: Sergio Goncalves, Miguel Pereira
items.summary: Thailand welcomes US engagement with Myanmar and expects discussions at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations' November summit in Manila on how to proceed with the member barred since the 2021 coup, Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow told Reuters on Friday.
items.body:
Thailand welcomes US engagement with Myanmar and expects discussions at the Association of Southeast Asian Nations' November summit in Manila on how to proceed with the member barred since the 2021 coup, Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow told Reuters on Friday.
The United States and Myanmar's military-backed government held [USN:L6N46300W TEXT:"talks in Tokyo"] two weeks ago, their second meeting in a month as Washington steps up re-engagement with the generals it shunned after the coup.
"We don't want to see Myanmar isolated, we don't want Myanmar to be an arena for geopolitical rivalry ... so the US engagement is something that we welcome," he said.
Engagement "does not mean legitimizing the regime," but aims to encourage peaceful conflict resolution and reconciliation with the opposition, Sihasak, who is also deputy prime minister, added.
He said there was "some shift in ASEAN's position," citing Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing's recent visits to Laos, Cambodia, Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia, but said it was unclear whether the Manila summit would address restoring Myanmar's full representation.
"It's good that we're going to have a very substantive, very extensive, and very in-depth discussion on how to proceed on Myanmar," he said.
He also said Thailand and Cambodia could resolve their longstanding land and maritime boundary disputes within 12 to 18 months despite limited progress.
"It is possible, everything is possible," he said, cautioning that confidence-building and addressing security concerns along the land border, where clashes have occurred, must come first.
Cambodia launched a conciliation process under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea in June to resolve the maritime boundary dispute, after Thailand terminated a 2001 joint development framework in May following deadly border clashes. The first meeting was held about a month ago.
"Right now, we haven't achieved, to be very frank, much progress," he said.
The maritime dispute centers on overlapping claims to about 26,000 sq km in the Gulf of Thailand, believed to hold oil and gas reserves worth around $300 billion. Thailand wants the boundary defined before discussing resource-sharing, he said.
Thailand-EU free-trade talks are in their final stage and could conclude by year-end if there is mutual political will, he added.

items.title: Time for Canadian newcomers to step into spotlight, says Ruggiero
items.author: Amy Tennery
items.creator: Amy Tennery
items.summary: Canada are entering a critical rebuilding phase ahead of next month's ice hockey Women's World Championship, retired US great Angela Ruggiero told Reuters, after falling to the US in the Milano Cortina Olympic gold medal game.
items.body:
Canada are entering a critical rebuilding phase ahead of next month's ice hockey Women's World Championship, retired US great Angela Ruggiero told Reuters, after falling to the US in the Milano Cortina Olympic gold medal game.
Canada have often had the upper hand in the countries' rivalry, with five Olympic golds to three for the US. But US youth conquered Canadian experience in Milano Cortina, as an American roster loaded with [USN:L8N3Z02EC TEXT:"collegiate talent"] held off the veterans from the north in a spine-tingling finale.
Eight months later, Canada announced a World Championship roster with seven tournament debutants at the worlds, with an eye towards replicating US success in developing young up-and-comers.
"They're going with a very young team, an inexperienced team that could really work in their favour," said Ruggiero, speaking to Reuters at the Women's Sports Foundation annual gala this week. "They're building for four years from now. So it was a strategic decision."
The Hall of Famer helped propel the US to four world golds and made her Olympic debut at 18 years old, when the Americans took the first-ever women's ice hockey gold at the 1998 Games.
She said Canada's youth corps should not be underestimated.
"I think back to the 2008 World Championship team. We were a very, very young team. And we believed in ourselves. We were able to win those World Championships because of the psychology in the locker room, even though on the ice we weren't the best team," said Ruggiero.
"If I were Canada's GM, I think it's the smartest thing to do. Reset the clock, figure out chemistry."
The World Championship begins on November 6 after a memorable Milano Cortina Olympics, with the advent of the Professional Women's Hockey League in North America bringing the game into [USN:L8N3ZC0ZU TEXT:"a new era"].
"It was probably all around the most elite, highest skilled, fastest, best brand of women's hockey I have ever seen," said Meghan Duggan, Ruggiero's 2010 Olympic teammate who also appeared at the WSF gala in support of women's sports.
"That shows what the professional league is doing to elevate the game."

items.title: Fever GM Amber Cox follows team president out of Indy
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Fever general manager Amber Cox followed team president Kelly Krauskopf out the door in a major shakeup of the front office on Friday.
items.body:
Fever general manager Amber Cox followed team president Kelly Krauskopf out the door in a major shakeup of the front office on Friday.
Kraskopf resigned earlier in the day and Cox was let go hours later, with the Fever saying the franchise was announcing "the departure of Amber Cox."
The franchise wrapped up its best regular season in team history with 26 wins and went to the conference semifinals in Cox's first season in the GM role.
Indiana had three players named WNBA All-Stars and two of the league's top three scorers in Kelsey Mitchell (second) and Caitlin Clark. Mitchell is a pending free agent and said she will shop around to find the best fit for her and her family this offseason.
Mel Raines, president and CEO of Pacers Sports & Entertainment, said a national search is underway to fill the front-office spots.
"Through her two seasons with the Fever, Amber has helped us navigate the seismic growth of the WNBA and our franchise," Raines said. "We're grateful for her contributions and wish her the very best moving forward."
--Field Level Media

items.title: Ronaldinho voltará aos gramados pelo italiano Ravenna
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: O craque brasileiro Ronaldinho Gaúcho voltará ao futebol competitivo no próximo mês, quando jogará pelo Ravenna, time da terceira divisão italiana, contra o rival local Forlì, no dia 15 de novembro, anunciou o clube da Série C nesta sexta-feira.
items.body:
O craque brasileiro Ronaldinho Gaúcho voltará ao futebol competitivo no próximo mês, quando jogará pelo Ravenna, time da terceira divisão italiana, contra o rival local Forlì, no dia 15 de novembro, anunciou o clube da Série C nesta sexta-feira.
O ex-atacante do Barcelona e do Milan, de 46 anos, que conquistou a Copa do Mundo de 2002 com o Brasil e a Bola de Ouro em 2005, jogou pela última vez em competições oficiais pelo Fluminense, em 2015. Ele se aposentou oficialmente em 2018.
O Ravenna contratou Ronaldinho em junho e, posteriormente, ele adquiriu uma participação no clube, que é de propriedade de seu amigo Ignazio Cipriani.
Cipriani disse que a iniciativa tinha como objetivo “aproximar toda a cidade do time”.
Ronaldinho Gaúcho não chegou a confirmar que jogaria quando chegou à Itália em agosto, embora tenha deixado em aberto a possibilidade de marcar o 300º gol de sua carreira.
“Estou aqui para ajudar”, disse ele na ocasião.
O clássico contra o Forì será disputado no Stadio Bruno Benelli, em Ravenna. O Ravenna ocupa a segunda colocação do Grupo B da Série C, com 20 pontos em 10 partidas, oito pontos atrás do líder, o Spezia.

items.title: Oregon State breakout WR Jesse Legree re-signs with school for 2027
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Oregon State star freshman receiver Jesse Legree announced Friday that he has re-signed with the Beavers for the 2027 season.
items.body:
Oregon State star freshman receiver Jesse Legree announced Friday that he has re-signed with the Beavers for the 2027 season.
Legree made the announcement at his former high school, Saint Frances Academy in Baltimore, partly because he was lightly recruited and didn't have a signing day a year ago.
"We've built a great culture and it's only going to get bigger from here," Legree told ESPN. "This is going to be the start of a national powerhouse."
The 5-foot-10, 172-pound Legree was only a three-star recruit but has exploded onto the scene in Corvallis. He leads the nation with 1,040 receiving yards and 14 touchdown receptions. He is two touchdown catches away from matching the school record held by longtime NFL receiver Brandin Cooks (16 in 2013).
Legree has topped 100 yards receiving in all seven games for Oregon State (5-2, 3-0 Pac-12). His top outing was 240 yards - second-most in school history -- against then-No. 13 Texas Tech on Sept. 12.
He has caught three touchdown passes twice and grabbed two on three other occasions. He has at least one touchdown catch in each game.
His season high for receptions is 10 against San Diego State. He had 191 yards and three scores in the Beavers' 66-14 trouncing of the Aztecs. Legree is averaging 22.6 yards on 46 receptions.
Legree has recently been mentioned as a Heisman Trophy candidate. He said he belongs at the top of the conversation.
"Never seen a freshman do what I'm doing week in and week out, and I feel like I'm going to continue to do that," Legree said. "And I feel like everybody who doesn't feel like I should be in that conversation will notice by the end of the season that I deserve that, or should at least be in the top-three conversation."
Oregon State is averaging 51 points per game during a five-game winning streak in JaMarcus Shepherd's first season as head coach.
Legree also held the event during Oregon State's bye week to help attract media attention to the program in hopes of landing athletes for the program.
Oregon State also has a quarterback on the rise in Mercer transfer Branden Atkinson, who won the Jerry Rice Award last season as the top freshman in the FCS. Atkinson leads the nation in passing yardage (2,604 yards) and touchdown passes (24) and has thrown just two interceptions for Oregon State.
The Beavers return to action on Oct. 31 at Fresno State (4-3, 1-2).
--Field Level Media

A surge in jet fuel expenses due to the Iran war has [USN:L4N46813M TEXT:"pressured margins for US airlines"] despite higher airfares and steady demand for air travel.

items.title: Ronaldinho volverá a jugar con el club italiano Ravenna
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: El brasileño Ronaldinho volverá al fútbol competitivo cuando juegue con el Ravenna de la tercera división italiana contra el Forlì, el 15 de noviembre, anunció el viernes el club de la Serie C.
items.body:
El brasileño Ronaldinho volverá al fútbol competitivo cuando juegue con el Ravenna de la tercera división italiana contra el Forlì, el 15 de noviembre, anunció el viernes el club de la Serie C.
El exdelantero del Barcelona y del AC Milan, de 46 años, que ganó el Mundial de 2002 con Brasil y el Balón de Oro en 2005, jugó por última vez en una competición oficial con el Fluminense en 2015.
Se retiró oficialmente en 2018.
El Ravenna fichó a Ronaldinho en junio y, posteriormente, este adquirió una participación en el club, propiedad de su amigo Ignazio Cipriani.
Ronaldinho no llegó a confirmar que jugaría cuando llegó a Italia en agosto, aunque dejó abierta la posibilidad de marcar el gol número 300 de su carrera.

items.title: India's Scotch probe of Diageo, Pernod undermines UK pact benefits: ISWAI
items.summary: The liquor industry group representing Diageo and Pernod Ricard said that India's move to exclude bulk Scotch imports from the reduced tariff contradicts the trade pact ...
items.body:
Home / Industry / News / India's Scotch probe of Diageo, Pernod undermines UK pact benefits: ISWAI

India's Scotch probe of Diageo, Pernod undermines UK pact benefits: ISWAI The liquor industry group representing Diageo and Pernod Ricard said that India's move to exclude bulk Scotch imports from the reduced tariff contradicts the trade pact

Directorate of Revenue Intelligence searched the offices of Pernod and Diageo and questioned executives this month as part of an investigation into whether they misclassified imported products (Photo: AdobeStock)

Reuters NEW DELHI 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 24 2026 | 11:11 AM IST

Listen to This Article

India's move to exclude bulk Scotch imports from a reduced 75 per cent tariff goes against provisions agreed in an India-UK trade deal, a group representing liquor makers Diageo and Pernod Ricard wrote in a letter seen by Reuters.
Whisky tariffs were a sticking point during the years of protracted negotiations leading up to the deal's July 15 implementation, though India ultimately agreed to halve import taxes on certain Scotch imports from 150 per cent to 75 per cent immediately and to 40 per cent over 10 years.
The British government said "iconic UK products" like whiskies would benefit from the pact. Indian investigators, however, have privately told companies the reduced rate does not apply to bulk Scotch concentrates, creating the first significant dispute over the free trade agreement since it took effect.
  India's Directorate of Revenue Intelligence searched the offices of Pernod and Diageo and questioned executives this month as part of an investigation into whether they misclassified imported products to benefit from the reduced rate.
Classification issue risks undermining pact, group says In a letter to India's commerce minister on Friday, the International Spirits and Wines Association of India wrote that the classification issue "risks undermining, in practice, an important market-access benefit negotiated and agreed between India and the United Kingdom".
Also Read

Tax dept probes Pernod, Diageo Scotch imports under UK trade pact

Pernod Ricard India sales grow 19% in Sep quarter; IPO plan awaits approval

UK trade delegation signs growth partnership with businesses in Maharashtra

India-US trade deal talks nearing 'landing point', says Jaishankar

Govt's free trade push could lead to $140 billion GDP gain for India

"The preferential tariff treatment negotiated ... could effectively become unavailable for these imports," continued the letter, a copy of which was seen by Reuters.
ISWAI declined to comment on its letter, while India's commerce ministry did not immediately respond.
Pernod, which counts India as its biggest market by volume, declined to comment. Diageo did not respond to a request for comment. Both told Reuters earlier this week that they were cooperating with Indian authorities carrying out the investigation.
In the British government's first comment on the controversy, a spokesperson said: "We are working with the government of India to resolve this issue to ensure UK businesses can export under the tariffs agreed in the trade deal."
Import tariff disputes have long been a sore point for foreign investors in India, who have in the past faced demands for large amounts of back tax. Such disputes have embroiled the likes of Samsung and Volkswagen.
Pernod faces antitrust cases in India and a $314 million back-tax demand from Indian authorities, who accuse it of undervaluing some imports. The company denies wrongdoing.
Big implications for India's drinks sector ISWAI's letter underscores the shockwaves the investigation has sent through India's $65 billion alcohol market. Britain accounts for almost 75 per cent of India's imported spirits, primarily driven by Scotch whisky, according to Crisil Ratings.
Indian government inspectors have told companies that they do not benefit from the reduced 75 per cent tariff on bulk imports of Scotch concentrates, which must be declared under a customs classification that attracts a 150 per cent duty, three people with direct knowledge of the matter told Reuters.
Pernod and Diageo import bulk concentrates, mixing them with other ingredients to produce hugely popular Indian brands like Royal Stag, Blenders Pride and McDowell's.
The three people said companies including Diageo and Pernod believe concentrates imported from Britain should benefit from the new, lower tariff. ISWAI said in its letter that the India-UK agreement expressly provides preferential tariff treatment for whisky under the relevant tariff lines.
An urgent clarification could ensure market-access benefits negotiated by India and Britain are realised "while avoiding uncertainty and disruption for legitimate industry participants", the letter said.
On Saturday, the UK-based Scotch Whisky Association told Reuters in a statement that the import of bulk Scotch is key to whisky's overall success in India and that upholding the core principles of the bilateral pact is vital.
The association, which counts Diageo and Pernod's Chivas Brothers as members, added the industry was "committed to working in partnership with the UK and Indian governments on the smooth implementation of the deal", so its benefits are unlocked.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

items.title: Caso de Ebola na Nigéria está ligado ao vírus encontrado no primeiro caso do Quênia, diz ministro da Saúde
items.author: Camillus Eboh, George Obulutsa
items.creator: Camillus Eboh, George Obulutsa
items.summary: Uma análise genômica do único caso confirmado de Ebola na Nigéria mostra que o vírus está estreitamente relacionado à cepa detectada no primeiro caso registrado no Quênia, disse nesta sexta-feira o ministro da Saúde nigeriano, Muhammad Ali Pate, fornecendo a primeira ligação genética entre os surtos.
items.body:
Uma análise genômica do único caso confirmado de Ebola na Nigéria mostra que o vírus está estreitamente relacionado à cepa detectada no primeiro caso registrado no Quênia, disse nesta sexta-feira o ministro da Saúde nigeriano, Muhammad Ali Pate, fornecendo a primeira ligação genética entre os surtos.
As autoridades nigerianas afirmaram que não há evidências de que o caso do Quênia tenha viajado para a Nigéria ou tenha tido uma conexão direta com o caso nigeriano.
Pate disse que os contatos ligados ao caso estão sendo rastreados, colocados em quarentena e testados, com alguns resultados negativos e outros ainda pendentes
A Nigéria registrou apenas um caso confirmado de Ebola, de um viajante que havia visitado Uganda
Uganda, que faz fronteira com a República Democrática do Congo (RDC) e já enfrentou surtos de Ebola anteriormente, afirmou nesta sexta-feira que continuava livre do Ebola, mas estava reforçando as precauções
O Ministério da Saúde de Uganda informou que os formulários de localização de viajantes foram restabelecidos para todos os que chegam ao país, independentemente do país de origem
Uganda informou que viajantes com histórico de viagem à RDC, onde o surto teve início, não terão permissão para transitar pelo país

items.title: Ronaldinho to return to action with Italian club Ravenna
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Brazil great Ronaldinho will return to competitive football next month when he plays for Italian third-tier side Ravenna against local rivals Forli on November 15, the Serie C club announced on Friday.
items.body:
Brazil great Ronaldinho will return to competitive football next month when he plays for Italian third-tier side Ravenna against local rivals Forli on November 15, the Serie C club announced on Friday.
The 46-year-old former Barcelona and AC Milan forward, who won the 2002 World Cup with Brazil and the Ballon d'Or in 2005, last played competitively for Brazilian club Fluminense in 2015. He officially retired in 2018.
Ravenna signed Ronaldinho in June and he later acquired a stake in the club, which is owned by his friend Ignazio Cipriani.
Cipriani said the move was intended "to bring the whole city closer to the team".
[USN:L8N44H1KF TEXT:"Ronaldinho"] stopped short of confirming he would play when he arrived in Italy in August, although he left open the prospect of scoring the 300th goal of his career.
"I'm here to help," he said at the time.
The derby against Forli will take place at Ravenna's Stadio Bruno Benelli. Ravenna sit second in Serie C Group B with 20 points from 10 games, eight behind leaders Spezia.

items.title: Gutierrez: US Has Gone Too Far With Tariffs
items.summary: Carlos Gutierrez, former Commerce Secretary and CEO of Kellogg and author of Sheer Will, says trade under the Trump administration has become all-encompassing and can be used as part of geopolitical and political negotiations beyond trade itself. Gutierrez says the US has gone too far with tariffs and that easing them could help reduce inflationary pressure on American consumers. Gutierrez says the US has the infrastructure and capabilities to be a strong exporter, but should focus on high-value industries rather than making consumers pay more to bring back lower-value production. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

items.summary: Andrew Brandt says the Brewers and Rays reaching the World Series—despite ranking 19th and 26th in payroll, respectively—shows how strong management, scouting and player development can compete with high spending. AMSTERDAM, Oct 23 : The discovery of two serious flaws in PHP this week set off a global scramble to keep websites safe from hackers, showing just how critical the three-decade-old open-source programming language is to the internet.
Yet the nonprofit foundation that supports PHP,  which may underpin up to 70 per cent of sites globally, operates on a shoestring budget. 
“We have one full-time staff member (that's me) and 14 mostly part-time contractors,” Executive Director Elizabeth Barron of the PHP Foundation said via email in an interview on Friday. Board members are unpaid volunteers, and funding comes from donations and grants.
The foundation works with outside researchers and companies, including OpenAI and cybersecurity firms Wiz and Calif, to investigate security flaws and coordinate fixes, including Wednesday's patches.

While Web security company Cloudflare has reported millions of hacking attempts, Barron said the foundation had no evidence hackers were able to exploit the vulnerabilities before they were disclosed, or on sites that have been patched.
"We received no further indication from OpenAI, Wiz or Calif, with whom we're working closely on this issue, regarding any issues on patched systems,” she said.
Artificial intelligence has proved both a help and a burden to the foundation. It helped researchers find the flaws, which had been present for a decade, and Barron said it made programmers more efficient.
However, it is also increasing maintainers' workloads. The PHP project is receiving nearly twice as many proposed code changes as a year ago, “yet the number of contributors hasn't doubled,” she said. Reviewing contributions and bug reports requires “a massive amount of human input and experience.”
Recent events have shown how heavily companies and governments rely on PHP, Barron said.
“Given that reliance, it is clear that PHP is incredibly under-funded.”

Source: Reuters

items.title: In Florida, Trump vows to deal with Cuba after Iran gets settled
items.author: Bo Erickson, Maria Cardona, Steve Holland
items.creator: Bo Erickson, Maria Cardona, Steve Holland
items.summary: US President Donald Trump on Friday used a campaign rally in Florida, where Cuban Americans are a potent voting bloc, to vow to address his concerns about Cuba once the Iran war is settled.
items.body:
US President Donald Trump on Friday used a campaign rally in Florida, where Cuban Americans are a potent voting bloc, to vow to address his concerns about Cuba once the Iran war is settled.
In a 90-minute speech in Fort Myers, Trump repeated more military action against Iran may lie ahead as he tries to address the causes of a spike in oil prices that has put Republicans on the defensive ahead of the November 3 midterm elections .
With an eye toward the senior Americans who live in Florida, Trump said he planned to spend $250 million to hire at least 5,000 new nurses in elder care facilities all across America.
While the Iran war has no end in sight, Trump talked tough about Cuba, part of a pattern of putting pressure on the communist government there after ousting the leader of Venezuela early this year.
Trump, who won 68% of the Cuban American vote in Florida in the 2024 election, said American naval forces from Iran will stop at Cuba on the way home.
"We'll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They'll raise up their hands, and then we're going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal," he said.
Secretary of State Rubio, a former US senator from Florida, has been handling much of the Cuba-related policy for Trump.
"To those who seek to create positive change in Cuba - now is the time," Rubio said on X on Friday, urging those disappointed by Cuba's government "to create the change you desire through a discrete partnership with the CIA." His post did not elaborate.
Trump's rally was intended to boost the electoral prospects of Florida Republican Representative Byron Donalds, who is running for governor against Democrat David Jolly.
His speech, the latest in a near-daily blitz of campaign rallies in largely friendly areas, rambled from topic to topic such as the size of his crowds and his White House renovations.
Trump has increased pressure on Cuba in his second term. In September, he labeled Cuba a "failed state" at the UN General Assembly and said, "Freedom will be coming to Cuba," prompting a walkout by the Cuban delegation.
Trump has openly stated that his goal is to fundamentally change Cuba's government. A US-imposed oil blockade has put the country under severe strain as it contends with fuel shortages and blackouts exacerbated by failing infrastructure.
UN human rights experts have condemned the oil blockade as a violation of international law while rights advocates say the Trump administration's threats have echoed an [USN:L4N3YE036 TEXT:"imperialist approach"].

items.title: トルコ、フーシ派との戦闘「想定せず」　サウジとの防衛協定下でも＝国防相
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [アンカラ　２３日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[アンカラ　２３日　ロイター] - トルコのギュレル国防相は２３日、サウジアラビアおよびパキスタンとの防衛協定に基づいて自国軍がイエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派との戦闘に加わることは想定していないとの考えを示した。 

ギュレル氏はスターテレビに対し「われわれはフーシ派とのいかなる衝突も想定していない」と述べ、サウジへのトルコの軍事支援は、カタールの場合と同様、主に抑止力の強化を目的とするものになると語った。

ギュレル氏は、トルコは議会が協定を批准した後、必要な法的手続きと議会の承認に従って、サウジからの軍事支援要請を評価し、支援の範囲を決定すると説明した。

８月に署名され、今週、批准に向けてトルコ議会に提出された「メッカ共同防衛協定」は、トルコ、サウジ、パキスタンの３カ国のいずれか１カ国への武力攻撃を全３カ国への攻撃と見なすことを定めている。

items.title: Russia, Ukraine agree on ceasefire in embattled town, to hold peace talks next month
items.author: Steve Holland, Yuliia Dysa
items.creator: Steve Holland, Yuliia Dysa
items.summary: Ukraine and Russia said on Friday they had agreed on a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky, brokered through US first lady Melania Trump, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said peace negotiators would meet next month for new talks.
items.body:
Ukraine and Russia said on Friday they had agreed on a [USN:L1N4690MZ TEXT:"ceasefire"] in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky, brokered through US first lady Melania Trump, while Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said [USN:L1N4690TJ TEXT:"peace negotiators"] would meet next month for new talks.
The two sides said the ceasefire would go into effect on October 27, allowing the delivery of aid and the evacuation of residents through humanitarian corridors.
Amid a US push to organise new talks aimed at ending the 4-1/2-year-old war , Zelenskiy said negotiators from Ukraine, Russia and the United States had agreed to technical-level meetings in the first half of November in Abu Dhabi. A US official later said the three countries may hold their next talks in a couple weeks in Abu Dhabi or Switzerland.
Zelenskiy said he hoped a meeting of the countries' leaders would follow.
Previous rounds of talks headed by the United States stalled in February with no significant progress towards ending the bloodiest conflict in Europe since World War Two. Russia continues to demand Ukraine cede all of the eastern Donbas region, including territory Russia has not occupied militarily, while Kyiv rejects any notion of giving up land it currently holds.
The latest peace efforts follow a rift between Washington and Kyiv in recent weeks and a series of moves by US President Donald Trump seen as favouring Russia.
A major source of friction was limitations placed on SpaceX's Starlink communication system that Ukraine uses to protect against incoming attacks. Trump [USN:L6N4690ZQ TEXT:"said on Friday"] that if Ukraine still faced a problem with the system, he would straighten it out and, if necessary, speak about the matter to SpaceX (SPCX.O) CEO Elon Musk.
Another contentious point was Trump's announcement of a deal to allow Russia to provide diesel for the US and global markets, an agreement denounced by Ukraine and meant to keep prices down as the president's Republicans contest US midterm elections.
On Friday, Russian Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak [USN:L1N469146 TEXT:"said"] the first three tankers with Russian diesel were on their way to North America.
In the town of Oleshky, occupied by Russian forces since February 2022, residents have reported that they faced a deepening food crisis.
"Both nations agreed to temporarily stop all military action in Oleshky to allow for humanitarian aid to enter and to prepare a civilian evacuation through a designated safe passageway," the White House said in a statement.
The chief of staff of Russian forces, Valery Gerasimov, said on the Defence Ministry's Telegram channel that Russian troops would halt fire from 4 a.m. local time (0100 GMT) on October 27 to allow for the humanitarian operation to start.
Ukraine's General Staff issued a statement agreeing to observe the ceasefire from the same time and pledging to "do everything possible to help Oleshky's residents." Ukraine says it has already [USN:L1N45Q03T TEXT:"used drones twice"] to send food into the town.
Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, also [USN:S8N4390AW TEXT:"said"] the ceasefire would go into effect on October 27 and told Reuters the operation [USN:S8N4390AW TEXT:"would involve"] demining roads to the town, deliveries of food and evacuations of civilians.
MELANIA TRUMP'S DIPLOMATIC EFFORTS Both sides said Melania Trump played an important role in coordinating the agreement. The first lady has been active in trying to get Ukrainian children seized by Russia during the war returned to their families.
"Oleshky is a front-line war city on the brink of disaster," she said in a statement.
"Oleshky's remaining population is comprised primarily of elderly residents who urgently need medical attention, medicine, food and clean water."
Pope Leo [USN:L8N4651KU TEXT:"had spoken"] in the past week both to Zelenskiy and to Russian President Vladimir Putin about conditions in Oleshky.
The White House said Oleshky, located across the Dnipro River from the Ukrainian-held city of Kherson, had 1,700 to 2,000 residents remaining, down from 24,000 before the war.
US ENVOYS Zelenskiy's comments on resuming peace talks followed a meeting with US presidential envoy Steve Witkoff in Norway early this week and a subsequent meeting between Witkoff and Putin in St Petersburg.
Zelenskiy said he spoke on Friday with Witkoff and US envoy Jared Kushner. He said any peace agreement would need strong security guarantees for Ukraine and funding for 10 years to maintain the Ukrainian army.
"The plan is to meet in the first half of November, and as early as possible, of course," Zelenskiy told the Hudson Institute think tank via a video link. He said much would depend on Russia, noting that a similar meeting expected this month had not materialised.
Zelenskiy spoke of the importance of continued diplomatic efforts to reach a ceasefire and end the war, now in its fifth year, adding that Europe should also be involved in the talks.
Ukrainian officials said on Friday that speed restrictions on Starlink systems in Ukraine remained in place, despite Trump's previous statement that the services had been fully restored.
Trump told reporters at the White House on Friday that he had not spoken to Musk about the restrictions but would do so if required.
"If there is a problem, I'll get it straightened out," he said. The caps have been in place since October 13.
Ukraine and Russia also swapped 270 servicemen each in a prisoner exchange on Friday, the Russian Defence Ministry said. Zelenskiy described the swap, the first since August, as a "very important result."
Ukraine's acting prosecutor, Anton Kovalskyi, writing on Telegram, said more than 19,000 [USN:S8N44Z032 TEXT:"Ukrainian civilians"], including 762 children, had been killed since Russia launched its full-scale war more than four years ago.

items.body:
＜為替＞　ドルが円やユーロなどの主要通貨に対しやや上昇した。来週は米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）、日銀が金融政策決定会合を開く。いずれも政策金利の据え置きが予想されているが、今後の金融政策の方向性の手がかりを示すか注目されている。    終盤の取引で、円は対ドルで０．１％安の１５６．９円。ただ、週間ベースでは円は対ドルで約０．７％上昇。９月中旬以来の大幅な上昇となる。ＭＵＦＧのシニア通貨アナリスト、リー・ハードマン氏は「リスク回避姿勢が強まる中、円買いが続いている」と述べた。    ユーロに対してはフランスの債務リスクプレミアムが２０１１年のユーロ圏債務危機以来の高水準に拡大したことなどが重しになっており、ユーロは対ドルで０．２１％安の１．１１９１ドル。週初からは０．４３％下落した。    ユーロは対円でより大きく下落し、一時１７５．０８円と、２０２５年１０月以来の安値を更新。週初からは約１．１％下落した。    フランスでは１７日の抗議デモが過去数十年で最大規模の暴動に発展してから１週間が経過し、ヌニェス内相は暴力行為や略奪の再発防止に向け、２４日に全国で予定される抗議活動に７万人の警察官を動員すると発表。パリのルーブル美術館、オルセー美術館、オペラ座などの主要文化施設の一部が臨時休館となるほか、治安上の懸念からパリで予定されているサッカーフランス１部リーグの試合が２５日から２６日に延期されるなどの影響が出ている。    終盤の取引で、主要通貨に対するドル指数は０．２５％高の１０１．８２。    ＦＲＢの金融政策を巡っては、前日の株式相場急落を受け、１２月の会合での利上げ観測がやや後退したことがＬＳＥＧのデータで示された。ただ、ＦＦ金利先物市場では１２月利上げの確率はなお８１％と見込まれている。    ＥＣＢについては、１２月の理事会で利上げが決定される確率は６６％と織り込まれている。ラガルドＥＣＢ総裁が９月下旬にインフレに対し穏健な政策対応が適切との認識を示していることから、今後の金利見通しについて新たな示唆があるか注目されている。    日銀については、１２月の利上げの確率が６１％と織り込まれている。 

ＮＹ外為市場：[USD/J]

＜債券＞　国債利回りが上昇した。ただそれでも、指標１０年債利回りは５％を下回る水準にとどまっている。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株の上昇が持続するかどうかへの懸念がくすぶっていることが背景にある。    １０年債利回りは３．７ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）上昇の４．９９％。週間では約１１ｂｐ低下しており、６月以来の長さとなる３週連続の低下に向かっている。    株式相場の強気局面を支えるＡＩ関連銘柄への投資の持続性を巡り、足元で懸念が浮上し、投資家は国債などの安全資産に資金を移している。    ３０年債利回りは２．９ｂｐ上昇の５．３１６％。ただ、週間では１３ｂｐ近く低下しており、こちらも３週連続の低下に向かっている。    経済指標が物価上昇圧力の強まりを示す一方、市場では米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が来週の米連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）で利上げするとの見方が後退している。ＣＭＥのフェドウオッチによると、少なくとも２５ｂｐの利上げが行われる確率は９．４％と、１週間前の１５．５％、１カ月前の７０．９％から低下した。    経済見通しを示す指標として注目される２年債と１０年債の利回り格差は２９．６ｂｐだった。    ＦＲＢの金利見通しを反映しやすい２年債利回りは５．５ｂｐ上昇の４．６９％。週間では約５ｂｐ低下しており、２０２６年で最長となる４週連続の低下に向かっている。    物価連動国債（ＴＩＰＳ）と通常の国債の利回り差で、期待インフレを示すブレーク・イーブン・インフレ率（ＢＥＩ）は、５年物が２．４５６％、１０年物ＢＥＩは２．３４６％だった。 

米金融・債券市場：[US/BJ]

＜株式＞　主要株価３指数が軒並み下落して取引を終えた。一方、ハイテク株は持ち直し、市場をけん引してきた人工知能（ＡＩ）関連銘柄にとって波乱の１週間を締めくくった。市場の関心は、来週予定される企業決算や連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）に移っている。

ハイテク株の比率が高いナスダック総合は小幅な下げにとどまった。前日は、巨額のＡＩ投資を支える資金調達コストへの懸念が強まり、１日として６月以来の大幅下落となっていた。

Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種の大半のセクターが軟調で、一般消費財や金融はいずれも１％を大きく超える下げとなった。一方、エネルギーセクターは２．５％上昇し、過去最高値を付けた。サウジアラビアでのイエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派による攻撃を受け、中東からのエネルギー供給が一段と混乱するとの懸念が高まり、北海ブレント原油はこの日、４月下旬以来の高値を付けた。

この日は通信関連銘柄が下落し、通信サービスセクターの重しとなった。宇宙開発企業スペースＸが全米で少なくとも８万カ所の携帯電話基地局の利用を確保するため、通信インフラ企業と協議していると報じられたことが材料となった。

ＡＴ＆ＴとＴモバイルはともに約８％下落し、ベライゾンは１．２％安。一方、スペースＸは１．９％上昇した。

アメリカン・エキスプレスは３．７％下落し、ダウ工業株３０種の重しとなった。同社は、２０２６年通期の利益予想を市場予想を上回る水準に引き上げた。また、事業再編の一環として世界の従業員の５％に当たる約３５００人を削減する計画を発表した。 

来週は、アルファベット、マイクロソフト、アマゾン・ドット・コムのＡＩ「ハイパースケーラー」３社の四半期決算発表が予定されており、各社の設備投資見通しが市場の注目を集めそうだ。

ニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹＳＥ）では値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を１．７２対１の比率で上回った。

米取引所の合算出来高は１５４億株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７２億株。 

米国株式市場：[.NJP]

＜金先物＞　金は３カ月ぶりの安値となり、週足では４カ月超ぶりの大幅な下落となる見通し。エネルギー価格の上昇によるインフレ懸念が強まり、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の利上げ観測が強まったことが背景。金現物は東部夏時間午前１１時２０分（日本時間２４日午前０時２０分）時点で０．６％安の１オンス＝３９９８．３５ドルとなり、７月中旬以来初めて４０００ドルを下回った。米金先物１２月限の清算値は１．３％安の４００７．９０ドルだった。今週の下落率は４％に達し、６月以来最悪の週となる見通し。

ＮＹ貴金属：[GOL/XJ]

＜米原油先物＞　３ドル超上昇し、約半年ぶりの高値で取引を終えた。イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派によるサウジアラビア攻撃を受け、中東からのエネルギー供給が一段と混乱するとの懸念が強まった。アラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）当局も原油流出を報告した。    清算値は、北海ブレント先物が３．５５ドル（３．１４％）高の１バレル＝１１６．７２ドルと、４月２９日以来の高値。米ＷＴＩ先物は３．８０ドル（３．８％）高の１０３．２７ドルだった。    週間では北海ブレントが６％、ＷＴＩが２．３％上昇した。    ＵＡＥの気候変動・環境省は、ウンムアルカイワイン沖でタンカーからの原油流出が確認されたと発表した。流出の原因は明らかにしておらず、当局は該当するタンカーを特定していない。 

ＮＹＭＥＸエネルギー：[CR/USJ]

items.title: ヨルダン南部の教会で銃撃、7人死亡　当局「過激派テロ」との見方
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [アル・ムシャイルフェ（ヨルダン）　２３日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[アル・ムシャイルフェ（ヨルダン）　２３日　ロイター] - ヨルダン南部のカラク県にある教会で２３日、葬儀中に武装集団が発砲し、少なくとも７人が死亡、４０人が負傷した。ヨルダンの公安総局は、キリスト教徒少数派を狙った極めて異例の襲撃で、「過激派によるテロ行為」との見方を示している。武装グループは逃走中で、治安当局が行方を追っている。今のところ犯行声明を出した団体はない。

公安総局のアブドラ・マアイタ少将によると、銃撃事件が起きたのはカラク県のハムード教会。ファラヤ内相は、襲撃は「過激派」によるものとの見方を示した。ただ、ヨルダン国内外の組織との関係があるかについては、現段階で判断するのは尚早としている。

ヨルダンのアブドラ国王は事件発生から数時間後にカラク県を訪問。声明で「カラクでのテロ攻撃に最も厳しい報復で応じる。銃弾でヨルダン国民を分断できると思い込んでいる者に勝ち目はない。われわれは結束している」とし、犯行に及んだ者は「鉄拳で」処罰されるとした。

ハッサン首相は「テロリズムの思想と盲目的な過激主義の産物だ。われわれは社会がそのような道に進むことを許さない」とＸに投稿した。

国連のグテレス事務総長も今回の襲撃を非難。「民間人や礼拝施設を標的とした攻撃は容認できない」とＸに投稿した。

国営テレビ局アルマムラカが放映した映像で、３人の人物が歩道から教会に向けて発砲した後、樹木や低い塀の陰に身を隠し、その後、教会の入り口に向かって走る様子が確認できる。映像は教会の監視カメラで撮影されたものと見られ、ロイターは教会へ続く通路や周囲の塀などの特徴からこの映像の撮影場所を特定した。襲撃後に教会で撮影されたロイターの映像では、教会の入口付近の床に血痕が残されている様子が確認できる。

キリスト教徒はヨルダンで少数派。ただ、ヨルダンには聖書ゆかりの地が複数あり、世界各地からキリスト教の巡礼者が訪れている。米国のウォルツ国連大使はＸへの投稿で、今回の事件について「礼拝施設に対する卑劣で残忍な攻撃だ」と非難した。

Bo Erickson　Kanishka Singh

[フロリダ州フォートマイヤーズ ２３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Bo Erickson　Kanishka Singh

[フロリダ州フォートマイヤーズ ２３日 ロイター] - トランプ米大統領は２３日、フロリダ州の集会で、イランへの対応を終えた後にキューバ問題に対処し、合意をまとめるためルビオ国務長官を派遣すると述べた。

トランプ氏は９月、米国とキューバは合意に達するとの見通しを示し、軍事行動は必要ないと考えていると述べていた。

米国が実施した石油封鎖は、キューバに深刻な打撃を与えている。同国は燃料不足や停電に直面しており、インフラの機能不全が状況を悪化させている。

米国は６０年以上にわたってキューバへの禁輸措置を維持している。

items.title: Wall Street mostly loses ground under pressure from rising oil prices
items.author: The Associated Press
items.summary: Futures are lower as oil prices reach levels not seen since May amid halting efforts to bring the U.S. and Iran back to the negotiation table.
items.body: NEW YORK — Stocks on Wall Street closed broadly lower Friday as oil prices climbed to their highest level in more than four years, ratcheting up pressure on the market. The S&P 500 fell 0.5 per cent, adding to its decline from a day before. The index posted its second-straight weekly loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.2 per cent, and the Nasdaq composite slipped 0.2 per cent after giving up a modest gain. Rising oil prices weighed heavily on the market, where nearly three out of every four stocks within the benchmark S&P 500 index fell. The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil rose 3.1 per cent to settle at US$116.72. It has surged from less than US$97 at the start of October and is now at its highest level since June 2022. Several AI-related companies rallied, helping ease some of the impact from the broader market slide. Micron Technology rose 2.5 per cent, Intel gained 1.7 per cent, Microsoft added 0.7 per cent, and Advanced Micro Devices closed 1.7 per cent higher. The tech sector’s influence is also capable of quickly switching over to a heavy weight. Stocks that have benefited from the frenzy over AI have been swinging over rising worries about their path ahead. Investors are worried about whether their high prices are justified. Many of those companies have been borrowing to fund investments in AI technology and high interest rates are making those loans more expensive. “Investors appear increasingly focused on the economics of AI, particularly the substantial upfront costs required to build AI infrastructure and the uncertainty around the timing of returns on those investments,” said Angelo Kourkafas, senior global strategist at Edward Jones, in a research note. The latest round of corporate earnings are being closely watched to help get a better sense of whether those investments are paying off, or might pay off. Several influential AI-related companies report their latest financial results next week, including Google’s parent, Alphabet, along with Microsoft and Amazon. Industrial companies had some of the biggest losses. Caterpillar fell 2.4 per cent. American Express slumped 3.7 per cent, one of several financial stocks that lost ground, despite r eporting profits for its most recent quarter that beat analysts’ forecasts. The company did announce its first major job cuts in roughly a decade. JPMorgan Chase fell 1.5 per cent, Citigroup dropped 1.5 per cent and Capital One Financial slid 1 per cent. While higher oil prices weighed down much of the market, they helped boost energy companies. Chevron rose 2.9 per cent and ConocoPhillips gained 3.6 per cent. European markets closed mostly lower. France’s main index fell 0.4 per cent, though yields on French government bonds eased a bit. Treasury yields in the U.S. edged higher following sharp drops on Thursday. The yield on the 10-year Treasury edged up to 4.99 per cent from 4.96 per cent late Thursday. Yields have been rising globally, partly over worries about governments taking on too much debt. Inflation also remains a concern and is stubbornly well above 3 per cent in the U.S. That prompted the Federal Reserve to raise its benchmark interest rate at its last meeting in an effort to cool inflation. Wall Street expects the central bank to hold rates steady at its meeting next week, but is leaning heavily toward another rate hike in December. Wall Street will also get several big economic updates next week, including the Fed’s preferred measure of inflation. The personal consumption expenditures index, or PCE, is expected to show that inflation rose at a 3.7 per cent rate in September, sharply above the Fed’s 2 per cent target. The U.S. war with Iran has severely cut the world’s oil supply, driving energy prices higher and fueling a sharp jump in the cost of everything from gasoline to food and clothes. All told, the S&P 500 fell 39.75 points to 7,623.68. The Dow dropped 652.82 points to 52,215.16, and the Nasdaq gave up 53.52 points to close at 25,955.34. --- Damian J. Troise and Alex Veiga, The Associated Press

items.title: SoftBank-backed OPay eyes up to $4.4 billion US IPO valuation
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: OPay is targeting a valuation of up to $4.42 billion in its US initial public offering, the digital payments company said on Friday, seeking to capitalize on growing demand for digital financial services in emerging markets.
items.body:
OPay is targeting a valuation of up to $4.42 billion in its US initial public offering, the digital payments company said on Friday, seeking to capitalize on growing demand for digital financial services in emerging markets.
The Nigeria-focused firm is seeking up to $366 million by offering roughly 16 million American Depositary Shares between $19 and $21 apiece.
The offering comes as the United States IPO market faces renewed pressure from higher inflation and a selloff in AI-related stocks, weighing on investor appetite for new listings and prompting several companies to delay their listing plans.
Founded in 2018, OPay provides digital financial services, including payments, money transfers, savings and loans, and also operates in Indonesia, Egypt and Pakistan.
Nigeria, the world's sixth-most-populous country, has emerged as one of Africa's leading fintech markets, producing several fintech companies including Moniepoint, Flutterwave and Interswitch, according to Tracxn.
OPay was founded by Chinese billionaire Yahui Zhou, who also founded Beijing Kunlun Tech, a Chinese gaming company that previously owned dating app Grindr.
The company raised $400 million in 2021 at a valuation of $2 billion. It had about 50 million monthly active users as of July 31, according to its IPO prospectus.
SoftBank entities own a 6.6% stake in OPay before the offering, according to the filing.
Investors including Redwheel Group, Coronation Africa Frontiers Fund and other existing backers have indicated non-binding interest in buying up to $270 million worth of ADS. Stanbic Africa Holdings has separately agreed to invest as much as $200 million through a concurrent private placement.
OPay plans to use the proceeds from its IPO and concurrent private placement to invest in technology, expand its distribution network and markets, develop new products and pursue potential acquisitions and strategic investments.
Citigroup, Deutsche Bank, Standard Bank and CICC are among the offering's underwriters.
OPay will list on the NYSE under the "OPAY" symbol.

items.title: 米国株式市場＝主要3指数軒並み下落、ハイテク株は持ち直し
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Lewis Krauskopf　Tharuniyaa Lakshmi　Ragini Mathur

[２３日 ロイター] -
items.body:
Lewis Krauskopf　Tharuniyaa Lakshmi　Ragini Mathur

[２３日 ロイター] - 米国株式市場は主要株価３指数が軒並み下落して取引を終えた。一方、ハイテク株は持ち直し、市場をけん引してきた人工知能（ＡＩ）関連銘柄にとって波乱の１週間を締めくくった。市場の関心は、来週予定される企業決算や連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）に移っている。

ハイテク株の比率が高いナスダック総合は小幅な下げにとどまった。前日は、巨額のＡＩ投資を支える資金調達コストへの懸念が強まり、１日として６月以来の大幅下落となっていた。

Ｓ＆Ｐ総合５００種の大半のセクターが軟調で、一般消費財や金融はいずれも１％を大きく超える下げとなった。一方、エネルギーセクターは２．５％上昇し、過去最高値を付けた。サウジアラビアでのイエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派による攻撃を受け、中東からのエネルギー供給が一段と混乱するとの懸念が高まり、北海ブレント原油はこの日、４月下旬以来の高値を付けた。

この日は通信関連銘柄が下落し、通信サービスセクターの重しとなった。宇宙開発企業スペースＸが全米で少なくとも８万カ所の携帯電話基地局の利用を確保するため、通信インフラ企業と協議していると報じられたことが材料となった。

ＡＴ＆ＴとＴモバイルはともに約８％下落し、ベライゾンは１．２％安。一方、スペースＸは１．９％上昇した。

アメリカン・エキスプレスは３．７％下落し、ダウ工業株３０種の重しとなった。同社は、２０２６年通期の利益予想を市場予想を上回る水準に引き上げた。また、事業再編の一環として世界の従業員の５％に当たる約３５００人を削減する計画を発表した。 

来週は、アルファベット、マイクロソフト、アマゾン・ドット・コムのＡＩ「ハイパースケーラー」３社の四半期決算発表が予定されており、各社の設備投資見通しが市場の注目を集めそうだ。

マン・グループのチーフ・マーケット・ストラテジスト、クリスティナ・フーパー氏は「ＡＩ関連銘柄を疑問視する動きの余波は依然として残っている」と指摘。「来年、ＡＩデータセンター拡張への投資がこれまでの予想よりも少なくなる可能性は確かにある。だからこそ、市場に様子見姿勢が広がっているのだと思う」と述べた。

ニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹＳＥ）では値下がり銘柄数が値上がり銘柄数を１．７２対１の比率で上回った。

米取引所の合算出来高は１５４億株。直近２０営業日の平均は１７２億株。

items.title: Marco Rubio calls on those seeking change in Cuba to partner with CIA
items.author: Bo Erickson, Kanishka Singh
items.creator: Bo Erickson, Kanishka Singh
items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on those seeking change in Cuba to partner with the CIA as President Donald Trump said Washington would "take care of Cuba" after dealing with Iran and send in the top US diplomat to finish the deal.
items.body:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio called on those seeking change in Cuba to partner with the CIA as President Donald Trump said Washington would "take care of Cuba" after dealing with Iran and send in the top US diplomat to finish the deal.
DETAILS AND QUOTES: "We'll take care of Cuba on our way back from Iran ... then we're going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal," Trump told a rally in Florida.
"To those who seek to create positive change in Cuba - now is the time," Rubio, who has been handling much of the Cuba-related policy for Trump, said on X on Friday.
Rubio urged those disappointed by Cuba's government to "seize this opportunity to create the change you desire through a discrete partnership with the CIA," without elaborating further.
The Trump administration [USN:L1N45L02I TEXT:"has previously stated"] its goal is to change Cuba's communist government.
A US-imposed oil blockade implemented earlier this year has put Cuba under severe strain as it contends with fuel shortages and [USN:L1N44002K TEXT:"blackouts"] exacerbated by failing infrastructure.
Washington has maintained an embargo on Cuba for over 60 years.
The Trump administration has been [USN:L1N4590T5 TEXT:"stepping up pressure"] on Havana after the US military in January seized then-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro in a deadly raid.
Cuba's foreign minister told the UN General Assembly last month Cuba would always be open for dialogue with Washington.
UN rights experts have condemned the oil blockade as a violation of international law while rights advocates say the Trump administration's threats have echoed an [USN:L4N3YE036 TEXT:"imperialist approach"].
Trump [USN:L1N45I044 TEXT:"predicted last month"] the US and Cuba would reach an agreement and that he did not think military action would be necessary.

items.title: 原油先物3ドル超上昇、半年ぶり高値　フーシ派攻撃で供給懸念
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Nicole Jao

［ニューヨーク　２３日　ロイター］ -
items.body:
Nicole Jao

［ニューヨーク　２３日　ロイター］ - 米国時間の原油先物は３ドル超上昇し、約半年ぶりの高値で取引を終えた。イエメンの親イラン武装組織フーシ派によるサウジアラビア攻撃を受け、中東からのエネルギー供給が一段と混乱するとの懸念が強まった。アラブ首長国連邦（ＵＡＥ）当局も原油流出を報告した。

清算値は、北海ブレント先物が３．５５ドル（３．１４％）高の１バレル＝１１６．７２ドルと、４月２９日以来の高値。米ＷＴＩ先物は３．８０ドル（３．８％）高の１０３．２７ドルだった。

週間では北海ブレントが６％、ＷＴＩが２．３％上昇した。

ＬＰＬファイナンシャルのチーフクロスアセットストラテジスト、アダム・ターンクイスト氏は「フーシ派が、エネルギーインフラを含むサウジ各地で一連の攻撃を実施し、供給混乱への懸念が相場を押し上げた」と述べた。

ＵＡＥの気候変動・環境省は、ウンムアルカイワイン沖でタンカーからの原油流出が確認されたと発表した。流出の原因は明らかにしておらず、当局は該当するタンカーを特定していない。

items.title: OpenAI resumes frontier AI training after security overhaul, discloses flaw in widely used software
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: OpenAI said on Friday it had resumed training of its most advanced AI models after tightening security and barring internet access, and disclosed a flaw in a widely used software that it found while testing its defenses.
items.body:
OpenAI said on Friday it had resumed training of its most advanced AI models after tightening security and barring internet access, and disclosed a flaw in a widely used software that it found while testing its defenses.
The disclosure comes amid concerns over the ability of increasingly capable AI agents to identify and exploit software flaws, including in the guardrails meant to contain them.
OpenAI had paused training of its most capable models after one of its research models used a configuration error to gain limited internet access in September. The company said it contained the incident and used the pause to strengthen its defenses.
To test them, OpenAI had teams of AI agents try to break out of their restricted environments. It said the agents found previously unknown flaws, which it had fixed, and training resumed on October 1.
During that exercise, the ChatGPT maker found a flaw in Brotli, a widely used data compression tool.
The company said attackers could exploit the flaw by sending malicious data that lets them run their own code on affected systems, including those using popular web software such as [USN:L6N4680ZQ TEXT:"Node.js"], Bun and Envoy.
OpenAI said the root cause was fixed in Brotli's source code in February, before it was known to create a security vulnerability, but no new version was released at the time. Brotli has since released updated versions and published a public record of the flaw after OpenAI disclosed it.

Oct 23 : OpenAI said on Friday it had resumed training of its most advanced AI models after tightening security and barring internet access, and disclosed a flaw in a widely used software that it found while testing its defenses.
The disclosure comes amid concerns over the ability of increasingly capable AI agents to identify and exploit software flaws, including in the guardrails meant to contain them.
OpenAI had paused training of its most capable models after one of its research models used a configuration error to gain limited internet access in September. The company said it contained the incident and used the pause to strengthen its defenses.
To test them, OpenAI had teams of AI agents try to break out of their restricted environments. It said the agents found previously unknown flaws, which it had fixed, and training resumed on October 1.

During that exercise, the ChatGPT maker found a flaw in Brotli, a widely used data compression tool.
The company said attackers could exploit the flaw by sending malicious data that lets them run their own code on affected systems, including those using popular web software such as Node.js, Bun and Envoy.
OpenAI said the root cause was fixed in Brotli's source code in February, before it was known to create a security vulnerability, but no new version was released at the time. Brotli has since released updated versions and published a public record of the flaw after OpenAI disclosed it.
Separately on Thursday, AI safety evaluators METR and Redwood Research said they found several new vulnerabilities in OpenAI's internal system, including an exploit agents could have used to keep hundreds of their actions from being monitored, in a pilot review earlier this year.
OpenAI told the safety organizations it has since patched all vulnerabilities affecting its production safeguards, although METR and Redwood said they had not verified the fixes.
OpenAI has been conducting a broad review of its AI models' activity since the Hugging Face incident in July, and has informed more than 100 organizations about incidents of unauthorized activity tied to its AI agents.

items.title: Trump says US may do another military operation against Iran
items.author: Bo Erickson, Kanishka Singh
items.creator: Bo Erickson, Kanishka Singh
items.summary: President Donald Trump said on Friday the US may carry out another military operation against Iran just as the Iran war nears its eight-month mark and rising fuel prices weigh on the US midterm elections.
items.body:
President Donald Trump said on Friday the US may carry out another military operation against Iran just as the Iran war nears its eight-month mark and rising fuel prices weigh on the US midterm elections.
"We may do another little Epic Fury," Trump told a rally in Florida, using the US military's term for its war on Iran. He did not elaborate.
Trump said earlier in the day the US could end the war quickly but questioned whether Washington should seek a swift conclusion or allow the conflict to gradually wind down.
Trump, who has offered [USN:L4N4061X8 TEXT:"shifting goals and timelines"] for the war, has said in recent campaign remarks that the war will end soon, "one way or the other."
He said this month the US would not launch an attack on Iran before the November 3 elections that will determine control of Congress, where Trump's Republican Party holds a narrow majority in both chambers.
The US and Israel attacked Iran on February 28, and Iran responded with its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon have [USN:L1N3ZZ07R TEXT:"killed thousands"] and [USN:L6N3ZY0Q0 TEXT:"displaced millions."]
The war has raised oil and gas prices around the world.
Tehran [USN:L6N46816Q TEXT:"plans a wider retaliation"] if the war resumes, Iranian officials said.
Iran has drawn up detailed plans to target undersea communications cables in the Gulf if the US and Israel attack Iran again, according to two senior Iranian security officials.
(This story has been refiled to remove extraneous word 'at' in paragraph 1.)

items.title: 仏、24日の抗議活動に警官７万人動員　先週末の暴動再発警戒
items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary:
Makini Brice　Crispian Balmer

[パリ　２３日　ロイター] -
items.body:
Makini Brice　Crispian Balmer

[パリ　２３日　ロイター] - フランスで生活費の高騰などに抗議するデモが大規模な暴動に発展してから１週間が経過する中、ニュネス内相は２３日、暴力行為や略奪の再発を防ぐため、２４日に全国で予定されている抗議活動に対応するため７万人の警察官を動員すると発表した。政府が治安維持能力を失ったとの懸念を払拭するため、精鋭治安部隊や重武装の機動隊を通常の警察部隊とともに配備し、厳戒態勢で臨む。

ニュネス氏は記者団に対し「暴徒や略奪者、あらゆる暴力行為を行う者に対し一切妥協しない」と述べた。「極左」団体がインターネット上で公共施設を標的にし、一段の無秩序状態を引き起こすよう呼びかけていると言及し「これは平穏で友好的なデモではない。最大限の警戒態勢を敷き、断固として対応する。一切の違法行為を容認しない」と語った。

警察当局は２４日に首都パリで予定されるデモについて、労働組合による１件のみを許可。フランス最大の学生組合ＵＮＥＦや、２０１８年に発足した反体制運動「黄色いベスト運動」が申請した集会は許可されなかった。パリ以外の多くの都市でも抗議活動が禁止されたが、第２の都市マルセイユでは禁止命令が撤回され、労組によるデモの実施が認められた。

当局は特に、中部オルレアンで週末に開かれる極右政党「国民連合（ＲＮ）」の年次党大会が新たな緊張の火種となる可能性を警戒。ニュネス氏によると、今週末に動員される警察官は前週末より１万人増員される。騎馬警官やヘリコプター、ドローン、対ドローン装備を全国に配備するほか、装甲車や放水車も待機。一部の要警戒地域で導入された夜間外出禁止令は継続されるという。

＜ルーブル美術館など休館、サッカー試合も延期＞

前週末の暴動再発への懸念から、パリの主要文化施設の一部は２４日、終日休館を決めた。対象にはルーブル美術館、オルセー美術館、オペラ座が含まれる。このほか、治安上の懸念から、サッカーフランス１部リーグのパリ・サンジェルマン（ＰＳＧ）対オリンピック・リヨン戦は開催日が２５日から２６日に変更された。一方、米ナショナル・フットボール・リーグ（ＮＦＬ）のピッツバーグ・スティーラーズ対ニューオーリンズ・セインツ戦は、トランプ米大統領が中止を求めたにもかかわらず、２５日にパリで予定通り開催されると見られている。

前週末の暴動で約３０００の店舗や事業所が略奪被害を受けていたため、経済団体も小売店に対し休業を呼びかけている。フランス商工会議所のアラン・ディ・クレセンゾ会頭は、一部の商店主は店舗を守るため野球バットや散弾銃などを準備しているとし、自警のために暴力に訴えないよう呼びかけた。

社会不安の拡大を受け、仏経済の先行き懸念が増大。政府が財政支出の抑制に十分取り組んでいないとの懸念が改めて意識される中、格付け会社ムーディーズが２３日にフランス国債格付けを引き下げるとの観測が市場で広がっている。

TORONTO: US President Donald Trump said on Friday (Oct 23) that Canada is working hard to make a trade deal with the United States.
" Canada is working very hard to make a deal with us , and I hate to say this, but we have all the cards," Trump told reporters at the White Ho us e.
A spokesperson for Dominic LeBlanc, Canada 's minister responsible for trade with the US , declined to comment.
The US and Canada have been locked in a trade standoff since talks broke down in Aug us t, triggering new tariffs and retaliation on both sides of the border.
The breakdown has widened a rift between the longtime allies, who have blamed each other for the failed talks. The dispute has spurred Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to urge a further shift away from Canada 's biggest trading partner and cast doubt on the viability of the US -Mexico- Canada Agreement.

NEW YORK, Oct 23 : Big AI stocks were mixed on Friday, a day after the biggest decline in the Nasdaq Composite Index in four months, giving investors a welcome respite as they look forward to more information on Anthropic's forthcoming IPO and a further wave of earnings over the next week.
Meta Platforms, the center of Thursday's storm, was fractionally lower following Thursday's 7 per cent decline. The operator of social media networks and major AI investor said in its earnings report this week that it would create a new class of shares in part to raise money for further capital spending, which was taken as evidence that the next leg of the AI buildout will be costly for shareholders.
Other major AI players were mixed on Friday, with SpaceX, Oracle and Dell Technologies up 1 per cent to 2 per cent and Nvidia, Alphabet and Amazon down less than 1 per cent. Big semiconductor stocks were mostly higher after their largest decline since the summer on Thursday.
Credit default swaps tracking the perceived risk of default at the biggest AI players were mostly modestly lower, with Meta's five-year CDS spread trading 0.3 per cent narrower at 123, according to LSEG data. The swaps enable investors to bet on a default using contracts typically with terms of five or 10 years, though contracts frequently change hands for the purposes of hedging positions and betting on near-term market moves.

Thursday's deluge and the day-after calm is the latest sign of indirection in a market that has hovered near record highs without breaking out, said Rick Meckler, partner at Cherry Lane Investments, a family investment office in New Vernon, New Jersey.
"To some extent, we're seeing the market tread water over a longer period of time because every sell-off has been met by buyers and every point upward has been met by sellers," Meckler said.
The Nasdaq was barely changed on Friday afternoon.
Credit-default swap premiums, reflecting the annual cost borne by the swap purchaser in thousands of dollars, have risen over the past year with concern about the risks being taken on by large AI spenders. The premiums rose on Thursday after Meta's decision to sell more stock, as much of the buildout to date has been financed through debt issuance.
The concerns around AI spending and investment returns have added to the market's volatility since Treasury yields rose sharply in August, which changed the economics of investing and bond issuance, given the increasing attractiveness of a higher risk-free rate.
It's been "a very volatile week," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B Riley Wealth in Boston. "There's no doubt at some point in time that the higher inflation moves, especially if driven by unsustainably higher energy prices ... would have to show up in corporate earnings. It hasn't yet, but that's the concern. And market participants are trying to position for that."
Shares of neoclouds, smaller companies tied to AI data centers and other infrastructure projects like CoreWeave, have dropped due to anxiety over their future. Their performance of late has also raised talk on Wall Street that capital is growing scarce - which stands to raise costs further and potentially raise funding issues down the road.
Even so, many investors remain positive on the sector, where giant AI lab Anthropic is expected to publish its IPO prospectus in coming days and Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft are expected to report earnings next week.
"In general, AI news in terms of revenues continues to be very strong, it's just at what cost and how long that growth is sustainable," Meckler said. "We really haven't gotten to the point of the market sort of focusing on winners and losers. It's been one big sector trade every day."
